findings.description: No rate limiting is enforced at any layer. Searched: package.json (no @fastify/rate-limit or equivalent dependency), src/routes.ts and src/auth.ts (no throttling middleware - registerRoutes installs only the requireRole preHandler), and infra/ecs.yaml (ALB-fronted ECS service with no WAF, no API Gateway and therefore no usage plan or throttle settings). SAFETY.md confirms the gap: 'No rate limiting; an automated caller can fan out unchecked.'
findings.gap: An agent retry loop can call the mutating endpoints at machine speed without any throttle, saturating the two-task Fargate service and the RDS connection pool, and fanning out unbounded calls to the payment and warehouse dependencies.
findings.recommendation: Register @fastify/rate-limit with per-principal (JWT sub/client_id) limits, applying a much tighter limit to the refund/cancel/delete routes than to reads, and return 429 with a Retry-After header. Add an AWS WAF rate-based rule on the ALB as a second, pre-application layer.

findings.title: Blast Radius and Transaction Limits
findings.description: There are no business-domain limits on the scope of an operation. src/routes.ts passes the client-supplied `amount` straight into OrderService.refund() with no cap, no per-principal refund budget and no daily/hourly ceiling; there is no maximum number of deletes or cancellations per caller or per session, and no bulk-operation size cap anywhere. infra/ecs.yaml contains no configuration surface for such limits. SAFETY.md lists 'cap auto-refund amount; require human approval above a threshold' as intended but unimplemented.
findings.gap: The blast radius of an agent error is unbounded: a looping agent could refund an arbitrary total value or hard-delete every order it can enumerate, and nothing in the system would stop it before the damage was done. The only protection contemplated is request-rate throttling (also absent - STATE-Q5), which does not cap business impact.
findings.recommendation: Add per-principal business limits as configuration: max refund amount per call, max cumulative refund value per hour, max cancellations and max deletes per session. Enforce them in the service before the downstream call and reject with a structured `limit_exceeded` error so the agent can surface it for human escalation.

findings.title: Draft/Pending State
findings.description: There is no proposable, uncommitted state. The Order status enum in src/services/order-service.ts is `'placed' | 'shipped' | 'cancelled' | 'refunded'` - every value is a committed terminal or in-flight business state, with no PENDING/DRAFT/PROPOSED member. create() inserts directly with status 'placed'; refund() and cancelAndRecallShipment() commit the status change and fire the irreversible downstream effect in the same call; hardDelete() removes the row outright. No two-step create-then-confirm route exists in src/routes.ts.
findings.gap: An agent cannot propose a refund, cancellation or deletion for review - every write it makes is immediately committed and, for the three irreversible operations, cannot be undone. There is no reviewable intermediate state to repurpose for agent-initiated proposals.
findings.recommendation: Add `refund_pending`, `cancel_pending` and `delete_pending` states (or a separate `order_actions` proposal table) that an agent can write, plus explicit confirm/reject endpoints that perform the real side effect. Keep the downstream warehouse/payment call behind the confirm step.

findings.title: Configurable Approval Gates
findings.description: No approval gate exists for any operation. src/routes.ts exposes no approval or confirmation endpoint, the irreversible routes take no `confirm` parameter and no approval token (openapi/orders.yaml: DELETE is 'IRREVERSIBLE hard delete ... No confirmation'), and there is no per-operation configuration flag that could require review. No Step Functions task-token workflow or equivalent exists in infra/ecs.yaml.
findings.gap: High-risk operations - a real refund, a physical dispatch recall and a hard delete of customer PII - execute autonomously on a single API call with no application-layer human checkpoint and no configurable threshold above which review is required.
findings.recommendation: Add an approval gate that is configurable per operation and per threshold: require an approval token (issued by a separate human-approval endpoint) on refund above a configured amount, and on cancel and delete unconditionally. Validate the token's binding to the specific order id and operation before executing the side effect.

findings.title: Data Residency and Sovereignty
findings.description: The service stores customer order data in PostgreSQL on RDS (README.md) and README.md/SAFETY.md state the order row holds customer PII, but no data residency or sovereignty posture is defined anywhere in the repository. Searched: all IaC (infra/ecs.yaml - no region constraint beyond the implicit !Ref AWS::Region, no cross-region replication, no RDS resource at all), all docs (README.md, SAFETY.md - no GDPR/LGPD/HIPAA or jurisdiction reference), the OpenAPI spec, and package.json. No residency classification, no allowed-region allowlist, and no egress restriction on where order data may be transmitted.
findings.gap: The jurisdiction and residency class of the stored customer PII is undocumented, so there is no basis on which to decide whether an agent may transmit order/customer data to an LLM endpoint in another region. No technical control pins data or model-inference egress to an approved region.
findings.recommendation: Document the residency class and governing jurisdiction of the orders dataset, then enforce it: pin the RDS instance and any replica to approved regions in infra/ecs.yaml, restrict outbound inference egress to in-region endpoints (VPC endpoint policy for the model provider), and record the approved-region list as configuration the agent layer can read.

findings.title: PII Redaction in Logs
findings.description: No log redaction exists and the claimed logging stack is not actually present. README.md states 'structured JSON logs (pino) with a request id', but package.json declares no pino dependency and no logging configuration or redaction allowlist appears in any source file - src/auth.ts, src/routes.ts and src/services/order-service.ts contain no logger wiring at all. Fastify's default logger, if enabled, serializes request metadata without redaction, and OrderService returns full `SELECT *` rows (src/services/order-service.ts) that would be logged verbatim by any error handler that prints the response or the thrown query error. infra/ecs.yaml ships container stdout to the CloudWatch log group /ecs/orders with no metric/subscription filter and no retention policy, and no Macie or scrubbing integration.
findings.gap: Order rows containing customer PII can reach CloudWatch unredacted via request/response or error logging, and the log group has no retention limit, so any leakage is retained indefinitely. There is no configured redaction path at all.
findings.recommendation: Add the logger explicitly with a redaction configuration (pino `redact` paths covering authorization headers, request bodies and customer fields), log identifiers rather than entity payloads, and replace `SELECT *` with explicit column projections so PII never enters a serializable response object by default. Set a retention policy on /ecs/orders and add a CloudWatch Logs data-protection policy for PII patterns.

findings.title: Immutable Audit Logging
findings.description: create_charge logs the authenticated principal (client_id) at src/payments/handlers.py:44, but refund_charge logs only correlation_id, charge_id and reason (handlers.py:70-71) — the principal is absent from the refund write record. infra/template.yaml declares no AWS::CloudTrail::Trail, no CloudWatch Logs retention policy, and no S3 Object Lock for log storage, so no log sink is immutable or tamper-evident.
findings.gap: Principal attribution is missing on the refund write path, and no immutable/tamper-evident audit sink is defined in IaC. For a payments ledger driven by write-enabled agents this breaks forensic attribution and regulated-domain audit requirements.
findings.recommendation: Add client_id (and scope list) to the refund_charge log record, then define the audit sink in infra/template.yaml: an AWS::CloudTrail::Trail with LogFileValidationEnabled, an explicit LogGroup RetentionInDays per function, and an S3 log bucket with ObjectLockEnabled for long-term retention.

findings.title: Agent Identity Suspension
findings.description: Authentication is OAuth2 client-credentials validated against Cognito (src/payments/authorizer.py:1-26, infra/template.yaml:138-141), so per-client revocation is technically possible by disabling the Cognito app client. However no revocation surface or procedure exists in the repository: no app-client resources are declared in infra/template.yaml (only a UserPoolId parameter), and RUNBOOK.md documents dashboards, alarms, deploy/rollback and escalation but no 'suspend a client' step.
findings.gap: No declared per-client identity resource and no documented suspension runbook step, so isolating one misbehaving machine client cannot be done predictably or quickly.
findings.recommendation: Declare one Cognito app client per calling service in infra/template.yaml so identities are reviewable in code, and add a 'Suspend a client' section to RUNBOOK.md with the exact disable command and verification step.

findings.title: Concurrency Controls
findings.description: _idempotent_put in src/payments/app.py:47-73 performs a get_item on the idempotency record and then an unconditional put_item. There is no ConditionExpression (attribute_not_exists) on the write and no version attribute or ETag/If-Match on any entity; the DynamoDB table (infra/template.yaml:22-34) carries no version attribute.
findings.gap: Read-then-write with no conditional write leaves a race window: two concurrent agent retries carrying the same Idempotency-Key can both pass the get_item check and both write ledger rows, which is exactly the duplicate-charge case idempotency is meant to prevent.
findings.recommendation: Make the idempotency record write conditional — put_item with ConditionExpression='attribute_not_exists(pk)' and treat ConditionalCheckFailedException as the existing-key path — and write the idempotency marker before the ledger row, or use the aws_lambda_powertools idempotency utility already available via the dependency in pyproject.toml.

findings.title: Rate Limiting and Throttling
findings.description: The AWS::Serverless::Api in infra/template.yaml:36-56 sets StageName, TracingEnabled, Auth and Domain but no throttling: no usage plan, no MethodSettings ThrottlingRateLimit/ThrottlingBurstLimit, no WAF association, and no application-level rate limiting in src/payments/. openapi/payments.yaml documents no limits. DynamoDB is PAY_PER_REQUEST, so there is no capacity ceiling either.
findings.gap: Nothing bounds request rate. A runaway agent retry loop can drive unbounded charge/refund attempts and unbounded on-demand DynamoDB spend at machine speed.
findings.recommendation: Add MethodSettings with ThrottlingRateLimit and ThrottlingBurstLimit on the PaymentsApi stage, and an AWS::ApiGateway::UsagePlan bound per client so limits are per calling identity rather than global.

findings.title: Blast Radius and Transaction Limits
findings.description: No business-domain caps exist anywhere in the repository. openapi/payments.yaml bounds a single amount only by 'minimum: 1' (no maximum) on ChargeRequest and RefundRequest; src/payments/handlers.py applies no per-client ceiling on refund value or count; infra/template.yaml exposes only LEDGER_TABLE and IDEMPOTENCY_TTL_SECONDS as tunables. There are no bulk endpoints, which bounds per-call scope, but nothing bounds cumulative spend per client or per session.
findings.gap: A correct-but-catastrophic agent loop — refunding every charge it reads — is not stopped by any business limit. Throttling alone (once added, STATE-Q5) limits request rate, not refunded value.
findings.recommendation: Introduce per-client configurable limits enforced in the refund path — max refund amount per request, max refunds and max refunded value per hour per client_id — backed by a counter item in the ledger table, and return a structured 429/422 error code when a limit is hit.

findings.title: Draft/Pending State
findings.description: The Charge and Refund schemas in openapi/payments.yaml include status enum [pending, succeeded, failed], so a reviewable intermediate state exists in the contract. The implementation never uses it: create_charge writes status='succeeded' (src/payments/handlers.py:48-50) and refund_charge writes status='succeeded' (handlers.py:75-78). No confirm, approve or commit operation exists in openapi/payments.yaml — the three paths are createCharge, getCharge, refundCharge.
findings.gap: Every agent-initiated write commits immediately. The 'pending' enum value cannot be used as a proposal state because no transition endpoint exists to move pending to succeeded.
findings.recommendation: Add a two-step path for agent-initiated refunds: have refundCharge accept a 'pending' flag (or add POST /charges/{chargeId}/refunds with status=pending) and introduce an explicit POST /refunds/{refundId}/confirm operation requiring a distinct scope such as payments:approve.

findings.title: Configurable Approval Gates
findings.description: No approval mechanism exists at the application layer. openapi/payments.yaml defines no approval operation and no per-operation gating flag; infra/template.yaml contains no Step Functions state machine and no waitForTaskToken task; the only per-operation control is scope enforcement via _require_scope (src/payments/app.py:42-44), which is binary authorization rather than a configurable human gate.
findings.gap: High-risk operations (large refunds in particular) cannot be configured to require human approval before execution, so there is no defense-in-depth below the orchestration layer.
findings.recommendation: Make approval a per-operation configuration: add an environment-driven threshold (for example REFUND_APPROVAL_THRESHOLD) that causes refund_charge to persist the refund as pending and return 202 with the pending id instead of executing, pairing with the HITL-Q1 confirm endpoint.

findings.title: Queryable Current State
findings.description: No queryable state interface exists. `frmCustomer.frm` contains exactly one data operation — an `INSERT` in `cmdSave_Click` (lines 24-34). There is no SELECT, no read-before-write, no status field, and no GET-equivalent surface; the form's only control bound to data is the `txtName` text box. State can only be inspected by opening the .mdb file directly.
findings.gap: A caller cannot inspect existing customer state before acting, so it cannot tell whether a record already exists — which compounds the idempotency gap in API-Q4.
findings.recommendation: Expose read operations (get/list customer) alongside the write path so callers can verify current state before mutating it.

findings.title: Sandbox/Staging Environment
findings.description: No sandbox or staging environment exists. README.md states 'No tests, no build server; compiled on one developer's machine' and describes a single production data path — `S:\CRM\sales.mdb` on the shared drive — hardcoded as a constant with an explicit instruction not to change it: 'DO NOT change the .mdb path - field laptops are mapped to S:\' (frmCustomer.frm lines 5, 7). There are no environment-specific configurations, no seed data scripts, and no synthetic data generators in the repository.
findings.gap: Because the database path is a compile-time constant pointing at production, there is no way to exercise the write path against production-shaped data without touching live customer records.
findings.recommendation: Externalize the data source to configuration and stand up a staging copy of the database with representative data so caller behaviour can be validated before production.

findings.title: Input Validation and Schema Enforcement
findings.description: There is no input validation. `cmdSave_Click` concatenates `txtName.Text` and `Environ("USERNAME")` directly into an SQL string (frmCustomer.frm lines 25-27) — the code's own comment states 'String-concatenated SQL - no parameters (injection risk)'. There is no length check, no type or format validation, no escaping, no parameterized command (`ADODB.Command` with parameters is not used), and no request-size limit. Validation failures cannot be reported because `On Error Resume Next` (line 28) discards all errors and the only feedback is a generic `MsgBox` with no field identification (line 31).
findings.gap: Malformed or adversarial input is accepted and executed as SQL. A caller cannot self-correct because rejections are neither structured nor, in most cases, reported at all. This is an exploitable SQL injection path, reachable by anything that can set the Name value.
findings.recommendation: Replace string-concatenated SQL with parameterized `ADODB.Command` parameters, add explicit field validation (length, allowed characters) and return structured, field-level rejection messages instead of swallowing errors.

findings.title: Temporal Metadata and Freshness
findings.description: Temporal metadata is minimal and locally-scoped. The insert sets `CreatedOn` from VB6 `Now()` (frmCustomer.frm line 26), which returns the client laptop's local system time with no timezone normalization and no UTC storage — field laptops may differ in clock and timezone. There is no `updated_at`/`LastModified` column, no event-time field, and no freshness signal; README.md notes downstream reporting data is refreshed by a nightly batch, so consumers of the reporting copy can be up to 24 hours stale with no indicator.
findings.gap: Timestamps are unnormalized client local time and there is no update timestamp or staleness/consistency signal, so a caller cannot reliably reason about record age or whether data it reads is current.
findings.recommendation: Store timestamps in UTC from a single authoritative source, add a last-updated column, and expose a freshness indicator (e.g. last-sync time) on any read path offered to agents.

findings.title: Schema Versioning and API Contracts
findings.description: There are no versioned contracts of any kind. The `Customers` schema is implied only by the inline SQL statement in `cmdSave_Click` (frmCustomer.frm lines 25-27) and lives inside the binary .mdb file; there are no migration files, no JSON Schema/Avro/Protobuf definitions, no schema registry, no `/v1/` style versioning, no changelog, and no breaking-change detection (there is no CI pipeline at all — README.md: 'No tests, no build server'). A schema change in the Access file would silently break every compiled client.
findings.gap: Schema and contract changes are undetectable and unversioned, so any caller binding to this data — including an agent tool definition — breaks silently when the .mdb schema changes.
findings.recommendation: Extract the schema into version-controlled migration files, publish a versioned contract for the data shape, and add breaking-change detection to a build pipeline.

findings.title: Distributed Tracing and Structured Logging
findings.description: There is no tracing and no logging. `frmCustomer.frm` contains no logging statements, no correlation or request identifier, no OpenTelemetry/X-Ray instrumentation, and no structured output of any kind; the three error handlers are `On Error Resume Next` (lines 28, 37) and a `MsgBox` (line 31). A failed save produces no record anywhere — the error object is explicitly cleared (`Err.Clear`, line 32).
findings.gap: Failures are unobservable. There is no trace, log line, or correlation identifier with which to reconstruct what happened during any request, agent-initiated or human.
findings.recommendation: Add structured logging with a per-operation correlation ID and propagate it through the service layer from API-Q1; remove the error-swallowing handlers so failures are recorded.

findings.title: Alerting on Error Rates and Latency
findings.description: No alerting exists. There are no CloudWatch alarms, anomaly detectors, SLO definitions, or paging integrations in the repository (no IaC and no configuration files beyond `.gitignore`). Failure detection is manual and user-reported: the application's response to a write failure is a dialog asking the user to try again (frmCustomer.frm line 31). README.md confirms recurring failure modes — monthly .mdb corruption and common 'record locked' errors — that today are discovered by field users rather than by monitoring.
findings.gap: Error-rate and latency degradation is invisible to operators, so a failing integration surface would be detected only after users or an agent had already been failing for an extended period.
findings.recommendation: Instrument the service layer with error-rate and latency metrics and configure threshold alarms on the operations agents will consume.

findings.title: API Test Coverage
findings.description: There are no automated tests. The repository contains no test files, test directories, or test framework references, and README.md states outright 'No tests, no build server; compiled on one developer's machine'. The write path in `cmdSave_Click` (frmCustomer.frm lines 24-34) — including its SQL construction and its error handling — has no coverage of input handling, output format, error responses, or edge cases.
findings.gap: No test coverage at all on the only data-mutating code path, so behavioural changes (including regressions in SQL construction or error handling) would reach production undetected.
findings.recommendation: Extract the data-access logic from the form into a testable unit and establish automated tests covering input handling and failure paths as part of introducing the build pipeline (ENG-Q2).

findings.title: Encryption at Rest for Agent-Accessible Data
findings.description: Customer data at rest is protected only by a legacy Jet database password. `frmCustomer.frm` opens `S:\CRM\sales.mdb` with `Provider=Microsoft.Jet.OLEDB.4.0` and `Jet OLEDB:Database Password=crm2005pw` (lines 7-8, 19-21). Jet database passwords are access gating, not encryption — the Access 2003 .mdb format's obfuscation is trivially recoverable and is not equivalent to encryption at rest. The file sits on an SMB share (README.md: 'Microsoft Access 2003 (.mdb) on a SMB file share') with no KMS key, no BitLocker/EFS configuration, and no encryption settings anywhere in the repository; the SQL Server 2012 reporting copy likewise has no documented TDE configuration.
findings.gap: The customer dataset is effectively unencrypted at rest on a file share. Anyone who can copy the .mdb file obtains the data, and the shared password offers no meaningful protection.
findings.recommendation: Migrate the data to a managed store with encryption at rest under a customer-managed key (e.g. RDS with KMS) and, in the interim, enable volume-level encryption on the file server and tighten share ACLs.

findings.title: Machine-Readable API Specification
findings.description: No machine-readable interface description exists. Searched for openapi.yaml/json, swagger.yaml/json, AsyncAPI documents, *.graphql/*.gql and *.smithy across the repository; the only files present are README.md, index.cfm, download.cfm and .gitignore. No dependency manifest exists that could declare a spec-generation toolchain.
findings.gap: No OpenAPI/GraphQL/Smithy artifact, so agent tool definitions cannot be generated and would have to be hand-authored against scraped HTML.
findings.recommendation: Once an API surface exists (API-Q1), publish and version an OpenAPI 3.x document for the document search and download operations, generated from the implementation rather than hand-maintained, and validate it in CI.

findings.title: Structured Error Responses
findings.description: No error handling exists in either page. download.cfm interpolates url.id directly into SQL (line 4) and passes doc.filename into <cfcontent file="#filepath#">; a missing id, a non-numeric id or a missing file on D:\docroot\files yields an unhandled ColdFusion exception page. There is no <cftry>/<cfcatch>, no <cferror>, no onError handler, and no Application.cfc. Failure is communicated as an HTML ColdFusion error page, not a structured body.
findings.gap: Callers receive HTML stack-trace pages rather than machine-readable error codes, so an agent cannot distinguish a retriable fault (database unavailable) from a terminal one (document id not found, file missing on disk).
findings.recommendation: Add an Application.cfc onError handler and <cftry>/<cfcatch> around both queries and the file-streaming call, returning a consistent JSON error envelope with an error code, message and retryable flag; map not-found, invalid-input and backend-failure to distinct codes.

findings.title: Queryable Current State
findings.description: Current state is readable only through the HTML UI. index.cfm renders doc_id, title, category, uploaded_by and uploaded_on into a presentation table, and download.cfm looks up a single filename by doc_id. There is no status query endpoint and no JSON representation of document state; the state must be recovered by parsing markup.
findings.gap: An agent cannot inspect document state in a machine-readable form before acting; it would have to scrape the HTML table, coupling it to presentation markup that carries no contract.
findings.recommendation: Expose the document metadata already selected in index.cfm lines 23-27 as a JSON read endpoint (list and get-by-id) so callers can inspect state without parsing HTML.

findings.title: Sandbox/Staging Environment
findings.description: No non-production environment is defined. The repository contains no environment-specific configuration, no docker-compose file, no seed or synthetic data script, and no IaC. The README describes the sole deployment path as "Copy .cfm files over the network share to wwwroot" on a single Windows EC2 instance, implying changes are exercised directly against production.
findings.gap: There is no environment with production-equivalent data shape in which agent behaviour could be rehearsed, so the first execution of any new integration would be against live documents and the live database.
findings.recommendation: Stand up a staging instance with a restored, de-identified copy of the docportal schema and a representative document set on separate storage, and require integrations to be validated there before production exposure.

findings.title: Selective Query Support
findings.description: The document listing query in index.cfm is unbounded: SELECT doc_id, title, category, uploaded_by, uploaded_on FROM documents WHERE title LIKE '%#url.q#%' ORDER BY uploaded_on DESC. There is no TOP clause, no OFFSET/FETCH, no limit or cursor parameter, and no page-size control. The only filter is the single free-text title term; category and uploaded_by are returned but not filterable. With an empty url.q (the <cfparam> default on line 8) the predicate matches every row in the table.
findings.gap: A caller that omits the search term receives the entire documents table in one response. There is no pagination or result cap to bound the payload, and no structured filters to narrow it by category, uploader or date.
findings.recommendation: Add server-enforced pagination (page size with a hard maximum, plus a cursor or OFFSET/FETCH clause) and explicit filter parameters for category, uploaded_by and date range, and return the total count so callers can page deterministically.

findings.title: Input Validation and Schema Enforcement
findings.description: There is no input validation anywhere. index.cfm takes url.q via <cfparam> with no type, length or character constraint and interpolates it directly into the SQL LIKE predicate (line 26), which the file's own comment acknowledges: "SQL built by string concatenation - injection vulnerable". download.cfm interpolates url.id straight into WHERE doc_id = #url.id# (line 4) with no numeric check and no <cfparam>, then concatenates the resulting doc.filename onto D:\docroot\files\ and passes it to <cfcontent file="..."> — a path-traversal exposure the file comments also acknowledge. No <cfqueryparam>, no validation library, no request size limit and no structured validation error responses exist.
findings.gap: Both entry points accept arbitrary input shapes with no validation and interpolate them into SQL and into a filesystem path. Malformed or hostile input is neither rejected nor reported; it reaches the database and the filesystem, and failures surface as ColdFusion error pages with no field-level detail.
findings.recommendation: Bind every query parameter with <cfqueryparam> (cf_sql_integer for url.id, cf_sql_varchar with a maxlength for url.q), validate url.id as a positive integer before use, canonicalise the resolved filepath and reject any path that escapes D:\docroot\files, and return structured validation errors naming the offending field and constraint.

findings.title: Temporal Metadata and Freshness
findings.description: Partial temporal metadata exists. dbo.documents carries uploaded_on, which index.cfm selects and sorts on (ORDER BY uploaded_on DESC) and renders with dateFormat(uploaded_on, 'mm/dd/yyyy') — dropping the time component and any timezone. There is no updated_at or last-modified column, no evidence of UTC normalisation, no Cache-Control or X-Data-Age header, and no consistency or freshness indicator on any response.
findings.gap: Timestamps are upload-time only, rendered date-only with no timezone, and no response metadata signals whether the data returned is current. An agent reasoning about document recency cannot establish ordering within a day or detect staleness.
findings.recommendation: Store and return uploaded_on as a full UTC timestamp in ISO 8601 form (not a localised date string), add a last-modified column maintained on change, and include freshness metadata on responses once the JSON surface exists.

findings.title: Schema Versioning and API Contracts
findings.description: Neither the schema nor the interface is versioned. There are no database migration files, no JSON Schema/Avro/Protobuf definitions, no schema registry and no OpenAPI definitions. The page URLs carry no version segment (index.cfm, download.cfm?id=) and no Accept-Version handling exists. There is no changelog or deprecation notice; the only version marker in the repository is the cosmetic footer string "ACME Document Portal v2.3" in index.cfm line 45, and the header comment records the file was "Built 2007, last edited 2016". No CI configuration exists, so no breaking-change detection runs.
findings.gap: The documents schema and the page contract can both change with no version signal and no detection, so any agent tool binding would break silently and without warning.
findings.recommendation: Bring the docportal schema under migration control, version the new API surface in its path, and add breaking-change detection (OpenAPI diff on the spec, plus migration review) to a CI pipeline.

findings.title: Distributed Tracing and Structured Logging
findings.description: Neither tracing nor structured logging is present. No OpenTelemetry or X-Ray instrumentation exists, no traceparent or correlation header is read or propagated, and no request_id or correlation_id is generated. Neither index.cfm nor download.cfm emits a log line of any kind — there is no <cflog>, no Application.cfc and no logging configuration in the repository. The only diagnostics available are IIS and ColdFusion server logs outside this repository.
findings.gap: There is no correlation identifier and no application log, so a failed request cannot be reconstructed. An agent-initiated failure would be indistinguishable from any other request in the server logs.
findings.recommendation: Add an Application.cfc that accepts or generates a correlation id per request, propagates it to responses, and writes structured JSON log entries for each search and download including the correlation id, principal and outcome.

findings.title: Alerting on Error Rates and Latency
findings.description: No alerting is configured. The repository contains no IaC and therefore no CloudWatch alarms, no anomaly detection, no SLO definitions and no PagerDuty/OpsGenie integration; there are no health or readiness endpoints in either page to alert on. The README notes the design is a "Single instance; reboot = downtime", with no monitoring described.
findings.gap: Error-rate and latency degradation on the document pages is undetected, so an overload or outage would be discovered only when users or callers report it.
findings.recommendation: Add a health endpoint and define alarms on error rate and latency percentiles for the agent-facing surface, routed to an on-call destination, before exposing the system to automated callers.

findings.title: Infrastructure Governance for Agent-Facing Surface
findings.description: No infrastructure is defined as code. Searched for *.tf/*.tfvars, CloudFormation templates, CDK entry points, Helm charts, Kustomize overlays and Ansible playbooks — none exist; the repository holds only README.md, index.cfm, download.cfm and .gitignore. The integration surface is therefore configured by hand: IIS 7 and the ColdFusion Administrator datasource are managed through consoles per the README, and deployment is "Copy .cfm files over the network share to wwwroot". None of the three required sub-checks pass — no IaC definition, no automated plan or peer review of infrastructure change, and no drift detection.
findings.gap: The server, the datasource credential and the network exposure are all manually managed with no reviewable definition and no drift detection, so the configuration an agent would depend on is neither reproducible nor auditable.
findings.recommendation: Define the agent-facing surface as code — the compute, the gateway, the IAM/identity configuration and the secret — under pull-request review, and enable drift detection against those definitions.

findings.title: CI/CD with API Contract Testing
findings.description: No pipeline exists. Searched for .github/workflows/, .gitlab-ci.yml, Jenkinsfile, buildspec.yml and appspec.yml — none are present. Deployment is manual file copy to wwwroot over a network share per the README, so there is no build, no automated test stage, and no contract or breaking-change check between a change and production.
findings.gap: Changes reach production without any automated verification, so a modification that breaks the integration surface (for example renaming a column in the index.cfm SELECT list) is caught only in production.
findings.recommendation: Introduce a pipeline that builds, tests and deploys the application, and add contract validation of the agent-facing API — spec validation plus a breaking-change diff — as a gate before deployment.

findings.title: Rollback Capability
findings.description: No rollback mechanism exists. There is no blue/green or canary configuration, no CodeDeploy or Helm release management, and no feature flags. Deployment is an in-place file copy to wwwroot on a single instance, so reverting means manually copying the previous .cfm files back — and the README notes the instance is a single point of failure ("reboot = downtime, disk loss = data loss"). No deployment artifact or release version is retained; the last recorded edit to index.cfm was 2016.
findings.gap: Recovery from a bad change depends on a manual file copy with no retained known-good artifact and no automated revert path, so the 15-30 minute recovery target cannot be relied on.
findings.recommendation: Deploy versioned, immutable artifacts to at least two instances behind a load balancer with an automated revert to the previous version, and rehearse the rollback so the recovery time is measured rather than assumed.

findings.title: API Test Coverage
findings.description: There are no tests of any kind. The repository contains no test directory, no test files, no Postman/Newman collection and no test framework dependency (there is no dependency manifest at all). Neither index.cfm nor download.cfm has any accompanying test for input handling, output format, error responses or edge cases such as a non-numeric url.id or a filename that does not resolve on disk.
findings.gap: The behaviour of the two entry points is entirely unverified, so no change can be shown not to alter the contract a caller depends on.
findings.recommendation: Add automated tests for the document search and download operations covering valid input, invalid and missing id values, empty search terms, and the missing-file case, and run them in the pipeline introduced for ENG-Q2.

findings.title: Encryption at Rest for Agent-Accessible Data
findings.description: No encryption at rest is configured or evidenced. The README places document bytes on a local Windows disk at D:\docroot\files with "no object storage, no backups offsite", and metadata in SQL Server 2005 — a version that predates SQL Server's modern encryption defaults and reached end of support in April 2016. There is no IaC, so no kms_key_id, no customer-managed key and no EBS or database encryption setting exists anywhere in the repository. The README also records that traffic runs over plain HTTP with no TLS, so the data is unprotected in transit as well.
findings.gap: Document contents and metadata are stored unencrypted on a single instance with no key management, so loss or theft of the disk exposes the entire corpus an agent would be able to read.
findings.recommendation: Move document bytes to encrypted object storage with a customer-managed KMS key, enable encryption at rest on the database volume as part of the platform upgrade off SQL Server 2005, and terminate TLS in front of the application.

findings.title: Machine-Readable API Specification
findings.description: No machine-readable API specification exists. Searched for `openapi.*`, `swagger.*`, `*.graphql`, `*.gql`, `*.smithy`, and AsyncAPI documents across the repository (4 files total: .gitignore, README.md, helpdesk/settings.py, tickets/views.py) — zero results. No spec-generating dependency is declared (no dependency manifest is present at all; README.md states pip requirements are pinned to versions no longer on PyPI mirrors).
findings.gap: Agent tool definitions would have to be authored by hand against HTML-rendering views and would drift from implementation immediately.
findings.recommendation: Once the JSON API from API-Q1 exists, generate an OpenAPI 3 document from code annotations (e.g., drf-spectacular) and publish it in the repository and at a served `/api/schema` path.

findings.title: Structured Error Responses
findings.description: Responses carry no structured error contract. `ticket_search` builds an HTML string and returns `HttpResponse(out)`; `ticket_list` renders a template. Neither view has try/except handling, and `DEBUG = True` in helpdesk/settings.py means unhandled exceptions return full Django HTML stack traces instead of machine-readable errors. No error-code enum, error body schema, or retryable indicator exists anywhere in tickets/views.py.
findings.gap: An agent cannot distinguish retriable failures (database unavailable) from terminal ones (bad input). A failed call returns an HTML traceback page with HTTP 500.
findings.recommendation: Define a JSON error envelope (`code`, `message`, `retryable`) applied by a single exception handler on the new API layer, and set `DEBUG = False` so tracebacks are never emitted to callers.

findings.title: Sandbox/Staging Environment
findings.description: No sandbox or staging environment is defined. The repository contains a single `helpdesk/settings.py` with `DEBUG = True` and one hardcoded database (`helpdesk` on 127.0.0.1) — there are no per-environment settings modules, no docker-compose, no seed or synthetic data scripts, and no environment-specific IaC. README.md describes deployment as 'git pull on the server + manual apache restart' against a single EC2 instance.
findings.gap: There is no non-production target with production-equivalent data shape, so the first execution of any agent against this system would be against live helpdesk data.
findings.recommendation: Create a staging environment from IaC with a sanitized copy of the ticket schema and seeded synthetic tickets, and require agent validation there before production access.

findings.title: Selective Query Support
findings.description: Queries are unbounded. `ticket_list` executes `SELECT id, subject, requester, priority FROM tickets_ticket WHERE status = '...' ORDER BY created DESC` with no `LIMIT`/`OFFSET`, and `ticket_search` runs `LIKE '%...%'` across the table and materializes every row with `fetchall()`. The only filter available is the single `status` or `q` GET parameter; no pagination, cursor, page-size, or sort parameters exist.
findings.gap: An agent calling the list view receives every open ticket in one response, exhausting context windows and loading the co-located database.
findings.recommendation: Add `limit`/`offset` (or cursor) parameters with a server-enforced maximum page size and a default cap, and expose field-level filtering on status, priority, and date range.

findings.title: Input Validation and Schema Enforcement
findings.description: There is no input validation, and the inputs flow into raw SQL by string interpolation. `ticket_list` takes `request.GET.get('status', 'OPEN')` and formats it into the WHERE clause with `% status`; `ticket_search` formats `q` into a `LIKE '%%%s%%'` clause. Searched for validation libraries and parameterized queries: no forms, no serializers, no pydantic/marshmallow, no `cursor.execute(sql, params)` parameter binding, and no request size limits anywhere in the repository. `ticket_search` additionally concatenates row values into an HTML response without escaping.
findings.gap: Unvalidated input is concatenated into SQL — an exploitable SQL injection path — and there are no structured field-level validation errors for an agent to self-correct against. Unescaped output concatenation is an additional stored/reflected XSS path.
findings.recommendation: Convert both queries to parameter binding (`cursor.execute(sql, [status])`) or the Django ORM, validate `status` against an allowlist enum and `q` against a length/charset bound, return field-level JSON validation errors, and escape all template output.

findings.title: Temporal Metadata and Freshness
findings.description: Temporal metadata exists but is not exposed or normalized. `ticket_list` orders by a `created` column (`ORDER BY created DESC`), so creation time is stored, but `created` is not included in the selected fields returned to callers, there is no `updated_at` evidence, and helpdesk/settings.py sets `TIME_ZONE = 'America/New_York'` with Django 1.4 (no `USE_TZ` setting present), so timestamps are local-time rather than UTC-normalized. No `Cache-Control`, data-age, or consistency-level signaling exists in the responses.
findings.gap: Callers receive no timestamps at all and no freshness or staleness indicator, so an agent cannot reason about how current a ticket record is.
findings.recommendation: Return `created` and `updated` timestamps in UTC (ISO-8601) on every ticket payload, set `USE_TZ`-equivalent UTC storage, and add explicit freshness headers on the API layer.

findings.title: Schema Versioning and API Contracts
findings.description: No schema or contract versioning exists. Searched for migration files, JSON Schema, Avro/Protobuf definitions, a schema registry, `/v1/` URL patterns, `Accept-Version` handling, changelogs, and breaking-change detection tooling: none found. The ticket schema is implied only by the hand-written SQL column lists in tickets/views.py; Django 1.4 predates built-in migrations and no South migrations directory is present. `ROOT_URLCONF = 'helpdesk.urls'` references a URL module that is not in the repository, so even the route contract is not captured here.
findings.gap: Any column rename or type change in `tickets_ticket` silently breaks the raw SQL in tickets/views.py and any agent tool bound to it, with no versioning or CI detection to catch it.
findings.recommendation: Capture the ticket schema in versioned migrations, version the new API under `/api/v1/`, and add breaking-change detection (OpenAPI diff) to CI once a spec exists.

findings.title: Distributed Tracing and Structured Logging
findings.description: There is neither tracing nor structured logging. Searched for OpenTelemetry, X-Ray instrumentation, `traceparent` propagation, JSON log formatting, and `request_id`/`correlation_id` fields: none present. helpdesk/settings.py defines no `LOGGING` configuration at all, and the only log statement in the codebase is the unstructured `print "searching tickets for:", q` in tickets/views.py. Logs are therefore plain Apache text files on a single EC2 instance (README.md).
findings.gap: An agent-initiated request cannot be correlated across the request path, and there is no trace ID or request ID to pivot on when a call fails.
findings.recommendation: Add a `LOGGING` configuration emitting JSON with a per-request correlation ID (accepting an inbound `traceparent`/request-ID header from the agent), and ship logs off-host to CloudWatch Logs.

findings.title: Alerting on Error Rates and Latency
findings.description: No alerting is configured. The repository contains no CloudWatch alarms, no anomaly detection, no PagerDuty/OpsGenie integration, and no SLO definitions — there is no IaC of any kind. The only operational notification path is Django's `ADMINS = (('IT Ops', 'it-ops@acme-corp.internal'),)` in helpdesk/settings.py, which emails unhandled exceptions; with `DEBUG = True` even that path is suppressed, because Django does not send error mail while DEBUG is on.
findings.gap: Error-rate and latency degradation on the endpoints an agent would consume is entirely undetected, so cascading failures would be discovered only by user complaint.
findings.recommendation: Publish error-rate and latency metrics for the agent-facing endpoints and configure alarms with explicit thresholds routed to IT Ops; as an immediate step, set `DEBUG = False` so the existing ADMINS error mail actually fires.

findings.title: Infrastructure Governance for Agent-Facing Surface
findings.description: The agent-facing surface is not defined as code. Searched the repository for Terraform (`.tf`), CloudFormation, CDK, Helm, Kustomize, and Ansible definitions: none exist. README.md states the architecture is a single EC2 instance with Apache 2.2 + mod_wsgi on Ubuntu 12.04 and PostgreSQL on the same box, deployed by 'git pull on the server + manual apache restart'. There is consequently no peer-reviewed change process for the integration surface and no drift detection (no AWS Config rules).
findings.gap: All three required controls are absent: no IaC definition of the serving/IAM/network surface, no automated plan or review gate on infrastructure changes, and no drift detection. Host configuration is mutable by hand.
findings.recommendation: Codify the agent-facing surface (instance/ALB, security groups, IAM role, secrets) in Terraform or CDK, require pull-request review with an automated plan step, and enable drift detection.

findings.title: CI/CD with API Contract Testing
findings.description: There is no CI/CD pipeline. Searched for `.github/workflows/`, `.gitlab-ci.yml`, `Jenkinsfile`, `buildspec.yml`, and CodePipeline definitions: none present (the repository contains only .gitignore, README.md, helpdesk/settings.py, and tickets/views.py). README.md confirms deployment is a manual `git pull` plus Apache restart, so no automated test, no API contract test, and no breaking-change detection runs before production.
findings.gap: API-breaking changes reach production unchecked, with nothing in the path to detect that an agent-facing contract has changed.
findings.recommendation: Introduce a pipeline that runs unit and API tests on every commit and blocks merges on an OpenAPI diff that reports breaking changes against the published spec.

findings.title: Rollback Capability
findings.description: No rollback capability is defined. Deployment is 'git pull on the server + manual apache restart' (README.md), with no blue/green configuration, no CodeDeploy rollback trigger, no canary or traffic shifting, and no feature flags anywhere in the repository. Recovery would depend on a manual `git checkout` of a prior commit on a single host, and any accompanying database change has no down-path (no migrations exist — see DISC-Q1).
findings.gap: There is no tested, time-bounded path back to the last known-good state, so a change that breaks an agent-facing endpoint leaves agents non-functional for an unbounded period.
findings.recommendation: Adopt versioned, immutable deploys with a one-command rollback (e.g., release directories with an atomic symlink swap, or blue/green behind a load balancer) and rehearse rollback to meet a 15-30 minute objective.

findings.title: API Test Coverage
findings.description: There is effectively no test coverage. No test files exist in the repository (no `tests.py`, no `test_*.py`, no Postman/Newman collections, no integration test directory), and no CI configuration to run them. README.md states 'No tests beyond a couple of stale unit tests' — those tests are not present in this repository snapshot, so even they cannot be executed or verified.
findings.gap: Input handling, output format, and error behavior of the endpoints an agent would consume are completely unverified, including the raw SQL paths flagged in DATA-Q4.
findings.recommendation: Add endpoint tests covering the status filter, the search path, empty results, and malformed input for both views, and run them in the pipeline from ENG-Q2.

findings.title: Encryption at Rest for Agent-Accessible Data
findings.description: Encryption at rest is not configured or evidenced. The data store is PostgreSQL 9.1 running on the same EC2 instance as the application (README.md), connected over `127.0.0.1:5432` (helpdesk/settings.py). Searched for `kms_key_id`, customer-managed KMS keys, and encryption settings in IaC: no IaC exists, so there is no evidence of EBS volume encryption, and README.md notes backups are a daily `pg_dump` cron with no mention of encryption for the dump files.
findings.gap: Ticket data — including requester identity and free-text subjects — and its backups have no demonstrable encryption at rest, so host or backup-file compromise exposes everything an agent can read.
findings.recommendation: Enable EBS encryption with a KMS key for the data volume (or migrate to RDS with encryption at rest enabled), and encrypt pg_dump output at rest with restricted access.

findings.title: Machine-Readable API Specification
findings.description: No OpenAPI, Swagger, AsyncAPI, GraphQL or Smithy artifact exists. The repository contains 4 files total; the only interface description is the Struts action mapping in struts-config.xml, which describes forwards to JSP pages, not request/response schemas. No spec-generating dependency is present (no dependency manifest at all — README states jars are committed to /lib with no version manifest).
findings.gap: There is no machine-readable contract from which agent tool definitions could be generated; request fields are only discoverable by reading LoanForm getters referenced in LoanAction.
findings.recommendation: Publish an OpenAPI 3 document for the extracted loan pricing/submission API and generate it from annotations so it cannot drift from the implementation.

findings.title: Structured Error Responses
findings.description: LoanAction.execute declares 'throws Exception' and saveApplication propagates all JDBC failures unhandled; the only failure path configured is the Struts input attribute input='/loan.jsp', which re-renders an HTML form. There is no error code, error body, or retryable indicator anywhere in the code.
findings.gap: Callers cannot distinguish retriable faults (Oracle connection failure, timeout) from terminal faults (bad input), and errors surface as container HTML error pages.
findings.recommendation: Return structured error payloads (code, message, retryable) from the new API layer and map JDBC/validation failures onto them explicitly.

findings.title: Queryable Current State
findings.description: The action supports only pricing (forward 'quote') and creation (forward 'confirm'). struts-config.xml declares no read/list mapping and LoanAction contains no SELECT — there is no way to query an existing application's state, and no status column is written by the INSERT.
findings.gap: An agent cannot inspect whether an application already exists or what state it is in before acting, which also makes retry-safety impossible to establish client-side.
findings.recommendation: Add a read operation that returns application records and their status, so callers can read before write.

findings.title: Sandbox/Staging Environment
findings.description: README documents 'No unit tests; testing is a shared UAT environment' and deployment as 'Manual WAR upload via WebLogic admin console'. The repository contains no environment-specific configuration, no docker-compose, no seed/synthetic data scripts, and no environment IaC. The hardcoded connection string points at a production host (dbprod01) with no environment switch.
findings.gap: The only test environment is a shared UAT instance with no isolation, no reproducible data shape and no automated provisioning, and the code's default target is production.
findings.recommendation: Provide an isolated, seedable environment with externalized connection configuration so agent behavior can be exercised without touching dbprod01.

findings.title: Input Validation and Schema Enforcement
findings.description: No input validation exists. LoanForm values are consumed directly: getAnnualRate()/getTermMonths()/getPrincipal() feed the amortization formula with no range or null checks (a zero rate or zero term yields division by zero or NaN), and the applicant name is concatenated straight into SQL — 'INSERT INTO applications (applicant, ...) VALUES ('" + lf.getApplicantName() + "'' — then passed to prepareStatement, so the PreparedStatement provides no parameterization and the endpoint is SQL-injectable. No javax.validation annotations, no Struts validation framework (no validation.xml), and no structured field-level error responses are present.
findings.gap: Malformed or hostile input is neither rejected nor reported per-field; the only write path is open to SQL injection through the applicant name, and numeric inputs are unbounded.
findings.recommendation: Bind parameters with real placeholders (ps.setString/setDouble) instead of string concatenation, add field-level validation with range checks on principal/rate/term, and return structured validation errors identifying the offending field.

findings.title: Temporal Metadata and Freshness
findings.description: The INSERT writes only (applicant, principal, rate, term, officer) — no created_at, updated_at or event_time column, and no timezone handling or UTC normalization appears anywhere. There are no Cache-Control, freshness or consistency headers because responses are JSP views.
findings.gap: Records carry no timestamps, so an agent cannot determine when an application was created or whether the data it reads is current.
findings.recommendation: Add created_at/updated_at columns stored in UTC and expose them on read responses along with a freshness or consistency indicator.

findings.title: Schema Versioning and API Contracts
findings.description: No versioning or contract artifacts exist: the action path is '/loan' with no /v1/ segment or Accept-Version handling, there are no migration files, no JSON Schema/Avro/Protobuf definitions, no schema registry reference, no changelog, and no CI (so no breaking-change detection or contract tests). README notes dependency jars are committed with 'no version manifest', so even library versions are unversioned.
findings.gap: Any change to the form fields or the applications table is invisible to callers and would silently break agent tool bindings.
findings.recommendation: Version the extracted API path, manage the database schema with checked-in migrations, and add breaking-change detection (OpenAPI diff or consumer contract tests) to a pipeline.

findings.title: Distributed Tracing and Structured Logging
findings.description: Neither tracing nor structured logging is present: no OpenTelemetry/X-Ray instrumentation, no traceparent or correlation-id propagation, and no log statements at all in LoanAction.java. There is no logging configuration file and no logging dependency (the project has no dependency manifest — jars are committed per README).
findings.gap: A failed agent-initiated submission leaves no correlated trace or log record, so it cannot be reconstructed or attributed.
findings.recommendation: Add structured JSON logging with a correlation id accepted from the caller and propagated into the data access path, then instrument with OpenTelemetry.

findings.title: Alerting on Error Rates and Latency
findings.description: No alerting configuration exists anywhere in the repository: no CloudWatch alarms or IaC, no PagerDuty/OpsGenie integration, no SLO definitions, no health-check endpoint (struts-config.xml declares only the /loan action). Deployment is manual via the WebLogic console per README, so there is no pipeline-managed monitoring either.
findings.gap: Degradation of the loan path would be detected only by user reports, after agent callers have already begun failing or retrying.
findings.recommendation: Define error-rate and latency SLOs for the loan endpoint and configure alerting on them, starting with WebLogic/Oracle metrics already available.

findings.title: Infrastructure Governance for Agent-Facing Surface
findings.description: There is no infrastructure as code: no Terraform, CloudFormation, CDK, Helm, Kubernetes or Ansible artifacts exist (the repository contains only README.md, .gitignore, struts-config.xml and one Java source file). README states deployment is 'Manual WAR upload via WebLogic admin console' on a Solaris host, so the integration surface, credentials and networking are configured by hand with no plan review and no drift detection.
findings.gap: All three sub-checks fail: the surface is not defined as code, changes are not reviewable, and drift is undetectable.
findings.recommendation: Codify the deployment target, datasource and network/auth configuration as IaC under peer review, with drift detection, before exposing the system to agents.

findings.title: CI/CD with API Contract Testing
findings.description: No pipeline exists: no .github/workflows, no .gitlab-ci.yml, Jenkinsfile, or buildspec.yml. The build is Apache Ant with jars committed to /lib (README), and release is a manual console upload. With no pipeline there is also no contract test, no spec validation and no breaking-change gate.
findings.gap: API-breaking changes reach the shared environment with no automated detection, so agent tool bindings can break without warning.
findings.recommendation: Stand up a build pipeline that compiles, runs tests, and validates the published API contract against the previous version on every change.

findings.title: Rollback Capability
findings.description: Rollback is manual and unbounded: deployment is a WAR uploaded by hand through the WebLogic admin console (README), with no blue/green or canary configuration, no feature flags, no traffic shifting, and no retained previous artifact referenced in the repository. The last Solaris host in the data center is the single deployment target.
findings.gap: Recovering from a change that breaks the agent-facing surface depends on a human locating and re-uploading a prior WAR, with no tested path or time guarantee.
findings.recommendation: Keep versioned, immutable build artifacts and automate redeploy of the previous version; longer term adopt blue/green or traffic shifting on a supported runtime.

findings.title: API Test Coverage
findings.description: There are no tests of any kind: no test directory, no JUnit/REST Assured/Postman artifacts, and README states plainly 'No unit tests; testing is a shared UAT environment'. The amortization formula in execute() and the write path in saveApplication are therefore entirely unverified.
findings.gap: No automated coverage of input handling, output values, or error behavior for the operations an agent would call.
findings.recommendation: Add unit tests for the amortization calculation and boundary inputs, plus endpoint-level tests for the submit path, and run them in CI.

findings.title: Encryption at Rest for Agent-Accessible Data
findings.description: No encryption-at-rest evidence exists for the Oracle 11g store holding applicant PII: there is no IaC, no KMS or TDE reference, no tablespace encryption configuration, and the JDBC URL 'jdbc:oracle:thin:@dbprod01:1521:LOANDB' specifies no TLS or wallet settings (so the connection is unencrypted in transit as well).
findings.gap: Encryption at rest for the applications table is unverified and uncontrolled from this repository, as is transport encryption to the database.
findings.recommendation: Confirm and document Oracle TDE (or equivalent) for the LOANDB tablespaces and enable TLS on the JDBC connection.

findings.title: Machine-Readable API Specification
findings.description: A WSDL exists (wsdl/PurchaseOrderService.wsdl) but its header comment states 'Hand-maintained WSDL - drifts from implementation. RPC/encoded style.' README.md repeats that wsgen/wsimport are 'run by hand' and that the 'WSDL maintained by hand; drifts from the implementation'. Searched for openapi.*, swagger.*, *.graphql, *.gql, *.smithy, asyncapi.* and for any build file that generates a contract: none exist (the repository has only .gitignore, README.md, one Java source, and the WSDL).
findings.gap: The one machine-readable artifact is RPC/encoded (not WS-I compliant, poorly supported by modern tooling), is not generated from the implementation, and is known to be stale. Agent tool definitions generated from it would not match runtime behaviour.
findings.recommendation: Generate the contract from the JAX-WS annotations as a build step (wsgen in the build, committed artifact verified in CI) and move the binding from rpc/encoded to document/literal so standard tooling can consume it.

findings.title: Structured Error Responses
findings.description: Errors are returned as an untyped string: the catch block in submitOrder returns "ERROR:" + e.getMessage() for every failure, and success returns "ACCEPTED:" + poNumber. There is no SOAP fault definition in the WSDL, no error code, no retryable indicator, and no field-level detail. A parse failure, a database outage, and a constraint violation are indistinguishable to the caller except by raw exception text.
findings.gap: No error code, no retryable/terminal classification, and no structured body. An agent cannot decide whether to retry, escalate, or abort, so it will either retry a terminal failure indefinitely or abandon a transient one.
findings.recommendation: Define typed SOAP faults (or a structured response envelope) carrying errorCode, message, retryable, and field-level validation detail, and stop propagating raw exception text to callers.

findings.title: Queryable Current State
findings.description: The service is write-only. portType PurchaseOrderPortType declares exactly one operation, submitOrder; there is no getOrder, no order-status query, and no list operation in the WSDL or in PurchaseOrderService.java. The partner_orders table is only ever inserted into (no SELECT appears anywhere in the source).
findings.gap: An agent cannot read current state before or after acting - it cannot check whether an order already exists before submitting (so it cannot avoid duplicates itself) nor confirm the outcome of an uncertain call.
findings.recommendation: Add a read operation (getOrderStatus by partnerId + poNumber) so agents can perform read-before-write and post-failure reconciliation.

findings.title: Sandbox/Staging Environment
findings.description: No non-production environment is defined. The repository has no environment-specific configuration, no docker-compose, no seed-data or synthetic-data scripts, and no IaC; the only datasource is the hardcoded production-looking Oracle instance at 10.0.9.30:1521:PARTDB in PurchaseOrderService.java. README.md states 'partner onboarding is a manual SOAP-UI session', which is the closest thing to a test procedure.
findings.gap: There is no environment with production-equivalent data shape where agent behaviour can be exercised safely; the first execution of an agent workflow would hit the live partner order table.
findings.recommendation: Stand up a staging deployment with a seeded Oracle schema and externalized connection configuration so agent integration can be tested before production exposure.

findings.title: Input Validation and Schema Enforcement
findings.description: There is no input validation and the input path is actively unsafe. poXml is parsed with a default DocumentBuilderFactory with no secure-processing feature, no DTD/external-entity restriction and no entity-expansion limit (lines 30-33) - the source comment itself states 'XML parsed with no XXE protection (external entities allowed)' and README.md lists 'XML parsing has no protection against XXE / billion-laughs'. poNumber and amount are read via getElementsByTagName(...).item(0).getTextContent() with no null check (a missing element throws NullPointerException), no type check on amount, and no length or range validation. The values are then concatenated into SQL: executeUpdate("INSERT INTO partner_orders (...) VALUES ('" + partnerId + "', '" + poNumber + "', " + amount + ")") - an unparameterized statement taking caller-controlled strings, so the endpoint is SQL-injectable. There are no validation libraries (no javax.validation usage), no schema validation against an XSD, and no request size limit.
findings.gap: No validation at the boundary and no structured rejection. Malformed agent payloads either crash into a generic "ERROR:" string or are written through; worse, unvalidated input reaches both an XXE-capable parser and string-built SQL. This is severe evidence recorded at the RISK-QUALITY severity this question carries.
findings.recommendation: Parameterize the INSERT with PreparedStatement, harden the parser (FEATURE_SECURE_PROCESSING, disallow-doctype-decl, disable external entities), validate poXml against an XSD, and return field-level structured validation faults.

findings.title: Temporal Metadata and Freshness
findings.description: No temporal metadata is written or returned. The insert populates only partner_id, po_number and amount - there is no created_at, updated_at, or event_time column in the statement, no timezone handling, and no UTC normalization anywhere in the source. The response carries no timestamp, no Cache-Control, and no freshness or consistency indicator.
findings.gap: An order carries no record of when it was submitted, so neither an agent nor an operator can reason about ordering, recency, or duplicate timing; and no read path exists that could signal staleness.
findings.recommendation: Add created_at (UTC) on partner_orders, set it on insert, and return it in the submission result so agents can reason about and reconcile submission time.

findings.title: Schema Versioning and API Contracts
findings.description: The contract is unversioned and manually maintained. targetNamespace is http://acme.com/partner with no version segment, the service path (/po/PurchaseOrderService) carries no /v1/, and there is no Accept-Version handling. The WSDL's own comment says it drifts from the implementation. There are no XSD files, no JSON Schema, no Avro/Protobuf, no schema registry, no database migration files (the partner_orders schema exists only implicitly in an INSERT statement), no changelog, no deprecation notices, and no breaking-change detection - there is no CI configuration at all in the repository.
findings.gap: Nothing detects or communicates a breaking contract change: an agent tool binding would break silently, and the database schema has no versioned definition in the repository at all.
findings.recommendation: Version the namespace and endpoint, generate the contract from code, add the partner_orders schema to a migration tool, and run a WSDL/schema diff gate in CI to catch breaking changes.

findings.title: Distributed Tracing and Structured Logging
findings.description: There is no observability instrumentation. PurchaseOrderService.java contains no logger of any kind, no OpenTelemetry or X-Ray SDK, no traceparent or correlation-id handling, and no request identifier is generated or returned. Searched the dependency surface (there is no build file - README.md states the build is Ant with wsgen/wsimport run by hand) and found no tracing or logging libraries. The only failure signal is the "ERROR:" string returned to the caller.
findings.gap: An agent-initiated submission cannot be traced or correlated. When a call fails or times out, there is no log line, no request id, and no trace to reconstruct what happened inside the service.
findings.recommendation: Add structured JSON logging with a generated correlation id returned in every response, and instrument the endpoint with OpenTelemetry so agent-initiated calls can be traced end to end.

findings.title: Alerting on Error Rates and Latency
findings.description: No alerting exists. There are no CloudWatch alarms, no anomaly detection, no PagerDuty/OpsGenie configuration, no SLO definitions, and no monitoring configuration of any kind in the repository (no IaC, no CI/CD, no config files beyond .gitignore). README.md documents the runtime as an out-of-support JBoss AS 5.1 / Java 6 stack and mentions no monitoring.
findings.gap: Degradation of the endpoint an agent depends on would be detected only by the agent failing, or by a partner complaint - there is no error-rate or latency threshold that notifies anyone.
findings.recommendation: Define error-rate and latency SLOs for submitOrder and configure alerting on them, including an alert on connection-exhaustion failures given the per-call DriverManager pattern.

findings.title: Infrastructure Governance for Agent-Facing Surface
findings.description: The agent-facing surface is not defined as code. Searched for Terraform (.tf/.tfvars), CloudFormation, CDK, Helm, Kustomize, Ansible, and Kubernetes manifests: none exist. README.md describes a WAR hand-deployed to JBoss AS 5.1 on RHEL 6 with the build run by hand via Ant and wsgen/wsimport. The endpoint address, the datasource, and the credentials are embedded in source and in the hand-edited WSDL rather than in reviewed infrastructure definitions, and there is no drift detection.
findings.gap: None of the three required controls are present: no IaC for the endpoint/network/credentials, no automated plan-plus-peer-review on infrastructure change, and no drift detection. Changes to the agent-facing surface are manual and unauditable.
findings.recommendation: Define the deployment, datasource, and network exposure as code with peer-reviewed changes and drift detection, starting by externalizing the endpoint and datasource configuration out of the Java source.

findings.title: CI/CD with API Contract Testing
findings.description: There is no CI/CD pipeline. Searched for .github/workflows/, .gitlab-ci.yml, Jenkinsfile, buildspec.yml, and any pipeline definition: none exist. README.md states the build is Ant with 'wsgen/wsimport run by hand' and that 'partner onboarding is a manual SOAP-UI session'; no build file is even committed. Consequently there is no contract test, no WSDL/schema diff, and no breaking-change gate.
findings.gap: API-breaking changes reach production undetected - nothing in the delivery path compares the deployed contract against the previous one, and there is no automated build at all.
findings.recommendation: Commit a reproducible build (Maven/Gradle or a checked-in Ant build), add a pipeline that generates the WSDL from code, and fail the build on a breaking contract diff.

findings.title: Rollback Capability
findings.description: No rollback mechanism exists. Deployment is a hand-built WAR copied to JBoss AS 5.1 (README.md); there is no blue/green or canary configuration, no CodeDeploy or Helm release management, no traffic shifting, and no feature flags anywhere in the repository. Reverting a bad change would mean rebuilding and redeploying the previous WAR by hand on an out-of-support application server, with no automation and no tested procedure.
findings.gap: There is no fast, reliable path back to a known-good state if a deployment breaks the agent-facing operation; recovery time depends entirely on manual effort and the 15-30 minute target is not credibly achievable.
findings.recommendation: Automate the deployment with versioned, retained artifacts and a scripted one-step rollback, and validate the rollback procedure before exposing the endpoint to agents.

findings.title: API Test Coverage
findings.description: There are no tests. The repository contains four files - .gitignore, README.md, one Java source file, and the WSDL - with no test directory, no test framework dependency, no Postman/Newman collection, and no integration tests. README.md states plainly: 'No tests; partner onboarding is a manual SOAP-UI session'.
findings.gap: Nothing validates input handling, response format, error behaviour, or edge cases on the one operation agents would call, so behavioural regressions would surface only in production.
findings.recommendation: Add automated endpoint tests covering valid submission, malformed XML, missing elements, duplicate po_number, and database-failure paths, and run them in CI.

findings.title: Encryption at Rest for Agent-Accessible Data
findings.description: No encryption-at-rest configuration is evidenced. The data store is an on-premises Oracle 11g instance reached over a plain jdbc:oracle:thin connection (line 21) with no TLS parameters in the URL and no wallet or TDE reference; there is no IaC, no kms_key_id, and no database configuration in the repository to establish whether tablespace encryption is enabled. README.md documents the Oracle 11g backend but says nothing about encryption, and does document WS-Security passwords sent in plaintext over plain HTTP, so data is also unprotected in transit.
findings.gap: Encryption at rest for partner order data cannot be demonstrated from the repository, and the connection carrying that data is unencrypted in transit - a breach of the host or the network path would expose everything the agent can write or read.
findings.recommendation: Confirm or enable Oracle TDE for the partner_orders tablespace, enable TLS on the JDBC connection, and move the endpoint to HTTPS so partner data is protected in transit as well as at rest.

findings.title: Asynchronous Operation Support
findings.description: No asynchronous invocation pattern, despite operations far exceeding any synchronous budget: README states the batch 'runs 5-7 hours and sometimes overruns'. Execution is a scheduled CA-7 job (`jcl/PAYRUN.jcl` line 3) with no job-submission API, no status/polling endpoint, and no webhook callback. Completion is signalled only by `NOTIFY=&SYSUID` (line 1) and the appearance of a new GDG generation.
findings.gap: An agent has no way to submit work, obtain a job handle, poll status, or receive a completion callback for a multi-hour operation.
findings.recommendation: Expose a submit/poll/callback trio at the API facade (job id on submit, status endpoint, optional webhook on completion) wrapping the CA-7 job, so agents never hold a synchronous connection against the batch window.

findings.title: Queryable Current State
findings.description: Current state is not queryable. `EMP-FILE` is read `ACCESS MODE IS SEQUENTIAL` from end to end (`src/PAYRUN.cbl` lines 13-17) even though the dataset is INDEXED, and the output is an opaque fixed-width `PAY-RECORD PIC X(120)` (line 29). There is no status field, no state machine, and no query interface — inspecting current payroll state requires reading a flat file or the DB2 tables directly.
findings.gap: An agent cannot inspect employee or pay-run state before acting; it would have to parse a 120-byte fixed-width file or obtain direct database access.
findings.recommendation: Expose read endpoints for employee and pay-run state (including run status and per-period totals) so an agent can read before acting instead of parsing batch output.

findings.title: Graceful Degradation Signaling
findings.description: No degradation signalling. The program's only state variable for control flow is `WS-EOF` (`src/PAYRUN.cbl` line 35); there is no health surface, no freshness or staleness indicator, and no partial-result marker. Critically, README documents that the state tax table lookup 'REMOVED IN 2011, DONE MANUALLY' (`src/PAYRUN.cbl` line 50) and tax tables are 'updated by hand each January' — the system is permanently running in a functionally degraded mode that it does not advertise.
findings.gap: Consumers receive net-pay figures that silently omit state tax and may be based on stale hand-maintained tax tables, with no machine-readable signal that the result is partial.
findings.recommendation: Emit an explicit completeness/freshness indicator with every result (e.g., tax-table effective date, `state_tax_applied: false`) so an agent can detect degraded output and defer to human review.

findings.title: Sandbox/Staging Environment
findings.description: There is no environment definition in the repository — no docker-compose, no environment-specific configuration, no seed or synthetic data generator, and no IaC. Dataset names are hardcoded to production-looking qualifiers (`ACME.PAYROLL.EMPMAST`, `ACME.PAYROLL.PAYOUT`) in `jcl/PAYRUN.jcl` lines 6-8, and README states changes are 'validated in a shared QA region only' with 'No automated tests'.
findings.gap: A shared QA region with no committed configuration and no production-shaped synthetic data is not a safe, reproducible place to exercise agent behaviour, and promotion requires hand-editing hardcoded dataset names.
findings.recommendation: Parameterize dataset qualifiers by environment (symbolic parameters), and stand up an isolated sandbox region seeded with synthetic employee data that matches the production record layout.

findings.title: Input Validation and Schema Enforcement
findings.description: No input validation. `PROCESS-EMP` computes directly from the input record (`COMPUTE WS-GROSS = EMP-RATE * EMP-HOURS`, `src/PAYRUN.cbl` lines 45-47) with no range, sanity, or completeness checks, and `READ-EMP` (lines 57-59) has no `FILE STATUS` or `INVALID KEY` handling. The `PIC` clauses provide implicit truncation only — `WS-GROSS PIC 9(07)V99` will silently truncate an overflowing product rather than reject it, and there is no structured rejection path or error record. No validation library or request validator exists (no API layer at all).
findings.gap: Malformed or out-of-range input (negative/absurd hours, corrupt packed fields, truncated records) is silently computed into a payout rather than rejected with a field-level error.
