findings.recommendation: Add explicit field validation with an ON SIZE ERROR branch and a reject-record path that identifies the failing employee id and field, and enforce schema validation at the future API boundary.

findings.title: Temporal Metadata and Freshness
findings.description: No temporal metadata. `EMP-RECORD` (`src/PAYRUN.cbl` lines 20-27) has no created/updated/effective-date field, and `PAY-RECORD` carries only employee id, name and net pay via the `STRING` concatenation (lines 51-55) — no pay-period date, no run timestamp, no timezone normalization. Freshness is implicit in the GDG generation number. The FICA wage base is a hardcoded literal (`WS-WAGE-BASE ... VALUE 132900.00`, line 34) last updated in 2019 per the file header, with no effective-date field.
findings.gap: An agent cannot determine which pay period a record belongs to, when the underlying data was last updated, or whether the embedded tax constants are current.
findings.recommendation: Add pay-period and last-updated timestamps (UTC) to the record layouts and the output file, and externalize the wage base and tax tables with explicit effective dates.

findings.title: Schema Versioning and API Contracts
findings.description: No schema versioning or contract management. The interchange contract is an undocumented fixed-width layout defined only by `DCB=(RECFM=FB,LRECL=120,BLKSIZE=0)` (`jcl/PAYRUN.jcl` line 12) and the `STRING` statement that builds it (`src/PAYRUN.cbl` lines 51-55); README lists 'Fixed-width file formats with no schema/versioning' as a known issue. There are no copybooks in the repository, no JSON/Avro/Protobuf schema, no migration files, no changelog, and no CI breaking-change detection (no CI configuration exists). The source header warns 'DO NOT RECOMPILE WITHOUT CONTACTING MAINFRAME TEAM'.
findings.gap: Consumers reverse-engineer byte offsets from code. Any field addition or width change silently breaks every downstream parser with no version marker or detection gate.
findings.recommendation: Publish the record layout as a versioned, machine-readable schema (copybook plus a generated JSON Schema), add a version marker to the file, and gate changes with automated breaking-change detection in CI.

findings.title: Distributed Tracing and Structured Logging
findings.description: No tracing and no structured logging. The sole diagnostic output is `SYSOUT DD SYSOUT=*` (`jcl/PAYRUN.jcl` line 13) — unstructured JES spool. `src/PAYRUN.cbl` contains no DISPLAY statements, no correlation or run id, and no counters. Searched for OpenTelemetry, X-Ray, `traceparent` propagation, JSON logging and `request_id`/`correlation_id` fields across all repository files — zero results.
findings.gap: An agent-initiated run cannot be correlated end-to-end (API facade to batch job to FTP hop), and there is no structured record of what the run did, making failures effectively undiagnosable.
findings.recommendation: Generate a run/correlation id at invocation, carry it through the job and the transfer step, and emit structured (JSON) run events including record counts, totals and outcome to a queryable log store.

findings.title: API Test Coverage
findings.description: No automated tests exist. The repository contains four files (`.gitignore`, `README.md`, `jcl/PAYRUN.jcl`, `src/PAYRUN.cbl`) — there is no test directory, no unit-test harness, no integration or contract tests, and no CI configuration to run them. README states plainly: 'No automated tests; changes validated in a shared QA region only'. The source header's 'DO NOT RECOMPILE WITHOUT CONTACTING MAINFRAME TEAM' warning indicates change confidence rests on tribal knowledge.
findings.gap: Payroll calculation logic (gross, FICA, net) has zero regression coverage, so behaviour changes that would mislead an agent — or miscalculate pay — are caught only by manual QA inspection.
findings.recommendation: Add unit tests for the calculation paragraphs against fixed input/expected-output fixtures and a file-level golden-output test for the payout layout, and run both in CI on every change.

findings.title: Encryption at Rest for Agent-Accessible Data
findings.description: No encryption at rest for the payroll data stores. There is no IaC in the repository, so no `kms_key_id`, no customer-managed key, and no DB2/dataset encryption setting is declared anywhere. `ACME.PAYROLL.EMPMAST` and the `ACME.PAYROLL.PAYOUT` generations (`jcl/PAYRUN.jcl` lines 6-12) are allocated with no encryption attribute, and the transferred file lands on the EC2 gateway at `/incoming/payout.dat` (line 20) with no declared volume encryption. These datasets hold SSN and bank account data.
findings.gap: Payroll PII is stored on mainframe datasets and an EC2 gateway filesystem with no evidence of encryption at rest or key management.
findings.recommendation: Enable dataset encryption (z/OS pervasive encryption with a managed key) on EMPMAST and the PAYOUT GDG, enable EBS/KMS encryption on the gateway volume, and declare both as code so the control is auditable.

findings.title: No machine-readable API specification
findings.description: No OpenAPI, Swagger, AsyncAPI, GraphQL, or Smithy artifact exists. The repository's ten files are .gitignore, CONTAINERIZE.md, Dockerfile, Makefile, README.md, pricing.cpp, and four k8s manifests; searches for openapi.*, swagger.*, *.graphql, *.gql, and *.smithy returned nothing, and there is no dependency manifest that could pull in a spec-generation framework. The closest thing to a contract is the prose health-check URL in CONTAINERIZE.md and the probe paths in k8s/deployment.yaml.
findings.gap: Agent tool definitions must be hand-authored from source reading and will drift from the binary's actual behaviour, which is undocumented beyond two query parameters.
findings.recommendation: Author an OpenAPI 3 document for the pricing operation (including the HEALTH sentinel SKU behaviour), commit it next to the source, and validate it in CI against the served responses.

findings.title: No structured error responses; failures return HTTP 200 with a zero price
findings.description: The binary cannot signal failure. lookup_price (pricing.cpp) returns 0.0 both when /etc/pricing/rules.dat cannot be opened and when the SKU is not found, and main() prints the same HTML template with Content-Type: text/html and no status line, so Apache returns 200 in every case. An unknown SKU, a missing rules file, and a successful lookup of a genuinely free item are indistinguishable to the caller. A missing or non-numeric qty silently becomes 1 or 0 via atoi. There is no error code, no error body, and no retryable indicator anywhere in the response.
findings.gap: An agent cannot distinguish success from terminal failure from retriable failure. The most likely agent-visible outcome of a backend fault is a confidently-wrong $0.00 price rather than an error.
findings.recommendation: Return distinct HTTP statuses (404 unknown SKU, 400 invalid qty, 503 rules file unavailable) with a JSON body carrying code, message, and a retryable flag; never represent 'not found' as a zero price.

findings.title: No sandbox or staging environment for agent testing
findings.description: The repository defines exactly one environment. k8s/namespace.yaml declares the single namespace legacy-pricing-cgi, and k8s/deployment.yaml and k8s/configmap.yaml are not parameterized per environment (no Helm chart, no Kustomize overlays, no staging manifests). There is no docker-compose file, no seed-data or synthetic-data script, and no environment-specific IaC. The only test data is the single line 'SAMPLE-SKU|9.99' baked into /etc/pricing/rules.dat by the Dockerfile; CONTAINERIZE.md instructs operators to mount the real production rules file over that path. README.md confirms 'Pricing rules edited in-place on prod; no source of truth'.
findings.gap: There is no production-shaped environment in which to exercise agent behaviour. Agent testing would either run against a one-row sample dataset that cannot validate real pricing logic, or against production rules.
findings.recommendation: Add a staging overlay (Kustomize or Helm values) deploying the same image into a separate namespace, and supply a representative, non-production rules.dat via a ConfigMap generated from a seed script so agents can be exercised against production-shaped data.

findings.title: No input validation at the request boundary; unbounded strcpy on caller-controlled data
findings.description: There is no validation of any kind at the boundary. parse_query (pricing.cpp) copies the entire QUERY_STRING into a fixed 256-byte stack buffer with strcpy and no length check, then copies the attacker-controlled sku= value into a 64-byte caller buffer with a second unchecked strcpy. qty is converted with atoi, which cannot report failure and yields 0 for non-numeric input and undefined behaviour on overflow. lookup_price uses sscanf with an unbounded "%[^|]" conversion into a 64-byte file_sku buffer. The SKU is then reflected into the HTML response unescaped. No validation library, schema, request-size limit, or type-safe parsing exists (there is no dependency manifest and no gateway request validator in k8s/*.yaml). README.md itself records 'No bounds checking on CGI query string parsing' and 'Uses unsafe C string functions (strcpy/sprintf) - buffer overflow risk'.
findings.gap: Malformed inputs are not rejected — they are either silently coerced (qty) or overflow fixed buffers (sku, query string). An agent constructing a long or odd SKU crashes or corrupts the process instead of receiving a field-level rejection, and the unescaped reflection is an XSS sink for any browser-rendered consumer.
findings.recommendation: Validate before use: bound the query string length, replace both strcpy calls with length-checked copies (snprintf/strncpy with explicit truncation handling), parse qty with strtol and reject out-of-range values, bound the sscanf conversion ('%63[^|]'), HTML-escape the reflected SKU, and return a structured 400 naming the offending field.

findings.title: No schema versioning, API versioning, or breaking-change detection
findings.description: Neither the interface nor the data file is versioned. The endpoint path is /cgi-bin/pricing.cgi with no /v1/ segment and no Accept-Version handling (pricing.cpp reads only QUERY_STRING). The data contract is the implicit 'SKU|PRICE' pipe-delimited layout parsed inline by sscanf in lookup_price, with no schema file, no header row, and no version marker; CONTAINERIZE.md documents it only as prose. There are no JSON Schema, Avro, or Protobuf definitions, no migration files, no CHANGELOG, no deprecation notices, and no breaking-change tooling — there is no CI configuration at all (no .github/workflows, .gitlab-ci.yml, Jenkinsfile, or buildspec.yml in the repository).
findings.gap: Any change to the query parameters, the HTML output structure, or the rules.dat column layout silently breaks agent tool bindings, and nothing in the build detects it. README.md notes the rules file has 'no source of truth', so the data contract can change outside version control entirely.
findings.recommendation: Introduce a versioned route (/v1/prices) for the JSON interface recommended in API-Q1, commit a schema for the rules file format, and add an OpenAPI diff / contract test step to CI that fails on breaking changes.

findings.title: No distributed tracing and no structured logging
findings.description: The process emits no logs and no telemetry. pricing.cpp writes only the HTML response to stdout (printf) and never logs to stderr, a file, or a logging library; there is no OpenTelemetry or X-Ray instrumentation and no traceparent/correlation-id handling (the binary reads only the QUERY_STRING environment variable, so inbound trace headers are discarded). The only observability surface is Apache's default access/error logs, whose directory is chowned to appuser in the Dockerfile; those are plain-text Common Log Format, not JSON, and carry no request or correlation identifier. No sidecar, collector, or agent is defined in k8s/deployment.yaml.
findings.gap: An agent-initiated failure cannot be reconstructed. There is no per-request identifier linking the agent's call to anything inside the service, no structured fields to query, and no trace context propagation.
findings.recommendation: Have the ingress inject and log a correlation identifier, configure Apache to emit JSON-formatted access logs including that identifier and the request duration, and ship them to CloudWatch Logs; propagate traceparent through the wrapper service introduced for API-Q1.

findings.title: No alerting on error rates or latency
findings.description: No alerting exists. The repository contains no CloudWatch alarm definitions, no anomaly-detection configuration, no PagerDuty/OpsGenie integration, and no SLO definitions — there is no IaC and no monitoring manifest (k8s/ holds only namespace, configmap, deployment, and service). The sole health signalling is liveness/readiness probes in k8s/deployment.yaml hitting /cgi-bin/pricing.cgi?sku=HEALTH&qty=1, plus the container HEALTHCHECK in the Dockerfile. Those restart or deregister a pod but notify no one, and because the binary returns HTTP 200 even when the rules file is missing (see API-Q3), the probes pass while the service returns $0.00 prices.
findings.gap: Degradation that matters to an agent — rising latency under machine-speed load, or a missing rules file producing zero prices — triggers no alert, and the only configured health check cannot detect it.
findings.recommendation: Create CloudWatch alarms on ALB/gateway 5xx rate, 4xx rate, and p99 latency for the agent-facing route, and add a semantic health check that asserts a known SKU returns its expected non-zero price, alarming when it does not.

findings.title: Agent-facing integration surface is not defined as code, reviewed, or drift-monitored
findings.description: Only the workload is declared as code; the integration surface is not. k8s/deployment.yaml, service.yaml, configmap.yaml, and namespace.yaml define the pods and a ClusterIP Service, but the ingress, TLS, IAM roles, network policy, and WAF that would expose this service to an agent exist nowhere — the ALB Ingress is only a commented-out YAML example inside k8s/service.yaml, and CONTAINERIZE.md assigns its creation to the operator as a manual action. There is no Terraform, CloudFormation, CDK, or Helm chart in the repository. There is no CI configuration (no .github/workflows, .gitlab-ci.yml, Jenkinsfile, or buildspec.yml), so no automated plan review or required approval gates the manifests, and no AWS Config rules or drift detection are configured. Deployment is manual: CONTAINERIZE.md instructs an operator to hand-edit the image reference and run 'kubectl apply -f k8s/', and Makefile's legacy install target still scps the binary to deploy@pricing01. k8s/deployment.yaml also pins image: legacy-pricing-cgi:latest, a mutable tag, so the deployed artifact is not identifiable from the manifest.
findings.gap: Of the three required controls — IaC definition, enforced change review, drift detection — only partial IaC is present. The exact surface an agent would call (ingress, auth, network policy) is created by hand and is unreviewed, unversioned, and unmonitored.
findings.recommendation: Express the full agent-facing surface (Ingress/ALB, TLS, IAM, NetworkPolicy, WAF) as IaC in this repository, require PR review on that directory, replace the :latest tag with an immutable digest, and enable drift detection on the deployed stack.

findings.title: No CI/CD pipeline and no API contract testing
findings.description: There is no pipeline at all. The repository contains no .github/workflows directory, no .gitlab-ci.yml, no Jenkinsfile, and no buildspec.yml; the build is the hand-written Makefile ('make all' compiling pricing.cpp with g++), and the Dockerfile invokes that same make in its builder stage. Release is manual: CONTAINERIZE.md documents operator-run docker build / docker push / kubectl apply commands, and Makefile's install target scps the binary to deploy@pricing01. Consequently there is no contract test, no OpenAPI validation (no spec exists — see API-Q2), and no breaking-change detection step anywhere.
findings.gap: Nothing between a source change and production verifies that the agent-facing contract still holds. A change to parse_query's parameter names or to the HTML output structure ships undetected.
findings.recommendation: Add a CI pipeline that builds the image, runs the container, and asserts the agent-facing contract (known SKU returns the expected JSON/price, unknown SKU returns an error status), failing the build on contract drift.

findings.title: Rollback depends on a mutable image tag and manual kubectl steps
findings.description: The deployment is a standard Kubernetes Deployment (k8s/deployment.yaml, replicas: 2), so 'kubectl rollout undo' is technically available, but the manifest pins image: legacy-pricing-cgi:latest — a mutable tag. If a bad build is pushed over :latest, rolling back the Deployment restores the same tag and therefore the same broken image, so the rollback is not reliably to a known-good state. There is no blue/green or canary configuration, no traffic-shifting at an ingress (the Ingress itself is only a comment in k8s/service.yaml), no CodeDeploy rollback trigger, and no feature flags. Because there is no CI/CD (ENG-Q2), rollback is an unautomated, manual operation performed by whoever ran CONTAINERIZE.md's kubectl apply.
findings.gap: No automated, artifact-pinned rollback path. Recovery time depends on an operator being available and on whether a distinct previous image tag happens to still exist.
findings.recommendation: Deploy immutable image digests (or semver tags) instead of :latest, automate rollback in the pipeline, and add progressive delivery with automatic rollback on error-rate regression at the ingress.

findings.title: Machine-Readable API Specification
findings.description: No machine-readable specification of any kind is present. Searched for `openapi.yaml/json`, `swagger.yaml/json`, AsyncAPI documents, `*.graphql`, `*.gql`, `*.smithy`, and `*.proto` across the repository (4 files total: .gitignore, README.md, app/controllers/orders_controller.rb, config/payment.yml), and for spec-generating gems — no dependency manifest exists at all (README states gems are pinned in `environment.rb`, not Bundler).
findings.gap: Agent frameworks cannot auto-generate tool definitions. Every integration would require hand-authored tool schemas reverse-engineered from controller code, which will drift from actual behaviour.
findings.recommendation: Once a JSON API exists (API-Q1), generate an OpenAPI 3 document from route/controller annotations and validate it in CI so the spec cannot drift from the implementation.

findings.title: Structured Error Responses
findings.description: Error handling is view-based, not structured. In `create`, a save failure falls through to `render :action => 'new'` — an HTML page with no error code or machine-readable body. `show` and `index` have no rescue handling: `Order.find(params[:id])` raises `ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound`, which Rails 2.3 renders as a bare 404/500 error page. No error-code constants, no error envelope, and no retryable indicator appear anywhere in the controller.
findings.gap: An agent receiving a 500 HTML page cannot distinguish a retriable failure (gateway timeout in `charge_card`) from a terminal one (validation rejection), so it will either retry a permanently-failing call or abandon a transient one.
findings.recommendation: Define a consistent JSON error envelope (`code`, `message`, `retryable`, `details[]`) and a central exception handler mapping domain and framework exceptions onto it. Return field-level validation detail for `create` rejections.

findings.title: Sandbox/Staging Environment
findings.description: No sandbox or staging environment is defined. `config/payment.yml` sets `mode: live` with a single gateway endpoint and no per-environment variants; there is no `config/environments/` content, no `docker-compose.yml`, no seed or synthetic-data scripts, and no environment-specific IaC in the repository. README describes deployment as Capistrano 2 to a fixed set of EC2 hosts with no non-production tier.
findings.gap: There is no safe place to exercise agent behaviour: any test of the order flow charges a real card against the live gateway. Agent bugs would first surface in production.
findings.recommendation: Stand up a staging environment with a gateway sandbox credential (`mode: test`) and production-shaped seed data, and make environment selection explicit in configuration rather than a single committed live-mode file.

findings.title: Selective Query Support
findings.description: `index` returns an unbounded result set: `SELECT * FROM orders WHERE status = '...' ORDER BY created_at DESC` with no `LIMIT`, no `OFFSET`, no cursor, and no caller-supplied page size. The only filter is a single `status` parameter defaulting to `'pending'`; there is no sort selection and no field selection.
findings.gap: An agent calling `index` retrieves every order in the matching status, which will exhaust LLM context windows and inflate cost as the table grows.
findings.recommendation: Add `limit`/`cursor` pagination with a server-enforced maximum page size, expose explicit filter and sort parameters, and support field selection so agents request only the columns they need.

findings.title: Input Validation and Schema Enforcement
findings.description: There is no input validation at the boundary, and two injection paths are open. `index` interpolates `params[:status]` directly into raw SQL (`"... WHERE status = '#{status}'"`), a SQL injection vector the code comments acknowledge. `create` passes the entire `params[:order]` hash into `Order.new`, and README confirms `attr_accessible` is not set — a mass-assignment vulnerability. No validation library or framework validator is declared (no dependency manifest exists), there is no request size limit, and validation failures surface as an HTML `render :action => 'new'` with no field-level detail.
findings.gap: Malformed or hostile agent-constructed payloads are neither rejected nor reported. Unparameterised interpolation permits SQL injection; unrestricted mass assignment lets a caller set any Order column, including payment and status fields.
findings.recommendation: Replace the interpolated query with a parameterised condition (`Order.where(['status = ?', status])`) and whitelist the status against an allowed set; declare `attr_accessible` (or an explicit permitted-params list) on `Order`; add model validations and return a structured validation error body naming each failing field and constraint.

findings.title: Temporal Metadata and Freshness
findings.description: Partial temporal metadata exists: `index` orders by `created_at DESC`, confirming a creation timestamp column. There is no evidence of an `updated_at` or source-event-time field being exposed, no timezone normalisation (Rails 2.3 defaults are not configured in this repository), no `Cache-Control`, `X-Data-Age`, or `last_refreshed` response headers, and no consistency-level indicator. No NTP configuration is present.
findings.gap: An agent can order results by creation time but cannot tell whether a record it reads is current, stale, or cached, and has no last-modified signal for change detection.
findings.recommendation: Expose `created_at` and `updated_at` as explicit UTC-normalised fields in API responses, and add freshness signalling (`Last-Modified`/`ETag`, or a `data_status`/`consistency_level` envelope field) so agents can reason about currency.

findings.title: Schema Versioning and API Contracts
findings.description: No schema or contract artefacts exist. There are no migration files (no `db/` directory), no JSON Schema, Avro, or Protobuf definitions, no schema registry reference, and no versioning in the interface: `redirect_to :action => 'show'` uses unversioned Rails default routes with no `/v1/` namespace and no `Accept-Version` handling. There is no changelog, no deprecation notice, and no breaking-change detection or consumer-driven contract tests (no CI configuration exists in the repository).
findings.gap: The order schema is only discoverable by reading controller code and querying MySQL, and any change to it would break agent tool bindings silently.
findings.recommendation: Version the API path, commit the schema as migrations plus a published JSON Schema/OpenAPI component set, and add breaking-change detection (OpenAPI diff or Pact contract tests) to CI once a pipeline exists (ENG-Q2).

findings.title: Distributed Tracing and Structured Logging
findings.description: Neither tracing nor structured logging is present. There is no OpenTelemetry SDK, X-Ray instrumentation, or `traceparent` propagation (no dependency manifest declares any instrumentation gem), and no logging statements at all in `OrdersController` — the only logs are Rails 2.3's default unstructured plaintext request lines. No `request_id` or `correlation_id` is generated, accepted from the caller, or propagated into the outbound gateway call in `charge_card`.
findings.gap: An agent-initiated failure — for example a `create` that saved an order but failed the charge — cannot be reconstructed: there is no correlation ID linking the inbound request, the database write, and the gateway call.
findings.recommendation: Accept and propagate a `traceparent`/correlation ID at the edge, emit JSON logs including that ID plus the authenticated principal, and instrument the gateway call as a child span so agent requests are traceable end to end.

findings.title: Alerting on Error Rates and Latency
findings.description: No alerting is configured. The repository contains no IaC, hence no CloudWatch alarms on error rate or latency, no anomaly detection, no composite alarms, and no SLO definitions; there is no PagerDuty/OpsGenie integration and no health-check endpoint in the controller. README's deployment section (Capistrano 2 to fixed EC2 hosts) describes no monitoring tier.
findings.gap: Degradation of the order endpoints — including a slow payment gateway (STATE-Q4) — would be detected only by user reports, after agents have already begun cascading retries.
findings.recommendation: Define error-rate and p99-latency alarms on the order endpoints and on gateway call failures, with thresholds tied to an SLO, and route them to an on-call channel before enabling agent traffic.

findings.title: Infrastructure Governance for Agent-Facing Surface
findings.description: None of the agent-facing infrastructure is defined as code. Searched for Terraform (`*.tf`, `*.tfvars`), CloudFormation (`template.yaml/json`, `*.cfn.*`), CDK (`cdk.json`), Helm (`Chart.yaml`, `values.yaml`), Kustomize, Ansible playbooks, and Kubernetes manifests — the repository contains only 4 files and none are IaC. README confirms a fixed set of hand-managed EC2 hosts with Apache and Mongrel configured outside the repository, no API gateway, and no HTTPS termination in the app tier. There is consequently no plan review on infrastructure change and no drift detection (no AWS Config rules).
findings.gap: All three required controls are absent: the integration surface (hosts, networking, TLS, credentials) is defined only by manual host state, so changes are unreviewable and drift is undetectable on the exact surface agents would call.
findings.recommendation: Codify the agent-facing surface — gateway/load balancer, TLS termination, IAM roles, secrets, security groups — in Terraform or CDK, require PR review with automated plan output on changes, and enable drift detection.

findings.title: CI/CD with API Contract Testing
findings.description: There is no CI/CD pipeline. Searched for `.github/workflows/`, `.gitlab-ci.yml`, `Jenkinsfile`, `buildspec.yml`, `appspec.yml`, and pipeline definitions in IaC — none exist in the repository. Deployment is Capistrano 2 pushing to fixed EC2 hosts (README), with no build, test, or contract-verification stage, and no OpenAPI spec or schema-comparison step to verify against.
findings.gap: API-breaking changes cannot be detected before production. Nothing in the delivery path would catch a change that invalidates an agent's tool definition.
findings.recommendation: Introduce a pipeline that runs the test suite and, once an OpenAPI document exists (API-Q2), validates it and runs breaking-change detection plus consumer-driven contract tests against the agent-facing endpoints.

findings.title: Rollback Capability
findings.description: Rollback relies on an unautomated legacy deploy path. README states deployment is Capistrano 2 to a fixed set of EC2 hosts; Capistrano's release-symlink rollback is not configured or evidenced in this repository (no `config/deploy.rb`, no `Capfile`). There is no blue/green or canary configuration, no CodeDeploy rollback trigger, no traffic shifting at a load balancer or gateway, and no feature flags. Gem pinning is in `environment.rb` rather than Bundler and README notes some gems are no longer fetchable, so rebuilding a prior release is not reliably reproducible.
findings.gap: There is no verified, time-bounded path back to a known-good state if a deployment breaks agent-facing behaviour, and dependency unavailability can block a rebuild entirely.
findings.recommendation: Establish an automated rollback: immutable artefacts with pinned, vendored dependencies, a documented and rehearsed one-step revert (or blue/green with traffic shifting), and a measured recovery time against the 15–30 minute target.

findings.title: API Test Coverage
findings.description: There is effectively no test coverage. README states the tests are "a stale Test::Unit suite that no longer runs", and no test files are present in the repository (no `test/` or `spec/` directory in the 4-file inventory). There are no API-level tests exercising `index`, `create`, or `show`, no error-response or edge-case tests, no Postman/Newman collections, no contract tests, and no CI to execute them.
findings.gap: Behaviour of the endpoints an agent would consume is unverified. Changes to request handling, response shape, or error semantics would go undetected.
findings.recommendation: Restore a running test suite and add request-level tests for each agent-facing endpoint covering valid input, malformed input, authorization failure, and gateway-failure paths, executed on every change in CI.

findings.title: Encryption at Rest for Agent-Accessible Data
findings.description: No encryption-at-rest configuration exists for the order data store. The repository contains no IaC, so there is no `kms_key_id` on RDS/EBS/S3, no customer-managed KMS key, and no encryption setting of any kind. README describes MySQL 5.1 on a self-managed EC2 instance — a release predating transparent data encryption in MySQL — and card data is stored in that database (`card_number`, `card_exp` per `charge_card`). Searched README and the full file inventory for KMS, encryption, and TLS configuration; README separately notes no HTTPS termination in the app tier.
findings.gap: Cardholder data that agents would reach through this service appears to sit unencrypted on EC2 storage, so a disk or snapshot compromise exposes everything in the agent's reach.
findings.recommendation: Migrate the store to a managed engine with KMS encryption at rest using a customer-managed key (or enable volume-level encryption as an interim step), tokenise stored card data so the plaintext PAN is never persisted, and enforce TLS in transit.

findings.title: Machine-Readable API Specification
findings.description: No OpenAPI, Swagger, GraphQL, AsyncAPI, or Smithy artifact exists. Searched all repository files by name pattern and inspected the only source file; the surface is an .aspx postback page.
findings.gap: No machine-readable contract from which agent tool definitions can be generated.
findings.recommendation: Generate an OpenAPI document once an HTTP API exists (API-Q1).

findings.title: Structured Error Responses
findings.description: No Try/Catch surrounds the SQL calls, and customErrors mode=Off returns an HTML stack-trace page rather than a machine-readable error body with a code and retryability indicator.
findings.gap: Callers cannot distinguish retriable from terminal failures.
findings.recommendation: Return a JSON error envelope with code, message, and a retryable flag.

findings.title: Queryable Current State
findings.description: Current state is readable only as rendered HTML: BindGrid() selects entry_date, hours, project for the session employee and binds it to a grid. No programmatic read endpoint exists.
findings.gap: State inspection requires scraping a ViewState-heavy HTML page.
findings.recommendation: Promote the BindGrid() query to a documented read-only API.

findings.title: Sandbox/Staging Environment
findings.description: Only one configuration exists, pointing at the single production host 10.0.6.15. There is no staging or sandbox config, no docker-compose, and no seed or synthetic data script.
findings.gap: No non-production environment in which to test agent behaviour.
findings.recommendation: Create environment-specific configuration and a seeded staging database.

findings.title: Selective Query Support
findings.description: BindGrid() issues an unbounded SELECT ... ORDER BY entry_date DESC with no TOP, no paging, and no filter parameters.
findings.gap: No pagination, filtering, or result-size cap.
findings.recommendation: Add limit/offset and date-range filters to the read path.

findings.title: Input Validation and Schema Enforcement
findings.description: No validation exists. txtDate.Text, txtHours.Text, txtProject.Text, and Session("EmployeeId") are concatenated directly into SQL strings on both the read and write paths; hours is interpolated unquoted and is neither type- nor range-checked. Both statements are SQL-injectable, as the file's own comment acknowledges.
findings.gap: No schema enforcement or field-level rejection, plus SQL injection exposure on read and write.
findings.recommendation: Replace string-concatenated SQL with parameterized SqlParameter commands and add typed range validation returning field-level errors.

findings.title: Temporal Metadata and Freshness
findings.description: The columns written are employee_id, entry_date, hours, project - entry_date is user-supplied business data. There is no created_at/updated_at, no UTC normalization, and no cache or freshness header.
findings.gap: No record-provenance timestamps and no freshness signalling.
findings.recommendation: Add UTC audit timestamps to the entity and expose them in responses.

findings.title: Schema Versioning and API Contracts
findings.description: No migration files, schema registry, JSON Schema, or versioned path exists; the timesheets table shape is implied only by inline SQL. No changelog or deprecation notice, and with no CI there is no breaking-change detection.
findings.gap: Schema and contract are undocumented and unversioned; changes are silent.
findings.recommendation: Introduce migration-managed schema and a versioned API contract.

findings.title: Distributed Tracing and Structured Logging
findings.description: No tracing or logging instrumentation: the source imports only System, System.Data, System.Data.SqlClient, and System.Configuration, and web.config declares no trace, healthMonitoring, or log provider. No correlation ID is generated or propagated.
findings.gap: Requests cannot be correlated or reconstructed after failure.
findings.recommendation: Add structured logging with a per-request correlation ID, then trace-context propagation.

findings.title: Alerting on Error Rates and Latency
findings.description: No alarm, monitor, or alerting integration exists in the repository - there is no IaC, no monitoring configuration in web.config, and no monitoring dependency.
findings.gap: Degradation is detected only by user report.
findings.recommendation: Define error-rate and latency thresholds with alert routing.

findings.title: Infrastructure Governance for Agent-Facing Surface
findings.description: No IaC of any kind exists (no Terraform, CloudFormation, CDK, Helm, or Ansible files). README.md states deployment is a manual Visual Studio 2005 publish to a network share onto a single IIS 6 / Windows Server 2003 host. No drift detection and no reviewed change path.
findings.gap: The integration surface is configured manually and is unreproducible.
findings.recommendation: Define the hosting, network, and identity surface as code under peer review.

findings.title: CI/CD with API Contract Testing
findings.description: No pipeline definitions exist (no .github/workflows, .gitlab-ci.yml, Jenkinsfile, or buildspec.yml); README.md confirms there is no build pipeline. Contract testing is therefore impossible.
findings.gap: Breaking changes reach production undetected.
findings.recommendation: Establish a build pipeline, then add API contract tests.

findings.title: Rollback Capability
findings.description: Deployment is a manual file-copy publish to a network share. There is no blue/green configuration, versioned artifact, feature flag, or traffic-shifting layer.
findings.gap: Rollback requires re-publishing from a developer workstation, with unbounded recovery time.
findings.recommendation: Produce versioned deployment artifacts with an automated rollback step.

findings.title: API Test Coverage
findings.description: No test files, test project, or test framework reference exists in the repository; the only code file is the page code-behind.
findings.gap: No automated verification of input handling, output shape, or error behaviour.
findings.recommendation: Add tests against the extracted service layer covering validation and error cases.

findings.title: Encryption at Rest for Agent-Accessible Data
findings.description: The connection string specifies no encryption options and the store is SQL Server 2005 on Windows Server 2003. No KMS or key-management configuration exists. requireSSL=false additionally leaves the forms-auth cookie unencrypted in transit.
findings.gap: No encryption at rest for employee timesheet data.
findings.recommendation: Migrate to a supported database engine with managed encryption keys.

findings.title: Structured Error Responses
findings.description: The only application-authored error is `throw new Error(`forbidden: requires scope ${scope}`)` in requireScope (src/resolvers/catalog.ts). A bare Error surfaces through Apollo Server 4 as extensions.code INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR — the same code an unexpected crash produces — so an agent cannot distinguish an authorization denial (terminal) from a transient fault (retriable). No GraphQLError with a domain-specific code is used anywhere, there is no retryable flag or category, and DynamoDB SDK errors (throttling, conditional-check failures) propagate unmapped.
findings.gap: No machine-readable error taxonomy and no retriable-vs-terminal signal. The GraphQL envelope is structured but the codes inside it are not.
findings.recommendation: Throw GraphQLError with explicit extensions { code: 'FORBIDDEN' | 'NOT_FOUND' | 'CONFLICT' | 'THROTTLED', retryable: boolean }, and wrap DynamoDB calls to map ProvisionedThroughputExceededException and ConditionalCheckFailedException onto THROTTLED / CONFLICT.

findings.title: Sandbox/Staging Environment
findings.description: The repository contains no second environment. infra/template.yaml takes a single UserPoolId parameter and declares no stage/environment parameter, no environment mappings, and no Conditions. There is no docker-compose.yml, no samconfig.toml with multiple deployment profiles, and no seed-data, fixture, or synthetic-data script anywhere in the tree (the complete file set is README.md, package.json, tsconfig.json, infra/template.yaml, schema/catalog.graphql, src/server.ts, src/resolvers/catalog.ts).
findings.gap: No production-shaped environment in which agent behaviour against the catalog can be exercised before it touches live data.
findings.recommendation: Add an Environment parameter to the template, commit a samconfig.toml with staging and prod profiles, and add a seed script that populates a representative SKU set.

findings.title: Temporal Metadata and Freshness
findings.description: Partial coverage. Product.updatedAt: String! is populated from ctx.now() as new Date().toISOString() in src/server.ts — UTC-normalized and format-consistent. Missing: there is no createdAt or source event time, so an agent cannot tell a brand-new SKU from one edited seconds ago. There is also no freshness or consistency signalling — ctx.db.scan in the products resolver uses DynamoDB's default eventually-consistent read (no ConsistentRead: true), yet the ProductConnection envelope carries only items and nextCursor, with no consistency_level, last_refreshed, Cache-Control, or X-Data-Age anywhere in src/server.ts.
findings.gap: Agents receive possibly-stale eventually-consistent reads with no indication that they are stale, and have no creation timestamp to reason with.
findings.recommendation: Add createdAt: String! to Product (set on first write only) and a consistency: ConsistencyLevel! field to ProductConnection reflecting whether the underlying read was strong or eventual; consider ConsistentRead: true on the by-SKU lookup.

findings.title: Schema Versioning and API Contracts
findings.description: The contract itself is strong: schema/catalog.graphql is schema-first, committed, docstring-annotated on every operation, and introspectable at runtime. The stability machinery is absent: the HTTP API route in infra/template.yaml is a bare /graphql with no /v1/ prefix and no Accept-Version handling in src/server.ts; package.json's "version": "1.2.0" versions the package, not the API; there is no CHANGELOG, @deprecated is unused in the schema, and no CI exists at all (searched .github/workflows/, .gitlab-ci.yml, Jenkinsfile, buildspec.yml) so there is no graphql-inspector/buf-breaking-class detection and no consumer-driven contract tests.
findings.gap: A breaking schema edit (removing a field, tightening nullability) would merge undetected and silently break agent tool bindings.
findings.recommendation: Add a CI job running graphql-inspector diff against the previously deployed schema, adopt @deprecated for field retirement, and publish a CHANGELOG entry per schema change.

findings.title: Distributed Tracing and Structured Logging
findings.description: One of the two required controls is present. infra/template.yaml sets Globals.Function.Tracing: Active, enabling AWS X-Ray on CatalogFunction. The structured-logging half is absent: there is not a single log statement in src/server.ts or src/resolvers/catalog.ts — no logger import, no JSON log emission, no request_id/correlation_id field, and no traceparent or X-Ray header propagation in application code — and package.json declares no logging library (no pino, winston, or @aws-lambda-powertools/logger). README.md claims "structured logs with a request id", which the code does not support.
findings.gap: X-Ray gives request-level timing but no correlated application log lines, so an agent-initiated failure inside a resolver cannot be reconstructed.
findings.recommendation: Add @aws-lambda-powertools/logger (or pino) emitting JSON with the Lambda request id and X-Ray trace id on every resolver entry and error, and correct the README claim once implemented.

findings.title: Alerting on Error Rates and Latency
findings.description: infra/template.yaml declares exactly three resources — ProductsTable, CatalogFunction, CatalogApi — and no AWS::CloudWatch::Alarm of any kind. There are no alarms on Lambda Errors/Throttles/Duration, none on API Gateway 5xx/Latency, no anomaly detectors, no composite alarms, no SNS notification topic, and no PagerDuty/OpsGenie integration anywhere in the repository.
findings.gap: Degradation of the exact API an agent consumes would be invisible until someone looks at a dashboard.
findings.recommendation: Add CloudWatch alarms to the template for Lambda Errors and p99 Duration, API Gateway 5xx rate, and DynamoDB ThrottledRequests, all wired to an SNS topic.

findings.title: Infrastructure Governance for Agent-Facing Surface
findings.description: Sub-check 1 passes decisively: the entire agent-facing surface is IaC — infra/template.yaml (SAM) defines the HTTP API, the Cognito JWT authorizer, the Lambda execution policy (DynamoDBCrudPolicy scoped to ProductsTable), and the table. Sub-check 2 fails: no CI configuration exists anywhere (searched .github/workflows/, .gitlab-ci.yml, Jenkinsfile, buildspec.yml), so no automated sam validate / cfn-lint / change-set plan review runs before an IaC change, and no CODEOWNERS or branch-protection artifact is committed. Sub-check 3 fails: no AWS Config rules, no drift-detection job, no stack policy.
findings.gap: The infrastructure is reproducible but ungoverned — a hand edit in the console or an unreviewed change to the authorizer would be neither caught nor detected afterwards.
findings.recommendation: Add a CI workflow running sam validate --lint and producing a change-set plan for review on every PR touching infra/, add CODEOWNERS on that path, and enable scheduled CloudFormation stack drift detection.

findings.title: CI/CD with API Contract Testing
findings.description: No CI/CD pipeline exists. All four conventional locations were searched and are absent: .github/workflows/, .gitlab-ci.yml, Jenkinsfile, buildspec.yml; the repository's complete file set is README.md, package.json, tsconfig.json, infra/template.yaml, schema/catalog.graphql, src/server.ts, src/resolvers/catalog.ts. package.json defines build (tsc), test (vitest run), and lint (eslint src) scripts, but nothing invokes them automatically, and no contract-testing dependency is declared (no Pact, no graphql-inspector, no OpenAPI diff).
findings.gap: A schema-breaking change reaches production with no gate — exactly the failure mode that silently breaks agent tool bindings.
findings.recommendation: Add a GitHub Actions workflow running tsc, eslint, vitest run, sam validate, and a graphql-inspector diff of schema/catalog.graphql against the deployed schema, failing the build on breaking changes.

findings.title: Rollback Capability
findings.description: Only the CloudFormation default remains. CatalogFunction in infra/template.yaml declares no AutoPublishAlias and no DeploymentPreference, so there is no Lambda alias, no versioned traffic shifting, no CodeDeploy canary or linear deployment, and no alarm-triggered automatic rollback (consistent with OBS-Q2, where no alarms exist to trigger one). CatalogApi has no stage-level canary settings, there are no feature flags in src/, and no AppConfig integration. Rollback today means a manual sam deploy of the prior commit, or CloudFormation's automatic rollback of a failed update — which covers failed deployments, not deployments that succeed and then break agent callers.
findings.gap: A successful-but-breaking deployment has no fast, automated path back to the last known-good state within the 15–30 minute target.
findings.recommendation: Add AutoPublishAlias: live plus DeploymentPreference { Type: Canary10Percent5Minutes, Alarms: [...] } to CatalogFunction, wired to the CloudWatch alarms recommended under OBS-Q2.

findings.title: API Test Coverage
findings.description: The harness is configured but empty. package.json declares vitest ^1.4.0 as a devDependency and a test script (vitest run), yet the repository contains zero test files — no *.test.ts, no *.spec.ts, no test/ or __tests__/ directory anywhere in the tree. tsconfig.json has "include": ["src"] and src/ holds only server.ts and resolvers/catalog.ts. Consequently nothing validates GraphQL input handling, the requireScope denial path, the base64 cursor round-trip in the products resolver, or the upsert-idempotency property that README.md identifies as the service's core safety argument.
findings.gap: No automated test exercises the API contract that agents bind to, and no CI would run them if they existed (ENG-Q2).
findings.recommendation: Add vitest suites covering each operation's success path, the forbidden scope-denial path, cursor encode/decode, and an idempotency assertion that two identical upsertProduct calls yield one item; wire vitest run into the ENG-Q2 pipeline.

findings.title: Machine-Readable API Specification
findings.description: No OpenAPI, AsyncAPI, GraphQL or Smithy file exists in the repo. The only machine-readable surface is _tool_specs() in agent.py, which advertises every tool with an empty inputSchema property set; real parameter names and types live only in the Python signatures in tools.py.
findings.gap: Tool input schemas are empty, so no consumer can generate correct tool bindings.
findings.recommendation: Derive a JSON Schema per tool from pydantic models or type hints and publish an MCP tool manifest alongside the gateway target.

findings.title: Structured Error Responses
findings.description: No tool returns an error envelope. load_claim and policy_lookup index row[0] on the result of fetchone(), so an unknown id raises TypeError, and the dispatch loop in agent.py has no try/except. No error code, message or retryable indicator exists anywhere in src/claims_agent/.
findings.gap: No structured, machine-readable error contract the agent can act on.
findings.recommendation: Return an explicit {code, message, retryable} envelope on every tool failure and classify DB/Bedrock exceptions as terminal vs retriable.

findings.title: Asynchronous Operation Support
findings.description: triage() is fully synchronous - retrieval, a Bedrock converse call, tool dispatch and a memory write all run inline. The tool Lambda has Timeout: 60 and batch mode processes up to 500 claims in one foreground process with no job submission, polling or callback. No queue worker or Step Functions definition exists.
findings.gap: No async job/poll pattern for the long-running batch and multi-tool paths.
findings.recommendation: Add a job-submission plus status-query pattern (SQS or Step Functions) for batch triage runs.

findings.title: Queryable Current State
findings.description: claims.status is written by settlement_writer but no tool reads it - load_claim selects only claim_id, claimant_name, claimant_ssn, policy_no, description and amount. The agent cannot inspect whether a claim is already settled, or read back settled_amount, before acting.
findings.gap: Claim lifecycle status is not exposed on the read path.
findings.recommendation: Include status and settled_amount in the load_claim projection so the agent can perform read-before-write.

findings.title: Graceful Degradation Signaling
findings.description: No health endpoint, degraded-mode flag or freshness metadata exists. retrieval.similar_claims returns a relevance score but no ingestion currency or partial-result indicator, and memory.recall returns [] indistinguishably from memory being unavailable because there is no error handling.
findings.gap: No machine-readable degradation or partial-result signal to the reasoning layer.
findings.recommendation: Return an explicit status/results_returned envelope from retrieval and memory so the agent can defer rather than guess.

findings.title: Sandbox/Staging Environment
findings.description: No staging or sandbox configuration exists - no docker-compose file, no environment-specific parameter or .env files, no seed/synthetic data scripts, and a single CloudFormation stack with fixed resource names (claims-triage, claims-tools) and no environment parameter. README.md's local instructions point at the live model and real claim ids.
findings.gap: No production-shaped environment to exercise agent behaviour safely.
findings.recommendation: Parameterise the templates per environment and stand up a staging stack with a seeded synthetic claims dataset.

findings.title: Selective Query Support
findings.description: payment_history runs SELECT ... FROM payments WHERE policy_no = %s ORDER BY paid_on DESC with no LIMIT, offset or cursor, so a long-lived policy returns its entire ledger into the prompt. Retrieval (top_k=8) and memory recall (topK 25) are bounded, so the gap is confined to the SQL tools, neither of which accepts filter or pagination parameters.
findings.gap: No pagination or result cap on the payment ledger query.
findings.recommendation: Add a bounded limit parameter with a server-side default and maximum to payment_history.

findings.title: Input Validation and Schema Enforcement
findings.description: SQL is correctly parameterised throughout tools.py, but there is no validation layer: requirements.txt declares no pydantic/marshmallow/jsonschema dependency, the advertised tool schemas have no properties, and agent.py splats model-supplied input straight into the callable. settlement_writer accepts any float amount - negative, zero or unbounded - and any string length; tests/test_tools.py notes happy path only, no adversarial input cases.
findings.gap: No boundary validation of model-generated arguments and no structured field-level rejection.
findings.recommendation: Validate each tool's arguments against a per-tool model with explicit constraints and return field-level rejection reasons.

findings.title: Temporal Metadata and Freshness
findings.description: Some temporal fields exist (paid_on, effective_date, released_at = now()) but they are returned as bare str() conversions with no timezone normalisation, load_claim returns no created_at/updated_at, and memory.remember passes eventTimestamp=None to create_event. Retrieval results carry no ingestion or as-of date, so the agent cannot tell how stale a comparable claim is.
findings.gap: Timezone-ambiguous timestamps and no freshness signal on retrieved or remembered data.
findings.recommendation: Normalise returned timestamps to ISO-8601 UTC, populate eventTimestamp, and add record created_at/updated_at to tool projections.

findings.title: Schema Versioning and API Contracts
findings.description: No versioning artefacts exist: no migration directory, no JSON Schema/Avro/Protobuf files, no schema registry, no versioned namespace, no changelog and no breaking-change detection (there is no CI pipeline at all). The DB schema is implied only by inline SQL in tools.py and the MCP tool contract is the empty-property inputSchema in agent.py, so a column rename would break the agent silently.
findings.gap: No versioned, documented contract for either the tool interface or the claims schema.
findings.recommendation: Publish a versioned tool manifest plus committed schema migrations with breaking-change checks.

findings.title: Distributed Tracing and Structured Logging
findings.description: logging.basicConfig emits unstructured plain-text lines with no request_id, session_id or correlation_id. requirements.txt includes no OpenTelemetry or X-Ray SDK, no TracingConfig is set on the tool Lambda, and no traceparent propagation exists between runtime, gateway and tool. docs/security-review-TODO.md confirms an end-to-end session cannot be reconstructed when an adjuster disputes a recommendation.
findings.gap: No trace propagation and no structured, correlatable logs across the three hops.
findings.recommendation: Adopt structured JSON logging keyed by a session correlation id and instrument runtime, gateway and tools with OpenTelemetry.

findings.title: Alerting on Error Rates and Latency
findings.description: infra/ contains no CloudWatch alarm, anomaly detector, SNS alarm topic or SLO definition - the templates declare only the runtime, gateway, target, memory, tool Lambda and a log group. No PagerDuty or OpsGenie integration appears anywhere in the repo.
findings.gap: No alerting on tool error rate, Bedrock throttling or triage latency.
findings.recommendation: Define error-rate and latency alarms for the tool Lambda and agent runtime with an on-call notification target.

findings.title: Infrastructure Governance for Agent-Facing Surface
findings.description: The gateway, IAM roles, memory and log group are all defined in CloudFormation, so the IaC sub-check passes. Change review and drift detection do not: there is no CI/CD definition anywhere in the repo, so no automated plan or peer review is enforced on infra/ changes, and no AWS Config rules or drift detection are configured. docs/security-review-TODO.md adds that the deploy role able to change the agent, its guardrails or its model is reachable from CI without MFA.
findings.gap: IaC exists but change review and drift detection do not.
findings.recommendation: Add a pipeline that produces a reviewable change set for infra/, schedule drift detection, and require MFA on the deploy role.

findings.title: CI/CD with API Contract Testing
findings.description: No pipeline definition of any kind was found (searched .github/workflows/, .gitlab-ci.yml, Jenkinsfile, buildspec.yml, appspec.yml), so there is no contract test, spec validation or breaking-change gate on the MCP tool surface. docs/security-review-TODO.md records that releases are promoted on unit tests only, with no safety or tool-correctness evaluation before deploy.
findings.gap: No automated pipeline and no tool-contract or agent-evaluation gate before production.
findings.recommendation: Stand up CI that validates the tool manifest against the implementation, runs the tests, and blocks breaking changes.

findings.title: Rollback Capability
findings.description: ClaimsAgentRuntime points at the mutable tag claims-agent:latest, so the previous known-good image is not addressable - the template contradicts the TODO doc's claim that digest pinning was completed, and IaC is ground truth. There is no blue/green config, canary or traffic-shifting setting, CodeDeploy configuration, Lambda alias/version, or feature flag to disable a bad tool.
findings.gap: No deterministic, fast rollback path for the agent-facing surface.
findings.recommendation: Replace the latest tag with an immutable digest parameter and add alias-based deployment so rollback is a parameter change.

findings.title: API Test Coverage
findings.description: tests/test_tools.py contains two mocked unit tests and states happy path only, no adversarial input cases yet. There are no tests for load_claim, payment_history, the agent dispatch loop, retrieval or memory; no error-path, malformed-input or idempotency tests; and no test runner wired into CI.
findings.gap: Agent-facing tool behaviour is largely untested, including every error and edge case.
findings.recommendation: Extend coverage to all four tools plus the dispatch loop, including malformed-argument cases, and run it in CI.

findings.title: Encryption at Rest for Agent-Accessible Data
findings.description: No KmsKeyId, KmsMasterKeyId or EncryptionConfiguration appears in either template. ClaimsTranscriptLogs - which holds prompts containing SSNs for 3653 days - has no KMS key, ClaimsMemory specifies no customer-managed key, and the Postgres claims database is not defined in this repository, so its encryption posture is unverifiable here.
findings.gap: No customer-managed encryption on the log group or memory store; data-store encryption unverifiable.
findings.recommendation: Attach a CMK to the transcript log group and memory resource and bring the claims database under IaC so its encryption is reviewable.

findings.title: Machine-Readable API Specification
findings.description: openapi/orders.yaml is present (OpenAPI 3.0.3) and its info.version 2.1.0 matches package.json, so it is current with respect to the route set - all five routes in src/routes.ts are described, with the bearerAuth security scheme. However the spec carries no schemas: every response is a bare `{ description: ... }` with no content or schema, no requestBody is declared for createOrder or refundOrder (so the refund `amount` field an agent must send is undocumented), and components contains only securitySchemes. The spec is hand-maintained - nothing in the repo generates or validates it against the implementation.
findings.gap: No request or response schemas, so an agent tool generated from this spec would know the operations and paths but not the payload shape or the returned fields. Nothing prevents the hand-written spec from drifting from src/routes.ts.
findings.recommendation: Add requestBody and response content schemas for all five operations (reusing the Order type from src/services/order-service.ts), register Fastify JSON schemas on each route and generate the spec from them with @fastify/swagger so it cannot drift, and validate the generated spec in CI.

findings.title: Structured Error Responses
findings.description: Error bodies are structured but incomplete. src/auth.ts returns `{ code: 'unauthorized', message: ... }` on 401 and `{ code: 'forbidden', message: ... }` on 403, and src/routes.ts returns `{ code: 'not_found', message: 'order not found' }` on 404 - a consistent code/message shape. There is no retryable flag or error category on any response, no Retry-After on any path, and no error handler registered for unhandled exceptions, so failures inside OrderService (a pg error or a WarehouseClient rejection) surface as Fastify's default 500 with no code field at all.
findings.gap: No machine-readable retriable-vs-terminal signal, and the 500 path - exactly the class of failure an agent must decide whether to retry - returns no structured body. An agent cannot distinguish a transient downstream timeout from a permanent failure.
findings.recommendation: Add a Fastify setErrorHandler that maps internal failures to a consistent envelope `{ code, message, retryable, details }`, set retryable=true with Retry-After for dependency timeouts and 429/503, and document the error codes in openapi/orders.yaml.

findings.title: Graceful Degradation Signaling
findings.description: The service exposes no degradation signal. There is no health endpoint at all in src/routes.ts (the ALB/ECS service in infra/ecs.yaml has no health-check path configured either), no X-Degraded or X-Data-Freshness header, no Cache-Control or response-envelope freshness field, no fallback response path, and no Retry-After. Responses are returned as bare entities (`return order`) with no envelope in which a degradation state could be carried.
findings.gap: When the payment/warehouse dependency or the database is impaired, callers receive either a success or an unstructured 500 - there is no machine-readable indicator that a response is stale, partial or served in a degraded mode, so an agent treats every 2xx as authoritative.
findings.recommendation: Add a /health endpoint returning granular states (healthy / degraded / read-only) with per-dependency detail, wire it to the ECS/ALB health check, and return a response envelope field or X-Degraded header whenever the service is operating with a failed dependency. Emit Retry-After on 503.

findings.title: Sandbox/Staging Environment
findings.description: No sandbox or staging environment is defined. infra/ecs.yaml is a single environment-agnostic CloudFormation template with no environment parameter, no per-environment parameter files and no second stack; there is no docker-compose.yml for local execution, no seed-data or fixture script, no migrations directory (package.json declares a `migrate` script via node-pg-migrate but no migration files exist), and no .env.example. The only environment switch in the repo is NODE_ENV=production in the Dockerfile.
findings.gap: There is no environment with production-equivalent data shape in which agent behaviour against the irreversible refund/cancel/delete operations can be exercised safely. The first execution of an agent against these endpoints would be against live data.
findings.recommendation: Parameterize infra/ecs.yaml with an Environment parameter and deploy a staging stack with its own RDS instance, add the node-pg-migrate migration files plus a synthetic seed-data script, and provide a docker-compose.yml with PostgreSQL and a stubbed WarehouseClient for local and CI agent testing.

findings.title: Input Validation and Schema Enforcement
findings.description: There is no input validation at the API boundary. src/routes.ts registers no Fastify JSON schema on any route and casts request payloads unchecked - `req.body as Record<string, unknown>` for createOrder and `req.body as { amount: number }` for refundOrder - so an absent, non-numeric or negative `amount`, or an order body with arbitrary/missing fields, is accepted and passed straight to the SQL layer. package.json declares no validation library (no zod, joi, yup, ajv-standalone or class-validator), and openapi/orders.yaml declares no request schemas that could drive a validator. Queries are correctly parameterized in src/services/order-service.ts ($1/$2 placeholders), so injection is prevented, but parameterization is not validation. No body-size limit is configured.
findings.gap: A TypeScript cast is a compile-time assertion with no runtime effect: malformed agent payloads are inserted as NULL/undefined columns or forwarded as an invalid refund amount rather than rejected, and no field-level error is returned that an agent could use to self-correct.
findings.recommendation: Attach Fastify JSON schemas (or zod parsing) to every route, validating required fields, types and ranges - in particular a positive integer `amount` bounded by the order total - and return a structured 400 listing field, constraint and message. Set a bodyLimit on the Fastify instance.

findings.title: Temporal Metadata and Freshness
findings.description: The data model carries no temporal metadata. The Order interface in src/services/order-service.ts declares only id, customerId, status and totalCents - no created_at, updated_at or event_time - and create() inserts only customer_id, total_cents and status, so no timestamp is set by the application. No timezone/UTC handling appears anywhere, responses carry no Cache-Control, X-Data-Age or last_refreshed header, and there is no consistency_level field. No migration files exist to confirm whether the table has database-level timestamp defaults.
findings.gap: An agent cannot tell when an order was placed or last modified, nor whether a response reflects the current state - which removes the basis for any time-sensitive decision (for example, whether a refund window has elapsed) and for detecting staleness.
findings.recommendation: Add created_at and updated_at (timestamptz, UTC, with an update trigger) to the orders table and to the Order interface and API responses, and return Cache-Control: no-store on the read path so freshness is unambiguous.

findings.title: Schema Versioning and API Contracts
findings.description: Versioning is partial and unenforced. openapi/orders.yaml declares info.version 2.1.0 matching package.json, which is a real contract version signal, but the paths carry no version prefix (/orders, not /v1/orders), no Accept-Version header is honoured in src/routes.ts, and there is no changelog or deprecation notice. The spec contains no schema definitions to version (components holds only securitySchemes). Crucially there is no breaking-change detection: the repository contains no CI configuration at all (no .github/workflows, .gitlab-ci.yml, Jenkinsfile or buildspec.yml), hence no OpenAPI diff, no Pact contract tests and no schema-registry check. The declared node-pg-migrate migration directory does not exist, so the database schema is likewise unversioned in-repo.
findings.gap: A breaking change to a route or payload can ship with nothing detecting it, and agent tool bindings - which have no version-pinned URL to bind to - would break silently at runtime.
findings.recommendation: Introduce a /v1 path prefix (or honour Accept-Version), add the request/response schemas to the spec, commit the node-pg-migrate migration files, and add an OpenAPI diff gate plus consumer-driven contract tests to a CI pipeline so breaking changes fail the build.

findings.title: Distributed Tracing and Structured Logging
findings.description: The documented observability stack is not implemented. README.md claims 'structured JSON logs (pino) with a request id; CloudWatch metrics', but package.json lists only fastify, jose and pg - pino is absent, as are any OpenTelemetry, AWS X-Ray or aws-sdk packages. No source file configures a logger, and no correlation_id or request_id field is emitted anywhere; src/routes.ts, src/auth.ts and src/services/order-service.ts contain no instrumentation. There is no traceparent or X-Amzn-Trace-Id propagation into the WarehouseClient calls, and infra/ecs.yaml contains no X-Ray sidecar or OTel collector - only the awslogs driver shipping raw stdout to /ecs/orders.
findings.gap: Neither distributed tracing nor correlated structured logging is actually present, so an agent-initiated request that fails cannot be reconstructed: there is no trace linking the API call to the SQL statement and the downstream warehouse/payment call, and no id to correlate log lines for a single request.
findings.recommendation: Add the logger dependency and register it with a request-id serializer (Fastify's requestIdHeader plus pino), propagate the inbound trace header into the WarehouseClient calls, and instrument with the OpenTelemetry Node SDK exporting to X-Ray or an OTel collector sidecar defined in infra/ecs.yaml.

findings.title: Alerting on Error Rates and Latency
findings.description: No alerting is configured. infra/ecs.yaml defines a Cluster, DbSecret, TaskDef, ExecutionRole and Service and nothing else - there is no AWS::CloudWatch::Alarm, no composite alarm, no anomaly detector, no SNS topic and no PagerDuty/OpsGenie integration. There are no error-rate or latency thresholds anywhere in the repository, no SLO definition, and no load balancer or target-group resources on which ALB 5XX/TargetResponseTime alarms could be hung (the ALB referenced in README.md is not defined in this template).
findings.gap: Degradation of the endpoints an agent consumes would go undetected until a human noticed: no alarm fires on rising 5xx rates, elevated latency, or a failing dependency, so an agent could keep retrying against an impaired service indefinitely.
findings.recommendation: Add CloudWatch alarms for ALB 5XX rate, TargetResponseTime p99 and ECS task health, plus an alarm on refund/cancel error counts, routed to an SNS topic and on-call integration. Define them in infra/ecs.yaml alongside the ALB resources so they are version-controlled with the service.

findings.title: Infrastructure Governance for Agent-Facing Surface
findings.description: One of the three required controls is present. The agent-facing surface is partly defined as code: infra/ecs.yaml (CloudFormation) defines the ECS cluster, task definition, execution role and the Secrets Manager secret. However the template omits key integration-surface resources - no ALB, listener or security group, and no RDS instance, despite both being described in README.md - so part of the surface is managed outside IaC. There is no change-review control in the repository (no .github directory, no CODEOWNERS, no branch-protection or PR-template configuration, and no pipeline that runs `cloudformation deploy --no-execute-changeset` for plan review), and no drift detection (no AWS::Config rules, no drift-detection schedule).
findings.gap: Change review and drift detection are both absent, and the ALB/RDS portion of the integration surface is not in the template - so the live configuration an agent depends on can diverge from the repository with nothing detecting it.
findings.recommendation: Bring the ALB, listener, security groups and the RDS instance into infra/ecs.yaml; add CODEOWNERS plus branch protection requiring review on infra changes; and run a change-set plan step in CI with a scheduled CloudFormation drift-detection check reporting to AWS Config.

findings.title: CI/CD with API Contract Testing
findings.description: There is no CI/CD pipeline in the repository. Searched the full tree: no .github/workflows directory, no .gitlab-ci.yml, no Jenkinsfile, no buildspec.yml, no appspec.yml, and no CodePipeline/CodeBuild resources in infra/ecs.yaml. package.json defines build, test, lint and migrate scripts, but nothing invokes them automatically. Consequently there is no OpenAPI spec validation, no schema comparison, no consumer-driven contract test (no Pact dependency) and no breaking-change detection of any kind.
findings.gap: No automated gate exists between a commit and production, so an API-breaking change to src/routes.ts or openapi/orders.yaml reaches the deployed service with nothing testing the agent-facing contract first.
findings.recommendation: Add a pipeline (e.g. GitHub Actions) that runs build, lint and test on every PR, validates openapi/orders.yaml against the implementation, runs an openapi-diff breaking-change check against the previous release, and gates deployment on all four.

findings.title: API Test Coverage
findings.description: No tests exist. package.json declares `"test": "vitest run"` with vitest 1.4.0 in devDependencies, and README.md claims 'Unit + integration tests' and 'a healthy test suite', but a full-tree search found no test files at all - no *.test.ts, *.spec.ts, no test/ or __tests__/ directory. The repository's only TypeScript files are src/auth.ts, src/routes.ts and src/services/order-service.ts. There is also no CI to run tests (see ENG-Q2), no Postman/Newman collection and no API test suite.
findings.gap: The agent-facing API has zero automated coverage: no test asserts the auth role checks in src/auth.ts, the 404 path, the error body shape, or the behaviour of the three irreversible operations. The README's claim of a healthy test suite is contradicted by the repository contents.
findings.recommendation: Add vitest coverage for the API surface: route-level tests for each endpoint covering success, 401/403, 404 and malformed input, unit tests for OrderService with a stubbed WarehouseClient (already injectable via the constructor), and an integration test against a containerized PostgreSQL. Run them in the pipeline from ENG-Q2 with a coverage threshold.

findings.title: Encryption at Rest for Agent-Accessible Data
findings.description: Encryption at rest cannot be confirmed for the data store the agent would reach. README.md states the data lives in PostgreSQL 15 on RDS, but infra/ecs.yaml declares no AWS::RDS::DBInstance or DBCluster at all - only a Secrets Manager secret named orders/db - so there is no StorageEncrypted or KmsKeyId setting under version control, and no customer-managed KMS key anywhere in the repository. The Secrets Manager secret itself relies on the default AWS-managed key (no KmsKeyId property). No S3, DynamoDB or EBS resources are defined.
findings.gap: The encryption posture of the customer-PII database is defined outside the repository and therefore unverifiable and unenforced here. If the instance was created without StorageEncrypted, it cannot be enabled in place.
findings.recommendation: Define the RDS instance in infra/ecs.yaml with StorageEncrypted: true and an explicit customer-managed KmsKeyId, set KmsKeyId on the orders/db secret, and add an AWS Config rule (rds-storage-encrypted) to detect any unencrypted instance.

findings.title: Temporal Metadata and Freshness
findings.description: Temporal metadata is present and well-typed: created_at is required on Charge and Refund with format date-time in openapi/payments.yaml, and _now_iso (src/payments/handlers.py:88-91) emits a UTC Z-suffixed timestamp. Freshness signalling is absent: _response (handlers.py:30-35) sets only Content-Type and X-Correlation-Id — no Cache-Control, no X-Data-Age, no consistency_level field — and _idempotent_put reads via get_item without ConsistentRead, so reads are eventually consistent with no indication to the caller.
findings.gap: No updated_at field on ledger entities and no machine-readable signal of read consistency, so an agent cannot tell whether a charge it just wrote and immediately read back is current.
findings.recommendation: Add updated_at to the Charge and Refund schemas, pass ConsistentRead=True on read-after-write lookups in src/payments/app.py, and return a consistency indicator (Cache-Control: no-store plus a consistency_level field) from _response.

findings.title: Schema Versioning and API Contracts
findings.description: Contracts are documented and versioned: openapi/payments.yaml is OpenAPI 3.1 with info.version 1.4.0 matching pyproject.toml version, the API Gateway stage is v1 (infra/template.yaml:39) and the server URL is /payments/v1, and the spec is the API Gateway DefinitionBody so it is the deployed contract. Breaking-change detection is absent: .github/workflows/ci.yml validates only that the spec is structurally valid (openapi_spec_validator) and runs pytest; there is no OpenAPI diff, no buf-breaking equivalent, no Pact consumer contract test, and no CHANGELOG or deprecation policy file.
findings.gap: A breaking edit to a schema or an operationId passes CI unchallenged, so agent tool bindings generated from this spec can break silently on deploy.
findings.recommendation: Add an OpenAPI diff step to .github/workflows/ci.yml comparing openapi/payments.yaml against the merge-base revision and failing the build on breaking changes, and add a CHANGELOG.md recording contract changes per version.

findings.title: Alerting on Error Rates and Latency
findings.description: RUNBOOK.md documents three alarms with thresholds and actions — payments-5xx at >1% over 5 min paging on-call, payments-idempotency-conflict at >10/min, payments-ddb-throttle on any — and a payments-prod CloudWatch dashboard. None of this exists in code: infra/template.yaml declares no AWS::CloudWatch::Alarm and no AWS::CloudWatch::Dashboard resource, and there is no PagerDuty/OpsGenie or SNS topic wiring in the template.
findings.gap: Alerting is documented intent, not deployed configuration. Treating IaC as ground truth, the alarms the runbook relies on are not reproducible from source and may not exist in the account; a latency alarm is not specified at all.
findings.recommendation: Declare the three runbook alarms as AWS::CloudWatch::Alarm resources in infra/template.yaml with an SNS alarm action, add a p99 latency alarm on the PaymentsApi stage, and reference the resource names from RUNBOOK.md so the two stay in sync.

findings.title: Infrastructure Governance for Agent-Facing Surface
findings.description: Sub-check 1 passes: the whole agent-facing surface is IaC — API Gateway with its authorizer and TLS 1.2 custom domain, the Lambda authorizer, per-function least-privilege DynamoDB policies, the DynamoDB table and the KMS-encrypted receipts bucket are all declared in infra/template.yaml. Sub-check 2 is partial: .github/workflows/ci.yml runs on pull_request so changes are gated by CI, but no CODEOWNERS file, no branch-protection configuration and no 'sam deploy --no-execute-changeset' plan-review step exist in the repository. Sub-check 3 fails: no AWS Config rules, no drift-detection schedule and no CloudFormation drift check in CI.
findings.gap: Peer-review enforcement is not expressed in the repository and drift detection is absent, so a console-side change to the authorizer, an IAM policy or the usage of the custom domain would go unnoticed.
findings.recommendation: Add a CODEOWNERS file covering infra/ and openapi/, add a changeset-plan step to the pull_request job in .github/workflows/ci.yml, and schedule CloudFormation drift detection (or an AWS Config conformance pack) with an alarm on DRIFTED status.

findings.title: CI/CD with API Contract Testing
