findings.description: .github/workflows/ci.yml runs on every push and pull_request with ruff, mypy strict (configured in pyproject.toml), an openapi_spec_validator check on openapi/payments.yaml and pytest. What it does not do is detect API-breaking change: spec validation proves the document is well-formed, not that it stayed compatible, and there is no consumer-driven contract test (no Pact dependency in pyproject.toml) and no schema comparison against the deployed v1 stage.
findings.gap: The pipeline cannot fail a build that removes an operationId, tightens a schema or renames a field — precisely the changes that break generated agent tools.
findings.recommendation: Extend the CI job with a breaking-change gate (openapi-diff or oasdiff against the base revision) and add a contract test that asserts each operationId in openapi/payments.yaml resolves to an implemented handler in src/payments/handlers.py.

findings.title: Rollback Capability
findings.description: RUNBOOK.md documents rollback as redeploying the previous immutable artifact with sam deploy, and states no manual resource edits are permitted, which is a credible manual path. Automated rollback is not configured: infra/template.yaml sets no AutoPublishAlias and no DeploymentPreference on ChargesFunction, RefundsFunction or AuthorizerFunction, so there is no canary or linear traffic shift and no CodeDeploy rollback trigger wired to the alarms; .github/workflows/ci.yml has no deploy job at all, so promotion is operator-driven.
findings.gap: Recovery depends on a human noticing and running sam deploy. A deploy that breaks the agent-facing contract is not automatically reverted on alarm.
findings.recommendation: Add AutoPublishAlias: live plus a DeploymentPreference (Canary10Percent5Minutes) with Alarms referencing the payments-5xx alarm to each function in infra/template.yaml so CodeDeploy rolls back automatically.

findings.title: API Test Coverage
findings.description: tests/test_idempotency.py is the only test module. It covers three valuable agent-facing properties on createCharge — retry with the same key does not double-execute, key reuse with a different body returns 409 idempotency_conflict, and a missing payments:write scope is denied — and pytest runs in CI. Two coverage gaps are concrete: the getCharge and refundCharge operations defined in openapi/payments.yaml have no tests (no 404 NotFound case, no 422 ValidationError case), and all three tests depend on a ledger_stub fixture that is defined nowhere in the repository — there is no tests/conftest.py — so the suite as committed errors on fixture resolution.
findings.gap: Error-path and refund behaviour are untested, and the committed suite cannot actually execute because its central fixture is missing, which means the CI pytest step is not providing the assurance it appears to.
findings.recommendation: Add tests/conftest.py providing the ledger_stub fixture (DynamoDB Local or a boto3 stub as the docstring describes), then extend coverage to refundCharge, getCharge 404 and the 422 validation response so every operationId has at least a success and an error test.

findings.title: Machine-Readable API Specification
findings.description: No HTTP/RPC surface exists (`has_http_rpc_surface = false`): `frmCustomer.frm` is a Win32 form with ADODB data access only. No `openapi.*`, `swagger.*`, `.graphql`, `.gql`, `.smithy`, or AsyncAPI file is present in the repository.
findings.gap: No machine-readable specification — but there is no callable API surface for a spec to describe. Surface-flag calibration applies: 'No HTTP/RPC surface — machine-readable spec is not applicable.'
findings.recommendation: When the API from API-Q1 is introduced, generate an OpenAPI document from the implementation annotations and publish it as the agent tool-binding source.

findings.title: Structured Error Responses
findings.description: No API responses exist to structure. Error handling in `frmCustomer.frm` is `On Error Resume Next` followed by a `MsgBox` dialog ('Could not save (record may be locked). Try again.', lines 28-33) — a human-facing modal with no error code, no category, and no retryable indicator. The error is then cleared (`Err.Clear`).
findings.gap: Failures are swallowed and surfaced only as UI text. Surface-flag calibration applies (no HTTP/RPC surface), so this is recorded as INFO rather than RISK-QUALITY.
findings.recommendation: Replace `On Error Resume Next` with explicit error propagation now, and define a structured error envelope (code, message, retryable) as part of the API introduced in API-Q1.

findings.title: Event Emission for State Changes
findings.description: No event emission exists. State changes are written directly to the Access database by `cn.Execute sql` (frmCustomer.frm line 29) with no notification path. README.md describes downstream propagation as 'a nightly sync job to a SQL Server reporting database' via a scheduled DTS/SSIS package — batch, once per day. No webhooks, SNS/EventBridge/SQS, Kafka, or CDC pipeline is present.
findings.gap: No event or webhook surface; the only change-propagation mechanism is a nightly batch sync, giving downstream consumers up to 24 hours of staleness.
findings.recommendation: If event-reactive agents are a target, emit domain events (e.g. EventBridge) from the service introduced in API-Q1 rather than relying on nightly batch sync.

findings.title: Rate Limiting and Throttling
findings.description: There is no API layer to throttle: `has_http_rpc_surface` is false — `frmCustomer.frm` is a Win32 form whose only data path is a direct ADODB connection (lines 19-21). No API Gateway configuration, WAF rate rule, or rate-limiting middleware exists (no IaC or config files in the repository). The effective limiter today is human click rate on `cmdSave`.
findings.gap: No rate limiting exists, but surface-flag calibration applies: 'System exposes no HTTP/RPC surface — API-layer rate limiting is not applicable.' Request-rate protection would have to be introduced along with the API itself.
findings.recommendation: Define throttling limits (per-principal request quotas) as part of the API introduced in API-Q1, since the underlying Jet data store cannot absorb machine-speed write traffic.

findings.title: Data Quality Awareness
findings.description: No data quality measurement exists for the CRM dataset held in `S:\CRM\sales.mdb`. There are no profiling reports, null-rate or duplicate-detection checks, freshness SLAs, or quality dashboards in the repository. The known-issues list in README.md points the other way: monthly file corruption under concurrent writes and frequent 'record locked' errors, plus the absence of any uniqueness enforcement (API-Q4) which makes duplicate customer rows likely.
findings.gap: Dataset completeness and duplication rates are unmeasured, and documented corruption events make quality degradation likely rather than hypothetical.
findings.recommendation: Profile the Customers table (null rates, duplicate names, orphan rows) and establish a baseline quality metric before an agent reasons over this data.

findings.title: Semantically Meaningful Field Names
findings.description: The field names that do exist are semantically clear: `Customers (Name, CreatedBy, CreatedOn)` in the insert statement (frmCustomer.frm lines 25-27) are readable, unabbreviated, and need no data dictionary. VB6 control and constant naming follows a conventional Hungarian prefix style (`frmCustomer`, `cmdSave`, `txtName`, `cn`, `DB_PATH`) which is interpretable in context. No legacy coded field names (e.g. `CUST_TYP_CD`) appear in the visible schema; however only three columns are visible in source — the remainder of the Access schema is inside the binary .mdb and was not assessable.
findings.gap: The visible schema is agent-friendly. The unassessable remainder of the .mdb schema is the open question, not the naming convention.
findings.recommendation: Export the full Access schema to text and review the remaining column names for legacy abbreviations before building agent tool definitions.

findings.title: Data Catalog / Metadata Layer
findings.description: No data catalog or metadata layer exists. The repository contains no data dictionary, schema documentation, catalog entries, or metadata files — README.md documents runtime architecture only, and the authoritative schema is embedded in the binary `sales.mdb` on the file share (frmCustomer.frm line 7). The nightly DTS/SSIS package that populates the SQL Server reporting database is also not in the repository, so the downstream mapping is undocumented here.
findings.gap: What the CRM dataset contains and what its fields mean is undiscoverable from the repository, so agent tool definitions would have to be reverse-engineered from the .mdb file.
findings.recommendation: Export the Access schema and register the dataset (and its nightly reporting projection) in a catalog or at minimum a checked-in data dictionary.

findings.title: Infrastructure Governance for Agent-Facing Surface
findings.description: There is no infrastructure as code: no Terraform, CloudFormation, CDK, Helm, Kustomize, or Ansible files exist (the repository contains exactly three tracked files — `.gitignore`, `README.md`, `frmCustomer.frm`). Infrastructure is manual by design: README.md records 'Distribution: EXE copied to each laptop by hand', 'No installer', 'File share is a single Windows file server with no failover', and 'compiled on one developer's machine'. Both `has_http_rpc_surface` and `has_auth_surface` are false, so surface-flag calibration applies and this is recorded as INFO.
findings.gap: No IaC definition, no change review on infrastructure, and no drift detection — but there is currently no API gateway, IAM, or network integration surface for agents, which is why this calibrates to INFO rather than RISK-QUALITY.
findings.recommendation: Define the agent-facing surface (gateway, identity, network, secrets) as code with peer-reviewed changes and drift detection at the time that surface is created in API-Q1.

findings.title: CI/CD with API Contract Testing
findings.description: There is no CI/CD pipeline: no `.github/workflows/`, `.gitlab-ci.yml`, `Jenkinsfile`, or `buildspec.yml` exists in the repository. README.md states 'No tests, no build server; compiled on one developer's machine'. `has_http_rpc_surface` is false, so surface-flag calibration applies: there are no APIs to contract-test and this is recorded as INFO.
findings.gap: No automated build, no pipeline, and no breaking-change detection. The absence of any API surface is why this is INFO rather than RISK-QUALITY — but the absence of a build server is itself a key-person dependency.
findings.recommendation: Establish an automated build pipeline and add API contract validation to it once the API from API-Q1 exists.

findings.title: Rollback Capability
findings.description: There is no deployment mechanism to roll back. Deployment is manual file copying — README.md: 'Distribution: EXE copied to each laptop by hand' and 'No installer; deployment is "copy the EXE and the .mdb template"'. There is no blue/green configuration, no canary, no feature flags, and no traffic shifting; recovery from a bad build would require locating and re-copying a prior EXE to every field laptop. `has_http_rpc_surface` is false, so surface-flag calibration applies and this is recorded as INFO.
findings.gap: No fast, reliable rollback path exists; recovery time is bounded by manual redistribution to every laptop. There is no deployed HTTP/RPC surface today, which is why this calibrates to INFO.
findings.recommendation: Introduce a packaged, versioned release with an automated deploy/rollback path as part of moving the agent-facing logic into the service from API-Q1.

findings.title: Idempotent Write Operations
findings.description: No write endpoints exist in the repository. index.cfm performs a single SELECT and download.cfm performs a SELECT plus a read-only file stream (deletefile="no"). The README documents an upload feature ("Uploaded files written to local disk with original filenames"), but no upload handler is present in the repository, so no write path can be assessed here. agent_scope resolved to read-only, so idempotency is informational.
findings.gap: Idempotency cannot be evaluated because no write surface is present. If the documented upload handler is added to this repository later, it will need idempotency keys or a unique business key before any write-enabled agent is pointed at it.
findings.recommendation: When the upload path is brought into this repository or rebuilt, require a client-supplied idempotency key and enforce a unique constraint on (filename, uploaded_by, content hash) so a retried upload cannot create duplicate document rows.

findings.title: Structured Response Format
findings.description: Responses are server-rendered HTML (index.cfm emits an HTML <table> via <cfoutput query="docs">) and raw binary (download.cfm sets Content-Disposition: attachment and <cfcontent type="application/octet-stream">). No JSON or XML serialization appears anywhere; no returnformat="json" declarations exist.
findings.gap: HTML-plus-binary responses are not directly consumable as agent tool output. An agent would need an HTML parser tightly coupled to the current table markup, which breaks on any presentation change.
findings.recommendation: Return JSON for document metadata and keep binary streaming only for the document bytes themselves, with the content type and filename carried in structured metadata rather than inferred from headers.

findings.title: Rate Limit Documentation and Headers
findings.description: No rate limiting or throttling of any kind was found: there is no IaC (no API Gateway usage plan, no WAF rate rule), no reverse-proxy configuration in the repository, and no application-level throttling in index.cfm or download.cfm. No X-RateLimit-* or Retry-After headers are emitted — the only <cfheader> call sets Content-Disposition. The README states the application runs on a single IIS 7 instance.
findings.gap: Limits are neither enforced nor advertised, so an agent cannot self-throttle and has no signal when it is overloading the single instance.
findings.recommendation: When the API surface is introduced, place it behind a gateway that enforces a per-caller usage plan and returns X-RateLimit-Remaining and Retry-After headers, and document the limits alongside the OpenAPI spec.

findings.title: Identity Propagation and Delegation
findings.description: No identity propagation mechanism exists: no JWT parsing, no OAuth token exchange, no on-behalf-of flow and no X-User-Id style header handling. Identity lives only in the ColdFusion session scope (session.userid, session.fullname in index.cfm) and is never carried onward — the sole downstream call is the <cfquery> to the shared docportal datasource, which connects with a single static credential regardless of the user. Severity downgraded to INFO per archetype calibration for data-gateway services.
findings.gap: An agent could not act on behalf of a specific user with that user's bounded permissions; it would either replay the user's session wholesale or connect as the shared datasource identity. Because the detected archetype is a read-only document query layer, this is recorded as an architecture input rather than a safety risk.
findings.recommendation: If an on-behalf-of agent workflow is planned, add token-based identity to the new API surface and distinguish agent-as-self from agent-for-user in both the authorization predicate and the audit record.

findings.title: Blast Radius and Transaction Limits
findings.description: No business-domain limits exist: no per-caller caps on records returned or documents retrieved, no bulk-operation size limit, and no spend threshold. The document listing query in index.cfm has no TOP/row cap, and download.cfm imposes no per-caller retrieval ceiling. agent_scope resolved to read-only, so this is recorded as INFO.
findings.gap: There are no business-impact caps. Under the current read-only scope this limits exposure to mass document retrieval rather than mass mutation, but no ceiling on documents retrieved per caller per session exists.
findings.recommendation: When scope expands to writes, add per-principal business limits (documents retrieved per hour, documents modified or deleted per run) configurable per agent identity and enforced independently of request-rate throttling.

findings.title: Data Quality Awareness
findings.description: A persistent data store exists but no data-quality instrumentation accompanies it. No profiling report, null-rate monitoring, duplicate detection, freshness SLA or quality dashboard was found in the repository. The documents table has no constraint evidence available here, and because download.cfm resolves files by concatenating doc.filename onto a fixed directory, a row whose filename is stale or whose file is missing from disk fails only at stream time.
findings.gap: There is no measure of completeness or correctness for the document corpus, and no detection of rows whose underlying file is missing — an agent cannot distinguish a genuinely absent document from a broken reference.
findings.recommendation: Profile dbo.documents for null and duplicate rates on title, category and filename, and add a reconciliation job that reports rows whose filename does not resolve to a file on disk.

findings.title: Semantically Meaningful Field Names
findings.description: The exposed field names are readable and self-describing: doc_id, title, category, uploaded_by, uploaded_on and filename (index.cfm lines 23-27, download.cfm line 4). They use full words in snake_case rather than legacy abbreviation codes, so no data dictionary is needed to interpret them. The one ambiguity is category, whose permitted values are not enumerated anywhere in the repository, and uploaded_by, whose type (user id versus display name) is not declared.
findings.gap: Field naming is adequate for LLM reasoning. What is missing is the value domain: the set of valid category values and the identity format of uploaded_by are undocumented.
findings.recommendation: Document the permitted category values and the identity format of uploaded_by as part of the schema description, so an agent can construct valid category filters without sampling the data.

findings.title: Data Catalog / Metadata Layer
findings.description: No catalog or metadata layer exists. No Glue Data Catalog, DataHub, Collibra or Alation reference, no data dictionary file and no schema documentation were found. The only description of what the system holds is the prose in README.md ("Legacy intranet portal for sharing policy documents and forms"); the dbo.documents column set must be inferred from the SELECT lists in index.cfm and download.cfm.
findings.gap: There is no discoverable description of the document corpus or its schema, so teams building agent tools against this system must reverse-engineer the data model from the two CFML pages.
findings.recommendation: Publish a schema description for dbo.documents and the document store — column meanings, category value domain and ownership — in a catalog or at minimum a versioned schema document in the repository.

findings.title: Idempotent Write Operations
findings.description: No write endpoints exist in the repository. Both views in tickets/views.py execute `SELECT` statements only; there are no POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE handlers, no form processing, and no idempotency-key handling. Idempotency is therefore informational for the current read-only surface.
findings.gap: No idempotency mechanism exists, so any future write endpoint (ticket create/update, which the ticketing domain clearly requires) would start without retry safety.
findings.recommendation: When write endpoints are added, require an `Idempotency-Key` header persisted with a unique constraint, and enforce unique business keys at the PostgreSQL layer.

findings.title: Structured Response Format
findings.description:
The response format is HTML, not structured data. `ticket_list` renders `tickets/list.html`; `ticket_search` concatenates `
  • #%d %s
    • ` fragments into an HTML string. No JSON serialization, no content-type negotiation, and no protobuf/XML marshaling were found.
findings.gap: LLM-based agents would need to parse presentation HTML, which breaks whenever the template or markup changes.
findings.recommendation: Return `application/json` with stable field names from the new API layer; keep HTML strictly for the browser UI.

findings.title: Rate Limit Documentation and Headers
findings.description: No rate limiting or rate-limit signaling exists. Searched helpdesk/settings.py MIDDLEWARE_CLASSES (CommonMiddleware, SessionMiddleware, AuthenticationMiddleware only) and the full view module for throttling middleware or `X-RateLimit-*`/`Retry-After` headers; none present. README.md describes Apache 2.2 + mod_wsgi on a single EC2 instance with no gateway or WAF in front.
findings.gap: Agents cannot self-throttle because no limits are documented or advertised in responses.
findings.recommendation: Document a request budget for agent callers and emit `X-RateLimit-Remaining` and `Retry-After` from the throttling layer added for STATE-Q5.

findings.title: Identity Propagation and Delegation
findings.description: No identity propagation exists. The views never read `request.user`, no JWT/OAuth token parsing is configured in MIDDLEWARE_CLASSES, and no `X-User-Id`-style context is forwarded. The only outbound dependency configured is SMTP to `exchange.acme-corp.internal` (helpdesk/settings.py), which carries no caller identity.
findings.gap: The system cannot distinguish an agent acting as itself from an agent acting on behalf of a specific helpdesk user. Calibrated to INFO for the `data-gateway` archetype, where the surface is a read-only query layer.
findings.recommendation: If on-behalf-of workflows are planned, add token-based identity propagation and record both the actor (agent) and subject (user) on each request.

findings.title: Blast Radius and Transaction Limits
findings.description: No business-domain transaction limits exist. There are no per-caller caps, bulk-operation size limits, or spend thresholds anywhere in the repository; `ticket_list` and `ticket_search` return every matching row with no `LIMIT`. With no write operations present, blast-radius limits are informational for the current surface.
findings.gap: If write capability is added, there would be no cap on records modified or deleted per agent run.
findings.recommendation: Before enabling write-capable agents, add configurable per-principal caps (e.g., max records modified per run) independent of request-rate throttling.

findings.title: Data Quality Awareness
findings.description: No data quality measurement exists. The repository holds a PostgreSQL-backed ticket table but contains no data profiling, null-rate monitoring, duplicate detection, freshness SLA, or quality dashboard definitions. README.md notes the database has no backup beyond a daily pg_dump cron, and no quality tooling is referenced.
findings.gap: There is no completeness or accuracy signal for ticket data, so agent reasoning quality on this dataset is unmeasured.
findings.recommendation: Profile the `tickets_ticket` table for null rates on `status`, `priority` and `requester`, and publish a simple completeness metric before relying on the data for agent decisions.

findings.title: Semantically Meaningful Field Names
findings.description: Field names are readable and semantically meaningful. The columns referenced in tickets/views.py are `id`, `subject`, `requester`, `priority`, `status`, and `created` — plain English, no legacy codes requiring a data dictionary. The table name `tickets_ticket` follows Django's app_model convention.
findings.gap: No data dictionary is needed for an LLM to interpret these fields, which lowers the cost of authoring agent tools. The gap is that these names are discoverable only by reading raw SQL, not from a published schema.
findings.recommendation: Preserve these names verbatim in the new API payloads so agent tooling can rely on them, and document them alongside the OpenAPI spec.

findings.title: Data Catalog / Metadata Layer
findings.description: No data catalog or metadata layer exists. The system owns a PostgreSQL database but the repository contains no Glue Data Catalog definitions, no DataHub/Collibra/Alation references, no data dictionary file, and no schema documentation — README.md documents runtime topology only (Python 2.7, Django 1.4, PostgreSQL 9.1, Apache + mod_wsgi) and lists known issues, not data semantics.
findings.gap: Teams building agent tools must reverse-engineer ticket semantics from raw SQL in tickets/views.py.
findings.recommendation: Publish a lightweight data dictionary for `tickets_ticket` (field, type, meaning, allowed status/priority values) in the repository as the first catalog entry.

findings.title: Structured Response Format
findings.description: Responses are server-rendered HTML: the action returns mapping.findForward('quote') or ('confirm'), resolved by struts-config.xml to /quote.jsp and /confirm.jsp. No JSON or XML serialization code and no content negotiation exist.
findings.gap: Agents would have to parse HTML produced by JSP templates, which is brittle and changes with presentation edits.
findings.recommendation: Emit JSON from the extracted service layer; keep the JSP views as a separate presentation concern over the same service.

findings.title: Event Emission for State Changes
findings.description: No event emission of any kind: saveApplication writes to Oracle and returns; there is no JMS, Kafka, SNS/EventBridge, webhook, or outbox table reference in the repository.
findings.gap: Agents cannot react to loan application submissions or status transitions without polling the database.
findings.recommendation: If event-reactive agents are in scope, add an outbox table written in the same transaction as the application insert, and publish from it.

findings.title: Rate Limit Documentation and Headers
findings.description: The HTTP surface is a WebLogic-hosted Struts action with no throttling: no rate-limiting filter, no gateway in front (deployment is a manual WAR upload per README), and no X-RateLimit/Retry-After headers in the code.
findings.gap: Agent callers have no documented limits and no self-throttling signal; they will discover limits only as connection or Oracle session exhaustion.
findings.recommendation: Document the supported call rate and return rate-limit headers from the fronting gateway once an API layer exists.

findings.title: Data Quality Awareness
findings.description: A persistent store exists (Oracle 11g applications table) but there is no data quality instrumentation: no profiling report, no null-rate or duplicate monitoring, no freshness SLA, and no quality metrics. Duplicate submissions are structurally possible (see API-Q4), so duplicate rate is both unmeasured and likely non-zero.
findings.gap: Agents reasoning over the applications dataset have no completeness or duplication signal to weigh.
findings.recommendation: Baseline null rates and duplicate rates on the applications table and publish a minimal data quality metric before exposing it to agents.

findings.title: Semantically Meaningful Field Names
findings.description: Naming is largely self-describing and free of legacy codes: Java properties are principal, annualRate, termMonths, monthlyPayment, applicantName, and the SQL columns are applicant, principal, rate, term, officer. Minor ambiguity exists where names drop units or qualifiers — 'rate' in the table versus annualRate in the form, and 'term' versus termMonths — and no data dictionary exists to resolve it.
findings.gap: No data dictionary documents units (monthly vs annual rate, months vs years) for the persisted columns, leaving room for an agent to misinterpret 'rate' and 'term'.
findings.recommendation: Rename or document the persisted columns to carry units (annual_rate_pct, term_months) so the semantics are unambiguous without a lookup.

findings.title: Data Catalog / Metadata Layer
findings.description: No catalog or metadata layer exists: no Glue/DataHub/Collibra reference, no data dictionary file, no schema documentation. The applications table structure can only be inferred from the INSERT statement in LoanAction.saveApplication; README describes the runtime stack but documents no data model.
findings.gap: Teams building agent tools must reverse-engineer the data model from source, slowing tool definition and increasing misinterpretation risk.
findings.recommendation: Publish a minimal data dictionary for the applications table (columns, units, sensitivity) as the first catalog entry for this system.

findings.title: Structured Response Format
findings.description: Responses are SOAP 1.1 RPC/encoded XML envelopes wrapping a single xsd:string part (wsdl/PurchaseOrderService.wsdl, submitOrderResponse). The payload inside that string is an ad-hoc colon-delimited convention: "ACCEPTED:<poNumber>" or "ERROR:<exception message>". No JSON serialization exists anywhere in the repository.
findings.gap: The response carries no structured fields - the agent must string-split a status prefix out of an XML-escaped string, and the ERROR branch has no fixed grammar at all.
findings.recommendation: When the contract is modernized, return a structured result (status, poNumber, errors[]) rather than a delimited string; this also removes the need for agent-side prefix parsing.

findings.title: Event Emission for State Changes
findings.description: The service changes state (inserts a purchase order) but emits nothing: there are no webhook callbacks, no SNS/EventBridge/SQS/Kafka clients, and no CDC configuration anywhere in the repository. The only signal of a completed submission is the synchronous return value of submitOrder.
findings.gap: No event or webhook for order acceptance, rejection, or downstream status transitions, so any agent needing to react to order state must re-poll - and no read operation exists to poll (see STATE-Q2).
findings.recommendation: If event-reactive agents are in scope, publish an order-accepted/order-rejected event (EventBridge or a partner webhook) at the point of successful commit.

findings.title: Rate Limit Documentation and Headers
findings.description: No rate limiting or throttling exists or is documented. The service is a WAR on JBoss AS 5.1 (README.md) exposed directly at http://partner-svc.acme-corp.internal:8080/po/PurchaseOrderService (wsdl/PurchaseOrderService.wsdl soap:address) with no gateway in front of it. Searched for API Gateway/WAF/usage-plan IaC, rate-limiting middleware, and Retry-After or X-RateLimit handling in the source: none found.
findings.gap: Agents have no documented call budget and no response header to self-throttle against; limits, if any, are whatever the JBoss thread pool and Oracle connection handling impose implicitly.
findings.recommendation: Publish an explicit per-partner call budget and surface it in responses (Retry-After on rejection) once a gateway or throttling filter is introduced - see STATE-Q5.

findings.title: Data Quality Awareness
findings.description: No data-quality signal exists for partner_orders. There are no quality dashboards, no profiling reports, no null-rate or duplicate monitoring, and no freshness SLA in the repository - and the write path actively admits poor-quality data: amount is inserted unvalidated and unparsed, no uniqueness is enforced on po_number (so duplicates are expected, see STATE-Q3), and no timestamp is recorded (DATA-Q5).
findings.gap: Neither agents nor operators have any measure of completeness, duplication, or accuracy for the dataset agents would be writing into.
findings.recommendation: Add duplicate and null-rate monitoring on partner_orders and publish a simple completeness metric before agents become a significant source of writes.

findings.title: Semantically Meaningful Field Names
findings.description: The field names that exist are readable and unabbreviated: the WSDL parts are partnerId and poXml, the parsed XML elements are poNumber and amount, and the database columns are partner_id, po_number and amount. 'po' is a domain abbreviation for purchase order, which is documented in README.md and the class name PurchaseOrderService. No legacy coded field names (of the CUST_TYP_CD form) appear.
findings.gap: Naming is adequate for LLM reasoning; the real discoverability gap is that the payload structure inside poXml is undeclared (API-Q1/API-Q2), not that the names are opaque.
findings.recommendation: Preserve these names when the contract is modernized, and expand 'po' to purchaseOrder in any new schema for unambiguous agent reasoning.

findings.title: Data Catalog / Metadata Layer
findings.description: No catalog or metadata layer exists for the Oracle 11g data the service writes. Searched for Glue/DataHub/Collibra/Alation references, data dictionaries, metadata files, and schema documentation: none are present. README.md describes the runtime and known issues but documents no data model, and the partner_orders table is only visible as an inline INSERT statement in PurchaseOrderService.java.
findings.gap: Anyone building agent tools against this system must reverse-engineer the data model from a single SQL string, which slows tool definition and invites misinterpretation.
findings.recommendation: Document the partner_orders schema and its field semantics in a data dictionary (or register it in a catalog) as part of publishing the agent-facing contract.

findings.title: Machine-Readable API Specification
findings.description: has_http_rpc_surface=false — the system exposes no callable API surface, so there is no interface for a machine-readable specification to describe. Searched for `openapi.*`, `swagger.*`, `*.graphql`, `*.gql`, `*.smithy` and AsyncAPI files across the repository: none found. The nearest thing to a contract is the implicit 120-byte fixed-width record layout in `src/PAYRUN.cbl` lines 51-55.
findings.gap: Recorded as INFO per surface-flag calibration: no HTTP/RPC surface — machine-readable spec is not applicable until an API facade exists (API-Q1).
findings.recommendation: When the API facade from API-Q1 is built, generate its OpenAPI specification from annotations rather than maintaining it by hand.

findings.title: Structured Error Responses
findings.description: has_http_rpc_surface=false — there are no API responses to structure. Failure signalling today is an abend plus JES return code; `READ-EMP` (`src/PAYRUN.cbl` lines 57-59) has no FILE STATUS clause, so there is no error code, message, or retryable indicator available to any caller.
findings.gap: Recorded as INFO per surface-flag calibration: no HTTP/RPC surface — structured error responses are not applicable until an API facade exists.
findings.recommendation: Design the API facade's error contract up front with an error code, message and explicit retryable flag, and back it with FILE STATUS handling in the COBOL (see DATA-Q4).

findings.title: Structured Response Format
findings.description: The response format is a fixed-width, positional, 120-byte flat file: `PAY-RECORD PIC X(120)` (`src/PAYRUN.cbl` line 29) populated by a `STRING ... DELIMITED BY SIZE` concatenation of employee id, name and net pay (lines 51-55), allocated as `RECFM=FB,LRECL=120` (`jcl/PAYRUN.jcl` line 12) and transferred in FTP `ascii` mode. There is no JSON, XML, or self-describing binary format.
findings.gap: Positional fixed-width output has no field names, so every consumer (and any agent tool) needs an out-of-band byte-offset map. EBCDIC/ASCII conversion in the FTP step adds a second interpretation hazard for packed numeric fields.
findings.recommendation: Have the API facade emit JSON with named fields, derived from a published copybook, rather than passing the fixed-width layout through to consumers.

findings.title: Event Emission for State Changes
findings.description: No event emission. State changes are visible only as a new catalogued GDG generation and a file landing at `/incoming/payout.dat` on the gateway (`jcl/PAYRUN.jcl` lines 9-20). There is no webhook, SNS/EventBridge/SQS integration, Kafka topic, or CDC pipeline — the only notification mechanism is `NOTIFY=&SYSUID` (line 1), which targets a human TSO user.
findings.gap: Agents cannot react to payroll state changes; they would have to poll for a new file generation on a biweekly cadence.
findings.recommendation: Publish a completion event (run id, period, record count, status) to EventBridge or SNS when the run finishes, so event-reactive consumers do not need to poll the dataset.

findings.title: Rate Limiting and Throttling
findings.description: has_http_rpc_surface=false — there is no API layer at which to enforce rate limits. Invocation is gated instead by the CA-7 biweekly schedule (`jcl/PAYRUN.jcl` line 3), and the job requests unbounded storage with `REGION=0M` (line 1). No API Gateway throttle, WAF rate rule, or rate-limiting middleware exists.
findings.gap: Recorded as INFO per surface-flag calibration: no HTTP/RPC surface — API-layer rate limiting is not applicable. Scheduler-based invocation incidentally bounds call frequency today, but that protection disappears the moment an API facade is added.
findings.recommendation: Add throttling at the API facade when it is introduced, sized to the batch window, and replace `REGION=0M` with a bounded region to cap a single run's resource consumption.

findings.title: Data Quality Awareness
findings.description: No data quality measurement. There is no profiling report, null-rate monitor, duplicate detection, freshness SLA, or quality dashboard anywhere in the repository. Known quality hazards are documented but unmeasured: state tax lookup 'REMOVED IN 2011, DONE MANUALLY' (`src/PAYRUN.cbl` line 50), tax tables 'updated by hand each January' and the FICA wage base hardcoded at the 2019 value (line 34).
findings.gap: An agent reasoning over this payroll data has no completeness signal and would treat manually-patched, structurally incomplete net-pay figures as authoritative.
findings.recommendation: Instrument basic quality metrics for each run (record counts, null/zero-rate on rate and hours, period-over-period variance) and publish them alongside the run, pairing with the degradation signal in STATE-Q7.

findings.title: Semantically Meaningful Field Names
findings.description: Field names are legacy COBOL abbreviations requiring a data dictionary: `EMP-ID`, `EMP-RATE`, `EMP-HOURS`, `EMP-SSN`, `EMP-ACCT` (`src/PAYRUN.cbl` lines 21-27) and working-storage names `WS-GROSS`, `WS-FICA`, `WS-FICA-RATE`, `WS-WAGE-BASE`, `WS-NET`, `WS-EOF` (lines 31-35). They are at least domain-recognizable rather than opaque codes, but the output `PAY-RECORD` is wholly positional with no field names at all, and no data dictionary file exists in the repository.
findings.gap: An LLM can infer most of these abbreviations (EMP-ACCT, WS-FICA) from context, so semantic readiness is moderate rather than poor — but the positional output file carries no names whatsoever and the 17-character `EMP-ACCT` has no documented format.
findings.recommendation: Publish a data dictionary mapping each PIC field to a semantic name, type and format, and use expanded names (employeeId, grossPay, ficaWithheld, netPay) in the API facade's JSON representation.

findings.title: Data Catalog / Metadata Layer
findings.description: No data catalog or metadata layer. The repository has no Glue Catalog reference, no DataHub/Collibra/Alation entry, no metadata files and no schema documentation; `README.md` is a 24-line architecture-and-known-issues summary with no field or dataset inventory. Semantic knowledge of the DB2 tables and the EMPMAST layout lives in the ops runbook referenced from `jcl/PAYRUN.jcl` line 4 and in retired authors' tribal knowledge ('AUTHOR: R. ANDERSON (RETIRED 2014)').
findings.gap: Teams building agent tools against payroll have no discoverable description of what data exists or what it means, which directly slows tool definition and raises the risk of misinterpreting fields.
findings.recommendation: Catalog the payroll datasets and DB2 tables with field-level descriptions and sensitivity labels, starting from the record layouts in `src/PAYRUN.cbl`, and treat the catalog as the source the API facade's documentation is generated from.

findings.title: Alerting on Error Rates and Latency
findings.description: has_http_rpc_surface=false — there are no API error-rate or latency metrics to alert on. Operational signalling consists of `NOTIFY=&SYSUID` on job completion (`jcl/PAYRUN.jcl` line 1) and `MSGCLASS=X` spool output. No CloudWatch alarms, anomaly detection, SLO alerting or paging integration exists, despite README noting the batch 'runs 5-7 hours and sometimes overruns' its window.
findings.gap: Recorded as INFO per surface-flag calibration: no HTTP/RPC surface — API alerting is not applicable yet. Note that even the existing batch-overrun condition is unalerted, so degradation is discovered by downstream complaint.
findings.recommendation: Alert on batch duration against the window and on job abend now; add error-rate and latency alarms at the API facade when it is introduced.

findings.title: Infrastructure Governance for Agent-Facing Surface
findings.description: has_http_rpc_surface=false and has_auth_surface=false — the repository defines no agent-facing integration surface to govern. There is no IaC of any kind (searched for `*.tf`, CloudFormation templates, CDK entry points, Helm charts, Kustomize and Ansible: none found), no drift detection, and no review automation. The EC2 gateway, its network path and the `payroll` account exist only as hardcoded values in `jcl/PAYRUN.jcl` lines 15-21. README confirms 'No source control until the files were copied here in 2021'.
findings.gap: Recorded as INFO per surface-flag calibration. Nonetheless the infrastructure that will carry the agent integration (gateway, credentials, network path) is entirely manually managed, so the governance gap becomes material as soon as the API facade from API-Q1 is built.
findings.recommendation: Define the gateway, IAM/RACF roles, secrets and network path as code with peer-reviewed changes and drift detection before exposing any agent-facing endpoint.

findings.title: CI/CD with API Contract Testing
findings.description: has_http_rpc_surface=false — there are no APIs to contract-test. There is also no CI/CD pipeline at all: searched for `.github/workflows/`, `.gitlab-ci.yml`, `Jenkinsfile`, `buildspec.yml` and `appspec.yml` — none present. Compilation and promotion are manual, as implied by 'DO NOT RECOMPILE WITHOUT CONTACTING MAINFRAME TEAM' (`src/PAYRUN.cbl` line 5) and README's 'changes validated in a shared QA region only'.
findings.gap: Recorded as INFO per surface-flag calibration: no HTTP/RPC surface — API contract testing is not applicable. The absence of any pipeline means there is also no automated gate for the fixed-width layout contract that consumers depend on (see DISC-Q1).
findings.recommendation: Stand up a pipeline that compiles, runs the ENG-Q4 tests, and diffs the published record layout for breaking changes; extend it to API contract tests once the facade exists.

findings.title: Rollback Capability
findings.description: has_http_rpc_surface=false — there is no deployed request-serving surface to roll back. Deployment is a manual load-module replacement into `ACME.PAYROLL.LOADLIB` (`jcl/PAYRUN.jcl` line 6); there is no blue/green config, no CodeDeploy rollback trigger, no feature flags and no traffic shifting. Data-side recovery is partially served by GDG generations (`PAYOUT(+1)`), which retain prior outputs but do not restore prior program versions.
findings.gap: Recorded as INFO per surface-flag calibration. Practically, reverting a bad payroll change depends on manual load-library restoration with no tested procedure, and GDG retention covers output files only.
findings.recommendation: Version load modules with a documented, tested restore procedure (and automate it in the ENG-Q2 pipeline) so a payroll-breaking change can be reverted predictably.

findings.title: No write endpoints; idempotency is informational under read-only scope
findings.description: The service exposes no write operation. pricing.cpp's main() reads QUERY_STRING, performs a file lookup, and prints a computed total; it never opens a file for writing, never mutates /etc/pricing/rules.dat (lookup_price opens it with mode "r"), and publishes no messages. Every invocation is a side-effect-free read, so repeated identical calls are naturally idempotent. No idempotency-key handling exists, but none is required at the current scope.
findings.gap: None at read-only scope. Note that if a rules-management or price-override endpoint is ever added, no idempotency mechanism exists to build on, and the CGI model (one process per request, no shared state) offers no dedupe store.
findings.recommendation: Keep the agent scope read-only. If write capability is introduced later, require an Idempotency-Key header with server-side dedupe before exposing it to agents.

findings.title: Responses are presentation HTML, not structured data
findings.description:
The response format is a hand-assembled HTML fragment. main() in pricing.cpp emits 'Content-Type: text/html' followed by printf calls producing

ACME Pricing

and four

elements carrying SKU, Qty, Unit, and Total, with the numeric values already formatted as '$%.2f'. There is no JSON serialization, no XML marshalling, no Protobuf/Thrift definition, and no content negotiation — the format is fixed regardless of Accept header. Currency is implied by the '$' literal and is not a field.
findings.gap: Consumers must regex or DOM-parse presentation markup to recover values, and the price arrives as a pre-formatted display string rather than a typed number with an explicit currency.
findings.recommendation: Emit application/json with typed fields (unit_price and total_price as numbers, explicit currency code) as part of the API-Q1 remediation; retain HTML only behind content negotiation for legacy browser callers.

findings.title: No rate limits documented and no rate-limit response headers
findings.description: No rate limit is documented anywhere and none is advertised in responses. README.md and CONTAINERIZE.md describe the endpoint and its health URL but state no throttling policy. pricing.cpp emits exactly one header — 'Content-Type: text/html' — and no X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, or Retry-After. There is no API Gateway usage plan, WAF rate rule, or rate-limiting middleware in the repository (the only commented gateway configuration, in k8s/service.yaml, carries no throttle annotations).
findings.gap: An agent has no published budget to respect and no server feedback to self-throttle against; it will discover limits only by saturating the deployment. This is the caller-visible facet of the enforcement gap in STATE-Q5.
findings.recommendation: Define and publish a per-client request budget alongside the API specification, and return X-RateLimit-Remaining and Retry-After from the throttling layer added for STATE-Q5.

findings.title: No identity propagation; archetype-calibrated to INFO
findings.description: The service neither receives nor forwards identity. pricing.cpp reads only the QUERY_STRING environment variable, so Authorization headers and X-User-Id style context are discarded by the application, and it makes no outbound service calls through which identity could be propagated. There is no JWT parsing, token-exchange, or on-behalf-of flow, and no separate credential path for agent-as-self versus agent-on-behalf-of-user. Native severity for AUTH-Q4 is RISK-SAFETY, but the archetype calibration for stateless-utility downgrades it to INFO: the response is derived solely from the requested SKU and quantity against a shared reference price list, so caller identity does not change what data is returned.
findings.gap: No identity context flows through the service. This is acceptable while responses are identity-independent, but it means customer-specific or contract-specific pricing could not be implemented or audited safely without first adding identity propagation.
findings.recommendation: Preserve the identity-independence of the response. If tiered or customer-specific pricing is ever introduced, add verified identity propagation and distinguish agent-as-self from agent-on-behalf-of-user before exposing it to agents.

findings.title: No audit logging; surface-calibrated to INFO (no auth surface, no writes)
findings.description: The application writes no audit record: pricing.cpp logs nothing, and there is no CloudTrail configuration, log-file validation, S3 Object Lock bucket, or CloudWatch retention policy in the repository (no IaC exists; k8s/ contains only namespace, configmap, deployment, and service). Apache's default access log, whose directory is chowned to appuser in the Dockerfile, is mutable container-local plain text with no authenticated principal — and no principal exists to record, since the surface is unauthenticated. Surface-flag calibration applies: has_auth_surface is false and has_write_operations is false, so this question is recorded as INFO rather than at its scope-resolved RISK-SAFETY severity. The system executes no agent-invoked write operations, so write-attribution audit is a consumer responsibility.
findings.gap: No immutable, attributable log exists. There are no writes to attribute today, but there is also no tamper-evident record of which caller requested which price — relevant if pricing lookups ever become subject to dispute or audit.
findings.recommendation: Capture gateway access logs (with the authenticated principal added for AUTH-Q1) into CloudWatch Logs or an S3 bucket with Object Lock and a defined retention period, so read access is attributable and tamper-evident before any write capability is contemplated.

findings.title: No identity lifecycle to suspend; surface-calibrated to INFO
findings.description: The service issues and enforces no identities, so there is nothing to suspend. There are no API keys, service accounts, Cognito users, or IAM principals defined in the repository, and no revocation endpoint or disable mechanism in pricing.cpp. Surface-flag calibration applies: has_auth_surface is false and has_write_operations is false, so AUTH-Q7 is recorded as INFO rather than RISK-SAFETY. The only available isolation lever today is coarse and global — scaling the Deployment to zero or deleting the Service in k8s/service.yaml, which removes access for every caller at once.
findings.gap: No per-caller revocation is possible, because no per-caller identity exists. Containing a misbehaving agent currently requires taking the whole service offline.
findings.recommendation: When machine identity is added for AUTH-Q1, issue one credential per agent at the gateway so an individual credential can be revoked without affecting other callers.

findings.title: No multi-step write sequences requiring compensation; archetype-calibrated to INFO
findings.description: There is nothing to compensate. Each request is a single, self-contained, side-effect-free computation: main() in pricing.cpp parses the query string, reads /etc/pricing/rules.dat in read mode, multiplies unit price by quantity, prints HTML, and exits. There is no saga, two-phase commit, undo endpoint, or Step Functions workflow, and none is needed — no persistent state is mutated and no downstream service is called, so a failure mid-request leaves no partial state behind. The archetype calibration for stateless-utility records this as INFO, consistent with the read-only agent scope.
findings.gap: None at the current scope. The absence of any transactional framework means that adding a multi-step write workflow later would start from zero compensation capability, in a CGI process model with no shared state between requests.
findings.recommendation: Keep the service stateless and side-effect-free. Any future write workflow should be implemented outside the CGI binary in a component that supports compensating transactions.

findings.title: No business transaction limits; scope-calibrated to INFO
findings.description: No business-domain limits exist: there is no per-caller cap on records affected, no spend threshold, and no bulk-operation size limit in pricing.cpp or k8s/*.yaml. One quantifiable gap does exist — qty is taken from the query string via atoi with no upper bound and multiplied directly into the returned total (double total = unit * qty), so a caller can request an arbitrarily large quantity and receive an arbitrarily large quoted total. Because agent_scope is read-only, this produces no state change or spend; the blast radius of the worst case is a misleading quote, not a committed transaction. Scope calibration therefore records STATE-Q6 as INFO.
findings.gap: No bound on caller-supplied quantity, so quoted totals are unbounded and negative quantities are accepted (atoi parses '-5'), yielding negative totals. Harmless while nothing acts on the quote; material if a downstream workflow ever consumes it.
findings.recommendation: Validate qty into a sane business range (positive, with a documented maximum) as part of the DATA-Q4 remediation, and introduce per-caller business limits before any write capability is exposed to agents.

findings.title: Not a sensitive-data handling target; no PII, PHI, financial records, or credentials
findings.description: Stage A of DATA-Q1 resolves to No. has_persistent_data_store is false: the only data the system reads is /etc/pricing/rules.dat, a pipe-delimited SKU-to-price reference list (lookup_price in pricing.cpp; the Dockerfile seeds it with the single line 'SAMPLE-SKU|9.99'), containing no user identifiers, health records, financial instruments, or credentials. has_logging_of_user_data is false: the binary logs nothing. The service's purpose — product price lookup — is not a regulated data domain, and CONTAINERIZE.md confirms 'No secrets are required by this application'. The stateless-utility archetype calibration independently records this question as INFO. Stage B was therefore not evaluated.
findings.gap: None. No sensitive fields exist to scope out of agent-facing responses; the response echoes only the caller's own SKU and quantity plus a reference price.
findings.recommendation: Re-run this assessment if the service is ever extended to customer-specific or contract pricing, which would introduce customer identifiers and commercially sensitive terms into responses.

findings.title: No data subject to residency or sovereignty constraints
findings.description: Surface-flag calibration applies: has_persistent_data_store is false and has_logging_of_user_data is false, so the system holds no data subject to residency requirements and DATA-Q2 is recorded as INFO. The only data read is the SKU/price reference file /etc/pricing/rules.dat (pricing.cpp, lookup_price), which contains no personal data; nothing is persisted or logged. No GDPR/LGPD/HIPAA references, region-pinned storage configuration, or cross-region replication settings appear anywhere in the repository (searched README.md, CONTAINERIZE.md, and all k8s manifests; no IaC exists). The stateless-utility archetype calibration points to the same result.
findings.gap: None for the data the system holds. Note that no region constraint is expressed in configuration either, so if customer-specific pricing is introduced later there is no residency control to inherit.
findings.recommendation: If the pricing rules ever incorporate customer- or contract-specific data, document the applicable residency constraints and pin storage and any LLM endpoint to the required jurisdiction before granting agent access.

findings.title: No user-data logging pipeline where PII could leak
findings.description: Surface-flag calibration applies: has_logging_of_user_data is false and has_persistent_data_store is false, so DATA-Q6 is recorded as INFO. pricing.cpp emits no log output at all — its only writes are the HTML response on stdout — and holds no user data. No log-scrubbing middleware, masking library, CloudWatch log filter, or Macie integration exists, but there is also no pipeline carrying user content into logs. The stateless-utility archetype calibration gives the same result. One residual consideration: Apache's default access log (its directory is chowned to appuser in the Dockerfile) records the full request line including the query string, so caller-supplied SKU values are captured verbatim in container-local logs; SKUs are product identifiers, not PII, but a caller that passes unexpected content in the sku parameter would see it persisted there unredacted.
findings.gap: No redaction exists for the one surface that does capture caller input — the Apache access log's query string. Low consequence today because the parameter space is product SKUs and quantities.
findings.recommendation: If access logs are shipped to a central platform, configure the log format to exclude or hash the query string, and keep the documented parameter contract limited to non-personal identifiers.

findings.title: Field names are short but semantically interpretable
findings.description: The externally visible vocabulary is small and readable rather than coded. The query parameters are sku and qty (parse_query in pricing.cpp), and the response labels are SKU, Qty, Unit, and Total (main()). Internal identifiers follow the same pattern: lookup_price, file_sku, unit, total. These are common commerce abbreviations an LLM resolves without a lookup table — there are no legacy mainframe-style codes such as CUST_TYP_CD. Two mild ambiguities remain: 'Unit' and 'Total' do not state that they are prices or name a currency (the '$' is a hardcoded literal in the printf format), and 'qty' is abbreviated. No data dictionary exists in the repository, and none is needed at this vocabulary size.
findings.gap: Minor only: field labels omit units and currency, which an agent must infer from the '$' glyph embedded in the formatted string.
findings.recommendation: When the JSON interface from API-Q1 is introduced, use explicit names (unit_price, total_price, quantity) and an ISO-4217 currency field so no inference is required.

findings.title: No automated tests of any kind; archetype-calibrated to INFO
findings.description: The repository contains no tests. There is no test directory, no test framework dependency (there is no dependency manifest at all), and no API test suite — Makefile defines only all, install, and clean targets, and no CI configuration exists to run tests in. README.md states this directly under Known Issues: 'No tests; correctness validated by spot-checking output'. ENG-Q4 is calibrated to INFO for the stateless-utility archetype. Untested behaviour that would matter to an agent is nonetheless concrete: unknown-SKU handling, missing-rules-file handling, quantity coercion by atoi, and the response field layout are all unverified.
findings.gap: No regression safety net for the agent-facing contract. Input handling, output format, and error behaviour are entirely unverified, which compounds the absence of contract testing in ENG-Q2.
findings.recommendation: Add a small black-box test suite that runs the container and asserts known-SKU pricing, unknown-SKU behaviour, missing-rules-file behaviour, and oversized/negative qty rejection, then execute it in the CI pipeline added for ENG-Q2.

findings.title: Structured Response Format
findings.description: Responses are server-rendered HTML. `create` ends in `redirect_to :action => 'show'` and `render :action => 'new'`; `index` and `show` assign instance variables (`@orders`, `@order`) for ERB views. No JSON/XML serializers, `to_json` calls, content-type handling, or Protobuf/Thrift definitions are present in the repository.
findings.gap: There is no text-structured machine format for an agent to consume; HTML scraping would be required.
findings.recommendation: Expose JSON representations with explicit `Content-Type: application/json` as part of the API facade work in API-Q1, and keep HTML views for human users only.

findings.title: Event Emission for State Changes
findings.description: No event emission exists for order state changes. `create` persists and charges inline and then redirects; there are no webhook endpoints, no SNS/EventBridge/SQS/Kafka clients, and no CDC configuration anywhere in the repository.
findings.gap: Agents cannot react to order status transitions or charge outcomes; any agent workflow must poll `show`.
findings.recommendation: If event-reactive agents are a target, publish domain events (`order.created`, `order.charged`, `order.failed`) to SNS/EventBridge from the order lifecycle rather than requiring polling.

findings.title: Rate Limit Documentation and Headers
findings.description: No rate limits are documented or enforced. The controller returns no `X-RateLimit-Remaining` or `Retry-After` headers, and there is no gateway in front of the app — README describes Mongrel behind Apache `mod_proxy_balancer` with no API Gateway, WAF, or usage plan. No rate-limiting middleware is present (no dependency manifest exists to declare one).
findings.gap: Agents have no self-throttling signal and no documented ceiling, so they will discover limits only as failures.
findings.recommendation: Publish a documented request budget and emit `X-RateLimit-*` and `Retry-After` headers from the edge once rate limiting is introduced (see STATE-Q5).

findings.title: Data Quality Awareness
findings.description: No data-quality instrumentation exists for the order dataset. The repository has a persistent store (MySQL-backed orders) but no data-quality dashboard, profiling report, null-rate or duplicate monitoring, and no freshness SLA. The only quality-relevant signal is negative: README documents long-standing data-integrity hazards (mass assignment) and the controller's unconstrained inserts (API-Q4) make duplicate orders likely.
findings.gap: There is no completeness or accuracy baseline for order data, so an agent reasoning over it cannot know how much to trust it.
findings.recommendation: Profile the orders table for null rates and duplicates, publish a small set of quality metrics alongside the service's operational metrics, and define a freshness SLA before pointing agents at the dataset.

findings.title: Semantically Meaningful Field Names
findings.description: Field and identifier names are semantically clear rather than legacy-coded. Observed names: `orders`, `status`, `created_at`, `total`, `card_number`, `card_exp`, `merchant_id`, `api_password`, `endpoint`, `mode`. These are human-readable and need no data dictionary; `card_exp` is the only abbreviation and is unambiguous in context. No data dictionary file exists, and none is required for interpretation.
findings.gap: LLM-based reasoning over this schema will interpret field meanings correctly without a lookup table — a positive signal for tool authoring.
findings.recommendation: Preserve these naming conventions in the new API surface, and document the `status` enum's allowed values since the value set is not discoverable from the code (only the `'pending'` default appears).

findings.title: Data Catalog / Metadata Layer
findings.description: No catalog or metadata layer describes the order data. Searched the repository for Glue Data Catalog definitions, DataHub/Collibra/Alation references, metadata files, data dictionaries, and schema documentation — none are present. README documents runtime architecture only (Ruby/Rails/MySQL/Mongrel versions), not data semantics.
findings.gap: Teams building agent tools against this system must reverse-engineer meaning from controller code and live MySQL inspection, slowing tool definition and raising the chance of misinterpretation.
findings.recommendation: Register the orders dataset in a catalog (Glue or an internal equivalent) with column-level descriptions and sensitivity labels, which also supplies the classification metadata DATA-Q1 B3 found missing.

findings.title: Structured Response Format
findings.description: Responses are server-rendered HTML - gridEntries.DataBind() emits a WebForms grid with ViewState, which README.md notes makes pages multi-megabyte. No JSON or content-negotiated serialization exists.
findings.gap: No machine-friendly response format.
findings.recommendation: Emit JSON from the extracted service layer.

findings.title: Event Emission for State Changes
findings.description: The insert emits no event - there is no webhook, SNS/SQS/Kafka publish, or CDC mechanism.
findings.gap: No event emission for state changes; agents must poll.
findings.recommendation: Publish a domain event on timesheet creation if event-reactive agents are planned.

findings.title: Rate Limit Documentation and Headers
findings.description: No rate limits are documented and no rate-limit or Retry-After headers are returned; there is no gateway, WAF, or limiting configuration.
findings.gap: Callers have no self-throttling signal.
findings.recommendation: Publish limits and return Retry-After once throttling is introduced (STATE-Q5).

findings.title: Data Quality Awareness
findings.description: No data-quality metric, profiling report, null-rate monitor, or duplicate detection exists, and there is no uniqueness constraint on the timesheet business key.
findings.gap: Dataset trustworthiness is unmeasured.
findings.recommendation: Baseline duplicate and completeness rates before agent use.

findings.title: Semantically Meaningful Field Names
findings.description: Field names are self-describing: employee_id, entry_date, hours, project. No cryptic legacy codes appear in the SQL.
findings.gap: None material - naming is already interpretable without a data dictionary.
findings.recommendation: Preserve these names when exposing an API.

findings.title: Data Catalog / Metadata Layer
findings.description: No data catalog or metadata layer exists; the only description of the data is README.md prose and the inline SQL column list.
findings.gap: Semantics must be inferred from source code.
findings.recommendation: Document the timesheet entity in a catalog or data dictionary.

findings.title: Structured Response Format
findings.description: Responses are JSON over a GraphQL envelope. Apollo Server 4 (@apollo/server ^4.10.0) serializes to application/json via @as-integrations/aws-lambda, and all scalar types in schema/catalog.graphql are LLM-friendly primitives (ID, String, Int, Boolean). No binary payloads, no XML, and no Protobuf/Thrift definitions exist in the repository.
findings.gap: None — the format requires no parsing adapter for agent tooling.
findings.recommendation: No change required. When defining agent tools, pin explicit field selections rather than requesting every Product field, to keep responses inside the context window.

findings.title: Event Emission for State Changes
findings.description: No event emission exists. infra/template.yaml declares no SNS topic, no EventBridge rule, no SQS queue, and no StreamSpecification on ProductsTable, so DynamoDB Streams/CDC is off. src/resolvers/catalog.ts publishes nothing after a write, schema/catalog.graphql defines no Subscription type, and package.json declares no messaging client.
findings.gap: Agents reacting to catalog changes must poll the products query, which combines poorly with the absent throttling (STATE-Q5) and the uncapped limit argument (STATE-Q6).
findings.recommendation: If event-reactive agents are a target, enable StreamSpecification with NEW_AND_OLD_IMAGES on ProductsTable and fan out to EventBridge — this would also give the AUTH-Q6 audit trail a natural data-plane source.

findings.title: Rate Limit Documentation and Headers
findings.description: No limits are documented or signalled. The CatalogApi HttpApi in infra/template.yaml has no throttle settings and no usage plan; src/server.ts sets no response headers, so no X-RateLimit-Remaining or Retry-After reaches the caller; README.md documents no rate limits. The only effective ceilings are account-level Lambda concurrency and DynamoDB on-demand defaults, neither visible to a caller.
findings.gap: An agent has no feedback channel to self-throttle and will discover limits only as unexplained failures.
findings.recommendation: Once stage throttling is configured per STATE-Q5, surface the limit and remaining budget in a GraphQL response extension or HTTP header, and document the published limits in README.md.

findings.title: Sensitive Data Classification
findings.description: Stage A scope gate resolved to No. ProductsTable is keyed on sku and the Product type in schema/catalog.graphql holds only product-merchandising attributes (sku, name, description, priceCents, currency, active, updatedAt). There is no user identifier, email, phone, address, account detail, health record, payment instrument, or persisted credential; priceCents is a product list price, not a financial instrument. has_logging_of_user_data is false (no log statements exist in src/), so no request bodies are captured, and a product catalog is not a regulated data domain. Stage B is therefore skipped per the rubric and absence of classification controls is not flagged.
findings.gap: No formal classification metadata (B3-class), which the rubric treats as aspirational and which is moot while Stage A is No.
findings.recommendation: Re-run this question if the schema gains customer-, supplier-, or cost-sensitive fields (e.g., wholesale cost, supplier contacts) — that would flip Stage A to Yes and engage the B1/B2 sub-checks.

findings.title: Data Quality Awareness
findings.description: No data-quality instrumentation exists for the products dataset. There are no quality dashboards or profiling reports, no null-rate or completeness monitoring, no duplicate detection (the SKU hash key structurally prevents duplicate rows, which is a property rather than a measurement), no freshness SLA documented in README.md, and no quality metrics emitted from src/resolvers/catalog.ts.
findings.gap: Dataset completeness is unmeasured — an agent cannot know whether description is populated for 95% or 40% of SKUs, or whether stale SKUs linger with active: true.
findings.recommendation: Emit periodic completeness metrics (percentage of active SKUs with non-null description, count of SKUs not updated in 180 days) to CloudWatch so agent tool descriptions can state known coverage.

findings.title: Semantically Meaningful Field Names
findings.description: Naming is consistently self-describing. schema/catalog.graphql uses sku, name, description, priceCents, currency, active, updatedAt, nextCursor, items — camelCase, unabbreviated, with no legacy codes requiring a data dictionary. priceCents encodes its unit in the name, removing an ambiguity an LLM would otherwise guess. DynamoDB attribute names in src/resolvers/catalog.ts match the GraphQL field names exactly, so there is no translation layer to misread, and every operation carries a docstring.
findings.gap: None — agent tool definitions can be generated from introspection with no field glossary.
findings.recommendation: No change required. Preserve the priceCents-style unit-in-name convention for any new numeric field.

findings.title: Data Catalog / Metadata Layer
findings.description: No dedicated catalog or metadata layer exists — no AWS Glue Data Catalog resource in infra/template.yaml, no DataHub/Collibra/Alation reference, no data dictionary file, and no sensitivity or ownership tags on ProductsTable. The partial substitute is strong: schema/catalog.graphql is a committed, docstring-annotated contract exposed at runtime through GraphQL introspection.
findings.gap: Portfolio-level discoverability is missing — nothing outside this repository advertises that this catalog data exists or who owns it.
findings.recommendation: Register the schema in a central API/data catalog and add owner and data-sensitivity tags to ProductsTable so portfolio-level agent planning can discover the service.

findings.title: Business Outcome Metrics
findings.description: Only infrastructure telemetry is configured. Globals.Function.Tracing: Active enables X-Ray and Lambda/API Gateway/DynamoDB publish their standard CloudWatch metrics automatically, but no custom business metric is emitted: there is no PutMetricData call, no embedded-metric-format log line, and no dashboard or business-KPI alarm in the template. README.md's "CloudWatch metrics" refers to these default infrastructure metrics.
findings.gap: Infrastructure metrics show that mutations succeeded but not whether they produced good outcomes — no signal for SKUs published per run, soft-delete rate, or price-change magnitude, which are what would reveal a misbehaving agent whose calls all return 200.
findings.recommendation: Emit EMF metrics from the mutation resolvers for products upserted, products soft-deleted, and absolute price delta, segmented by principal once AUTH-Q6 claim propagation is in place.

findings.title: Structured Response Format
findings.description: Every tool returns a plain dict or list[dict] of JSON-native scalars, with Decimal columns coerced via float() and dates via str(); prompts and completions are serialised with json.dumps. No XML, Protobuf or binary formats are used.
findings.gap: Date values are stringified without timezone normalisation.
findings.recommendation: Keep the JSON-native contract and standardise date serialisation to ISO-8601 UTC.

findings.title: Event Emission for State Changes
findings.description: settlement_writer commits a status transition and a payment release without emitting any event - no SNS publish, EventBridge put_events, SQS send or webhook exists in the repo. The only downstream signal is the payment_queue row, which consumers must poll.
findings.gap: No push notification path for agent-initiated state changes.
findings.recommendation: Publish a SettlementCommitted event to EventBridge from the settlement path; it also enables the approval flows called for by HITL-Q2.

findings.title: Rate Limit Documentation and Headers
findings.description: No throttle configuration, usage plan or WAF rate rule exists in infra/, and no rate-limit headers or quota documentation appear in code or README. The only documented bound on agent call volume is the --max-claims 500 batch flag.
findings.gap: No documented limits and no self-throttling signal for callers.
findings.recommendation: Document per-caller limits once gateway throttling is added (STATE-Q5) and return remaining-quota metadata in tool responses.

findings.title: Data Quality Awareness
findings.description: No data quality score, completeness metric, null-rate monitor, duplicate detection or freshness SLA exists for the claims database or the knowledge base. retrieval.py documents that ingestion loads the entire claims archive including closed and denied claims with no quality filter, returning only a similarity score.
findings.gap: No curation or quality signal on the comparables used to price settlements.
findings.recommendation: Define a curation filter and a freshness/completeness metric for the knowledge base corpus before expanding to the property-claims book.

findings.title: Data Catalog / Metadata Layer
findings.description: No Glue catalog, DataHub/Collibra reference, data dictionary or schema documentation exists. The claims, policies, payments and payment_queue tables are discoverable only by reading inline SQL in tools.py, and the knowledge base contents are described only in prose in retrieval.py and README.md.
findings.gap: No catalog or data dictionary for the claims schema or the knowledge-base corpus.
findings.recommendation: Publish a data dictionary covering the four tables and the knowledge base, including sensitivity labels (feeds DATA-Q1 B3).

findings.title: Business Outcome Metrics
findings.description: No put_metric_data call, custom namespace, dashboard or business KPI alarm exists; the only telemetry is free-text log.info output. Nothing measures settlement accuracy, adjuster override rate or auto-approve rate.
findings.gap: No business-outcome signal to detect degrading recommendation quality.
findings.recommendation: Emit adjuster-override rate, average settled amount and tool-failure rate as custom metrics and alarm on drift.

findings.title: Structured Response Format
findings.description: Responses are structured JSON throughout. The service is built on Fastify 4 (package.json), which serializes returned objects to application/json automatically - src/routes.ts returns the Order object directly, `reply.code(201).send(order)`, and JSON error bodies `{ code, message }`. No XML marshalling, Protobuf or Thrift definitions exist in the repository, and no binary response path is present.
findings.gap: None - JSON is directly consumable by an LLM-based agent.
findings.recommendation: Keep JSON as the agent-facing format and add explicit response schemas (see API-Q2) so Fastify's fast-json-stringify enforces the shape rather than serializing whatever the query returns.

findings.title: Event Emission for State Changes
findings.description: The service emits no events. There is no webhook endpoint in src/routes.ts, no SNS/EventBridge/SQS/Kafka client in package.json (dependencies are fastify, jose, pg only), no outbox table, and no CDC configuration in infra/ecs.yaml. State transitions - placed, shipped, cancelled, refunded - are written straight to PostgreSQL in src/services/order-service.ts with no notification to any consumer.
findings.gap: No event or webhook surface for state changes, so any agent needing to react to an order transition must poll GET /orders/{id}.
findings.recommendation: If event-reactive agents are a target, add a transactional outbox on the status transitions and publish to EventBridge - this would also provide the atomicity STATE-Q1 requires, so the two are best built together.

findings.title: Rate Limit Documentation and Headers
findings.description: No rate limits are documented and no rate limit headers are returned. openapi/orders.yaml contains no throttling documentation and no 429 response on any operation; src/routes.ts sets no X-RateLimit-Remaining or Retry-After header; and infra/ecs.yaml has no API Gateway usage plan or WAF rate rule. This is consistent with no rate limiting being enforced at all (STATE-Q5).
findings.gap: An agent has no published limit to respect and no response-header feedback to self-throttle against.
findings.recommendation: When the rate limiting from STATE-Q5 is implemented, emit X-RateLimit-Limit/Remaining/Reset and Retry-After on 429, and document the per-principal limits and the 429 response in openapi/orders.yaml.

findings.title: Sensitive Data Classification
findings.description: Stage A = Yes: the service persists customer order data in PostgreSQL (pg Pool in src/services/order-service.ts) with customer identifiers and financial amounts, and README.md states the order row holds customer PII. Stage B evaluated as follows. B1 (response scoping) does not fire: the only persisted entity is Order - id, customerId, status, totalCents - with no credential, card or secret field anywhere in the repository, and no password/token column exists to leak; sensitive-by-nature fields are absent rather than exposed. The projection is nonetheless loose - get() and create() return `SELECT *` / `RETURNING *` rows directly to the caller (src/services/order-service.ts), so any column added to the orders table later is exposed automatically.
