B2 (access-control differentiation) does not fire: src/auth.ts enforces distinct `orders:read` and `orders:write` role claims, so read and write access can be granted separately. B3 (formal classification metadata) fires: no classification tags in infra/ecs.yaml, no field-level sensitivity annotations in code, and no Macie or PII-detection tooling.
findings.gap: No machine-readable data classification exists, and API responses are built from wildcard projections rather than an explicit allowlist, so field-level exposure is governed by the table definition rather than by the API contract.
findings.recommendation: Replace `SELECT *` and `RETURNING *` with explicit column lists (and a response DTO) so new columns are never exposed by default, and add classification metadata - sensitivity tags on the data resources in infra/ecs.yaml and field-level annotations on the Order type - so agent-facing field scoping becomes enforceable rather than incidental.

findings.title: Data Quality Awareness
findings.description: No data quality measurement exists. The repository has a persistent data store (PostgreSQL via pg) but no data quality dashboard, no profiling report, no null-rate or duplicate-detection logic, and no freshness SLA. Searched src/services/order-service.ts (plain CRUD queries only), infra/ecs.yaml (no Glue DataBrew, Deequ or quality-check resources) and package.json (no data-quality tooling).
findings.gap: There is no completeness or accuracy baseline for the orders dataset, so the reliability of the data an agent reasons over is unmeasured.
findings.recommendation: If agents will make decisions from order data, add basic quality checks - null rates on customer_id/total_cents, duplicate-order detection, and a freshness metric - published as CloudWatch metrics alongside the business metrics in OBS-Q3.

findings.title: Semantically Meaningful Field Names
findings.description: Field names are semantically meaningful. The Order interface in src/services/order-service.ts uses id, customerId, status and totalCents - readable, unabbreviated camelCase with an explicitly unit-suffixed money field - and the database columns follow the matching snake_case convention (customer_id, total_cents). The status values are self-describing strings ('placed' | 'shipped' | 'cancelled' | 'refunded') rather than numeric or coded enums, and operationIds in openapi/orders.yaml (createOrder, getOrder, deleteOrder, refundOrder, cancelOrder) read directly as tool names. No legacy abbreviations or code-table lookups appear anywhere.
findings.gap: None of substance. The camelCase API shape and snake_case column names differ, and that mapping is implicit in the `SELECT *` pass-through rather than in an explicit mapper.
findings.recommendation: Preserve this convention as the schema grows, and make the camelCase/snake_case mapping explicit when the DTO projections from DATA-Q1 are introduced. No data dictionary is needed.

findings.title: Data Catalog / Metadata Layer
findings.description: No data catalog or metadata layer exists. There is no AWS Glue Data Catalog, DataHub, Collibra or Alation reference in infra/ecs.yaml, no data dictionary file, and no committed schema documentation - the only machine-readable description of the data is the Order TypeScript interface in src/services/order-service.ts, and openapi/orders.yaml declares no schemas. The node-pg-migrate migration directory declared in package.json does not exist, so the authoritative table definition is not in the repository at all.
findings.gap: The semantics of the orders dataset are documented only as source code, and the database schema is not represented in the repository, so teams building agent tools must read the implementation to learn the data shape.
findings.recommendation: Commit the node-pg-migrate migration files so the schema is in the repository, and add the entity schemas to openapi/orders.yaml. For a single-service surface this is sufficient - a full catalog product is unnecessary.

findings.title: Business Outcome Metrics
findings.description: No business metrics are published. infra/ecs.yaml configures the awslogs driver to /ecs/orders, which provides container log shipping and the default ECS/container infrastructure metrics, but there is no custom metric emission anywhere: no aws-sdk or CloudWatch client in package.json, no put_metric_data call or embedded-metric-format log line in src/routes.ts or src/services/order-service.ts, no dashboard definition and no business KPI alarm. Refund counts and values, cancellation rates and order-creation success rates are not measured.
findings.gap: Infrastructure telemetry exists but business outcomes do not, so the actual effect of agent-driven operations - how many refunds were issued, for what value, how many dispatches were recalled - would be invisible.
findings.recommendation: Emit custom metrics (or CloudWatch embedded metric format log lines) for order created, refund issued with value, and cancellation issued, dimensioned by principal so agent-driven activity is separable from human activity, and build a dashboard over them.

findings.title: Event Emission for State Changes
findings.description: The service is purely request/response. infra/template.yaml declares no SNS topic, EventBridge rule, SQS queue or Kafka integration, the DynamoDB LedgerTable has no StreamSpecification, and openapi/payments.yaml defines no webhook or callback. The only outbound signal on a state change is the CloudWatch metric ChargeCreated emitted in src/payments/handlers.py:57. RUNBOOK.md mentions replaying a failed webhook, but no webhook producer exists in this repository.
findings.gap: No event stream for charge or refund state changes, so a consumer that needs to react must poll getCharge.
findings.recommendation: If event-reactive agents are a target, enable StreamSpecification NEW_AND_OLD_IMAGES on LedgerTable and fan out ledger changes to EventBridge, then document the event schema alongside openapi/payments.yaml.

findings.title: Rate Limit Documentation and Headers
findings.description: Rate limits are neither documented nor surfaced. openapi/payments.yaml documents the Idempotency-Key and X-Correlation-Id headers and the 409/422/404 responses but declares no 429 response and no rate-limit headers; _response in src/payments/handlers.py:30-35 returns only Content-Type and X-Correlation-Id; infra/template.yaml configures no usage plan or stage throttling (see STATE-Q5).
findings.gap: An agent has no documented ceiling and no X-RateLimit-Remaining or Retry-After signal, so it cannot self-throttle and will discover limits only as unexplained failures.
findings.recommendation: Once stage throttling is configured, document the limits in the openapi/payments.yaml description, add a 429 response referencing the Error schema, and return Retry-After on throttled responses.

findings.title: Sensitive Data Classification
findings.description: Stage A is Yes — this is a payments ledger holding financial transaction records in DynamoDB. B1 is clear: the Charge response schema in openapi/payments.yaml exposes only id, amount, currency, status and created_at, and create_charge builds its result dict explicitly (src/payments/handlers.py:49-50) so the tokenized 'source' field persisted on the ledger item is never returned; the spec states a raw PAN is never accepted. B2 is clear: openapi/payments.yaml defines two distinct OAuth2 scopes, payments:read and payments:write, enforced per operation by _require_scope (src/payments/app.py:42-44). B3 is the only layer absent: no classification tags on the LedgerTable or ReceiptsBucket in infra/template.yaml, no field-level sensitivity annotations in src/payments/, and no Macie or equivalent PII detection integration.
findings.gap: No machine-readable data classification metadata. Protection today is correct but implicit in hand-built response DTOs, so a future field added to a result dict carries no classification signal to review against.
findings.recommendation: Tag LedgerTable and ReceiptsBucket in infra/template.yaml with a sensitivity label (for example DataClassification: pci-financial) and annotate the ledger item fields that must never be serialised, so response scoping is checkable rather than conventional.

findings.title: Data Quality Awareness
findings.description: Operational telemetry exists — a ChargeCreated business metric (src/payments/handlers.py:57), a payments-prod dashboard and throttle/5xx/idempotency-conflict alarms (RUNBOOK.md) — but no data-quality measure of the ledger itself: no completeness or null-rate monitoring, no duplicate-charge detection metric, no freshness SLA, and reconciliation is described in RUNBOOK.md as a manual GET per charge rather than a scored dataset check.
findings.gap: No quantified ledger quality or duplicate-rate signal, so an agent reasoning over charge history has no indicator of whether the dataset is complete.
findings.recommendation: Publish a duplicate-charge rate and a ledger reconciliation-delta metric to the Payments namespace and chart them on the payments-prod dashboard.

findings.title: Data Catalog / Metadata Layer
findings.description: API-level semantics are strong: openapi/payments.yaml carries described schemas for every entity and README.md plus RUNBOOK.md explain the architecture and operations. There is no catalog for the data layer itself — no Glue Data Catalog, DataHub or equivalent in infra/template.yaml, and the DynamoDB single-table design (pk/sk with charge#/idem# prefixes, used in src/payments/app.py and handlers.py) is documented only by convention in code, with no written key-schema or access-pattern reference.
findings.gap: The single-table key design and its access patterns are not described anywhere, so anyone building tooling directly against the ledger must infer the model from handler code.
findings.recommendation: Add a short data-model section to README.md documenting the pk/sk conventions, item types and access patterns of the LedgerTable, which is sufficient catalog for a single-table service.

cross_cutting_findings.title: Machine Identity Authentication
cross_cutting_findings.common_finding_summary: Ten services cannot authenticate a non-human caller. Credentials are a shared OS/file-share account (legacy-crm-desktop, legacy-timesheet-webforms), a session cookie issued only after an interactive human login (legacy-document-portal, legacy-helpdesk-tickets, legacy-storefront-rails, legacy-loan-calculator), no authentication at all (legacy-pricing-cgi, legacy-partner-soap, legacy-payroll-system), or an MCP gateway declared `AuthorizerType: NONE` with a self-asserted `--actor-id` (modern-claims-agent).
cross_cutting_findings.root_cause_pattern: Identity is modelled as a person, not a principal. There is no issuer in the portfolio that can mint a per-agent machine credential, so no service can attribute an action to a specific agent.

portfolio_remediation.immediate_action: Deploy a single portfolio identity plane (one Amazon Cognito user pool, or the existing pool from modern-payments-api promoted to shared) issuing OAuth2 client-credentials tokens with one app client per agent, and front the ten affected services with an API Gateway Cognito/Lambda authorizer.
portfolio_remediation.target_state: Every agent call carries a verifiable machine identity; `client_id` is available to every downstream authorization and audit decision.

cross_cutting_findings.title: Immutable Audit Logging
cross_cutting_findings.common_finding_summary: All ten write-enabled services fail to produce a tamper-evident record of agent writes. The modern services verify a JWT then discard the principal before writing (modern-catalog-graphql, modern-orders-service), log the principal on one path but not the refund path (modern-payments-api), or write to a mutable CloudWatch log group with no CloudTrail trail, log-file validation or S3 Object Lock (modern-claims-agent). The legacy services have no write log at all.
cross_cutting_findings.root_cause_pattern: Logging was built for debugging, not attribution. The authenticated principal is either unavailable (see AUTH-Q1) or available and dropped, and no log sink in the portfolio is immutable.

portfolio_remediation.immediate_action: Create one organization CloudTrail trail with log-file validation and an Object-Lock audit bucket, then patch each write path to emit a structured audit record containing principal, action, resource and correlation id — starting with modern-payments-api `refund_charge` and modern-claims-agent `settlement_writer`.
portfolio_remediation.target_state: Any agent write in the portfolio can be reconstructed end-to-end from an immutable log, with the acting principal named.

cross_cutting_findings.title: Data Residency and Sovereignty
cross_cutting_findings.common_finding_summary: Eight services can move regulated data out of its jurisdiction with no control: a .mdb on an unconstrained SMB share (legacy-crm-desktop), unrestricted bulk extracts (legacy-payroll-system, legacy-timesheet-webforms), partner SOAP responses with no residency tagging (legacy-partner-soap), and modern handlers whose export/read paths carry no region or residency predicate (modern-orders-service, modern-claims-agent).
cross_cutting_findings.root_cause_pattern: Residency was enforced implicitly by the fact that data never left the data centre. Once an agent can call the service, there is no code-level boundary preventing cross-jurisdiction export.

portfolio_remediation.immediate_action: Record the residency requirement per data store, pin agent-reachable stores and their replicas to the required Region, and add a residency predicate to every bulk-export and list operation.
portfolio_remediation.target_state: No agent-initiated read or export can relocate regulated data outside its declared jurisdiction.

cross_cutting_findings.title: Compensation and Rollback
cross_cutting_findings.common_finding_summary: Eight write-enabled services provide no compensation path for an incorrect agent write. There is no soft delete and no audit to reverse from (modern-orders-service `hardDelete`), no reversal for a written settlement (modern-claims-agent), no reversal of a committed payroll run (legacy-payroll-system), and no transaction boundary at all around multi-row writes (legacy-crm-desktop, legacy-storefront-rails, legacy-timesheet-webforms, legacy-loan-calculator, legacy-partner-soap).
cross_cutting_findings.root_cause_pattern: Correction was a human-operated database task, not a product feature. An agent that writes wrongly at machine speed therefore produces damage that cannot be undone programmatically.

portfolio_remediation.immediate_action: Adopt one portfolio pattern — append-only writes with soft delete plus a documented compensating operation per mutating endpoint — and implement it first where the write moves money or deletes records: modern-orders-service, modern-claims-agent, modern-payments-api, legacy-payroll-system.
portfolio_remediation.target_state: Every mutating agent operation has a documented, tested inverse that restores the prior state.

cross_cutting_findings.title: Sensitive Data Classification
cross_cutting_findings.common_finding_summary: Six write-enabled, data-handling services return unclassified sensitive data through agent-reachable paths: full customer records (legacy-crm-desktop), SSN and salary fields (legacy-payroll-system, legacy-timesheet-webforms), applicant financial data (legacy-loan-calculator), order and address data (legacy-storefront-rails), and claimant medical/settlement detail (modern-claims-agent). In each case sub-check B1 fired — API/query responses are not scoped to a classification — compounded in most by B3 (no formal classification metadata).
cross_cutting_findings.root_cause_pattern: No data classification scheme exists anywhere in the portfolio, so no response filter, retrieval filter or redaction rule can be expressed. Three further services (legacy-document-portal, legacy-helpdesk-tickets, modern-orders-service) resolve to RISK-SAFETY on the same question because only B2/B3 fired under read-only or scoped-write conditions.

portfolio_remediation.immediate_action: Publish one portfolio data-classification taxonomy (public / internal / confidential / regulated-PII) and tag the fields in the six affected stores; add response projection so unclassified or regulated fields are omitted from agent-facing payloads by default.
portfolio_remediation.target_state: Every agent-reachable field carries a classification, and the agent's identity determines which classifications it can receive.

cross_cutting_findings.title: Documented API Interface
cross_cutting_findings.common_finding_summary: Nine services expose no programmatic contract an agent can call. The integration surface is a GUI form (legacy-crm-desktop, legacy-timesheet-webforms), a server-rendered page or CGI binary (legacy-document-portal, legacy-pricing-cgi), a JCL/batch job (legacy-payroll-system), an undocumented SOAP endpoint (legacy-partner-soap), or HTML-only Rails/Python controllers (legacy-storefront-rails, legacy-helpdesk-tickets, legacy-loan-calculator). No OpenAPI, GraphQL schema, gRPC proto or AsyncAPI document exists in any of them.
cross_cutting_findings.root_cause_pattern: These are pre-API-era applications whose only consumer was a human at a screen or a scheduled batch window. There was never a machine-facing contract to document, so agent integration would require UI automation, direct database access, or screen scraping — all brittle and unauditable.

portfolio_remediation.immediate_action: Stand up a shared API facade layer (Amazon API Gateway + per-service adapter) and publish an OpenAPI 3 document per service, starting with the three services that already have a parseable request/response shape (legacy-partner-soap, legacy-pricing-cgi, legacy-document-portal).
portfolio_remediation.target_state: Every agent-facing service is reachable only through a versioned, documented HTTP contract; no agent touches a form, a CGI binary, a .mdb file or a batch queue.

cross_cutting_findings.title: Idempotent Write Operations
cross_cutting_findings.common_finding_summary: Eight write-enabled services accept repeated writes with no idempotency key and no dedupe window: INSERT-on-click (legacy-crm-desktop), re-runnable batch posting (legacy-payroll-system), non-idempotent SOAP operations (legacy-partner-soap), and modern handlers that accept a POST with no Idempotency-Key header (modern-orders-service, modern-claims-agent).
cross_cutting_findings.root_cause_pattern: Request de-duplication was delegated to a human who would not click twice. Machine-speed retry — the normal agent failure mode — therefore produces duplicate orders, duplicate settlements and duplicate payroll postings.

portfolio_remediation.immediate_action: Define one portfolio-wide idempotency contract (client-supplied `Idempotency-Key` header, 24h dedupe window, stored request fingerprint) and implement it first on the money-moving paths: modern-orders-service, modern-claims-agent, legacy-payroll-system.
portfolio_remediation.target_state: Every mutating operation is safe to retry; a replayed agent request returns the original result rather than creating a second side effect.

cross_cutting_findings.title: Action-Level Authorization
cross_cutting_findings.common_finding_summary: Authorization, where present, is coarse: a role claim checked once at the edge (modern-orders-service `requireRole`) or a session flag, with no per-action or per-resource decision inside the service.
cross_cutting_findings.root_cause_pattern: Policy decision point in front of the agent surface (Cedar / AgentCore Policy / API Gateway authorizer returning an action-scoped policy) rather than role checks scattered in handlers.

portfolio_remediation.immediate_action: Introduce action-level authorization as a shared middleware contract: every mutating handler asks a policy engine `can this principal perform this action on this resource?` before executing.
portfolio_remediation.target_state: Introduce action-level authorization as a shared middleware contract: every mutating handler asks a policy engine `can this principal perform this action on this resource?` before executing.

cross_cutting_findings.compensating_controls: Policy decision point in front of the agent surface (Cedar / AgentCore Policy / API Gateway authorizer returning an action-scoped policy) rather than role checks scattered in handlers.
cross_cutting_findings.portfolio_recommendation: Introduce action-level authorization as a shared middleware contract: every mutating handler asks a policy engine `can this principal perform this action on this resource?` before executing.

cross_cutting_findings.title: Agent Identity Suspension
cross_cutting_findings.common_finding_summary: No service can suspend a single agent. There are no per-agent credentials to disable (modern-claims-agent), token validation is stateless with no denylist or introspection (modern-orders-service), and no app-client or key-revocation procedure is documented (modern-payments-api).
cross_cutting_findings.root_cause_pattern: Per-agent app clients that can be disabled individually; a token denylist or introspection check on the hot path; a documented portfolio kill-switch runbook.

portfolio_remediation.immediate_action: Give every agent its own revocable credential at the shared identity plane and document one portfolio-wide revocation runbook, so a misbehaving agent can be stopped without taking down the service.
portfolio_remediation.target_state: Give every agent its own revocable credential at the shared identity plane and document one portfolio-wide revocation runbook, so a misbehaving agent can be stopped without taking down the service.

cross_cutting_findings.compensating_controls: Per-agent app clients that can be disabled individually; a token denylist or introspection check on the hot path; a documented portfolio kill-switch runbook.
cross_cutting_findings.portfolio_recommendation: Give every agent its own revocable credential at the shared identity plane and document one portfolio-wide revocation runbook, so a misbehaving agent can be stopped without taking down the service.

cross_cutting_findings.title: Rate Limiting and Throttling
cross_cutting_findings.common_finding_summary: Rate limiting is absent at every layer: no API Gateway usage plan or throttle settings, no WAF association, no application middleware, and no reserved concurrency (modern-catalog-graphql also has no GraphQL depth or complexity limit).
cross_cutting_findings.root_cause_pattern: API Gateway throttling and usage plans per agent client, AWS WAF rate-based rules at the perimeter, reserved concurrency on agent-invoked functions.

portfolio_remediation.immediate_action: Apply a portfolio-level rate-limit baseline — WAF rate-based rules at the edge plus per-client API Gateway usage plans — before any agent is pointed at these services at volume.
portfolio_remediation.target_state: Apply a portfolio-level rate-limit baseline — WAF rate-based rules at the edge plus per-client API Gateway usage plans — before any agent is pointed at these services at volume.

cross_cutting_findings.compensating_controls: API Gateway throttling and usage plans per agent client, AWS WAF rate-based rules at the perimeter, reserved concurrency on agent-invoked functions.
cross_cutting_findings.portfolio_recommendation: Apply a portfolio-level rate-limit baseline — WAF rate-based rules at the edge plus per-client API Gateway usage plans — before any agent is pointed at these services at volume.

cross_cutting_findings.title: Scoped Permissions (Least Privilege)
cross_cutting_findings.common_finding_summary: Agent callers inherit the full privilege of the application identity — a shared DB account, a root CGI process, or a single IAM/execution role covering every operation (modern-claims-agent's `claims-agent-execution` is assumed by both runtime and tool Lambda).
cross_cutting_findings.root_cause_pattern: Per-agent app clients with scope claims at the shared identity plane; resource-scoped IAM roles per tool; IAM Access Analyzer run continuously over the agent roles.

portfolio_remediation.immediate_action: Define a portfolio scope vocabulary (one scope per agent-callable operation) at the shared IdP and enforce it in each service's authorizer, so no agent holds a privilege it does not need.
portfolio_remediation.target_state: Define a portfolio scope vocabulary (one scope per agent-callable operation) at the shared IdP and enforce it in each service's authorizer, so no agent holds a privilege it does not need.

cross_cutting_findings.compensating_controls: Per-agent app clients with scope claims at the shared identity plane; resource-scoped IAM roles per tool; IAM Access Analyzer run continuously over the agent roles.
cross_cutting_findings.portfolio_recommendation: Define a portfolio scope vocabulary (one scope per agent-callable operation) at the shared IdP and enforce it in each service's authorizer, so no agent holds a privilege it does not need.

cross_cutting_findings.title: PII Redaction in Logs
cross_cutting_findings.common_finding_summary: Sensitive values reach logs unredacted — request bodies, query parameters, claimant and employee records are written to log sinks with no masking or data-protection policy.
cross_cutting_findings.root_cause_pattern: CloudWatch Logs data-protection policies with managed PII identifiers; a shared redaction helper applied before any log write; guardrail sensitive-information filters on model paths.

portfolio_remediation.immediate_action: Apply a CloudWatch Logs data-protection policy to every agent-path log group and add a shared redaction utility to the logging layer, so agent-driven traffic volume does not multiply PII exposure.
portfolio_remediation.target_state: Apply a CloudWatch Logs data-protection policy to every agent-path log group and add a shared redaction utility to the logging layer, so agent-driven traffic volume does not multiply PII exposure.

cross_cutting_findings.compensating_controls: CloudWatch Logs data-protection policies with managed PII identifiers; a shared redaction helper applied before any log write; guardrail sensitive-information filters on model paths.
cross_cutting_findings.portfolio_recommendation: Apply a CloudWatch Logs data-protection policy to every agent-path log group and add a shared redaction utility to the logging layer, so agent-driven traffic volume does not multiply PII exposure.

cross_cutting_findings.title: Configurable Approval Gates
cross_cutting_findings.common_finding_summary: No service has a configurable approval gate. Thresholds that would warrant human review — settlement amount, refund value, payroll run, bulk delete — are not expressed anywhere in code or config.
cross_cutting_findings.root_cause_pattern: Threshold-driven approval workflow (Step Functions callback pattern or equivalent) in front of high-impact operations; thresholds in configuration, not code.

portfolio_remediation.immediate_action: Define portfolio approval thresholds per operation class and implement one shared approval gate component, wired first into the money-moving and bulk-mutation paths.
portfolio_remediation.target_state: Define portfolio approval thresholds per operation class and implement one shared approval gate component, wired first into the money-moving and bulk-mutation paths.

cross_cutting_findings.compensating_controls: Threshold-driven approval workflow (Step Functions callback pattern or equivalent) in front of high-impact operations; thresholds in configuration, not code.
cross_cutting_findings.portfolio_recommendation: Define portfolio approval thresholds per operation class and implement one shared approval gate component, wired first into the money-moving and bulk-mutation paths.

cross_cutting_findings.title: Concurrency Controls
cross_cutting_findings.common_finding_summary: No concurrency control exists on agent-writable state: no optimistic version checks, no conditional writes, no row locking. Two concurrent agent writes silently last-write-wins.
cross_cutting_findings.root_cause_pattern: DynamoDB condition expressions / `ConditionCheck`, SQL optimistic locking with a version column, and ETag/If-Match on HTTP mutations.

portfolio_remediation.immediate_action: Require an optimistic-concurrency token (version column or ETag) on every agent-writable resource, so concurrent agent writes fail loudly rather than overwriting each other.
portfolio_remediation.target_state: Require an optimistic-concurrency token (version column or ETag) on every agent-writable resource, so concurrent agent writes fail loudly rather than overwriting each other.

cross_cutting_findings.compensating_controls: DynamoDB condition expressions / `ConditionCheck`, SQL optimistic locking with a version column, and ETag/If-Match on HTTP mutations.
cross_cutting_findings.portfolio_recommendation: Require an optimistic-concurrency token (version column or ETag) on every agent-writable resource, so concurrent agent writes fail loudly rather than overwriting each other.

cross_cutting_findings.title: Blast Radius and Transaction Limits
cross_cutting_findings.common_finding_summary: Nothing bounds the blast radius of a single agent operation: no row caps on bulk updates, no per-transaction value limits, no maximum batch size.
cross_cutting_findings.root_cause_pattern: Hard server-side caps on batch size and transaction value; a daily per-agent operation budget; mandatory pagination on list/bulk endpoints.

portfolio_remediation.immediate_action: Set server-side blast-radius caps (max rows per mutation, max value per transaction, max operations per agent per day) as a portfolio default rather than a per-service choice.
portfolio_remediation.target_state: Set server-side blast-radius caps (max rows per mutation, max value per transaction, max operations per agent per day) as a portfolio default rather than a per-service choice.

cross_cutting_findings.compensating_controls: Hard server-side caps on batch size and transaction value; a daily per-agent operation budget; mandatory pagination on list/bulk endpoints.
cross_cutting_findings.portfolio_recommendation: Set server-side blast-radius caps (max rows per mutation, max value per transaction, max operations per agent per day) as a portfolio default rather than a per-service choice.

cross_cutting_findings.title: Identity Propagation and Delegation
cross_cutting_findings.common_finding_summary: When an agent acts for a user, the user's identity is not propagated. Services either run entirely as the application principal or forward no on-behalf-of context, so downstream decisions and logs cannot see the human.
cross_cutting_findings.root_cause_pattern: On-behalf-of token exchange at the identity plane; an `act` / delegation claim carried on every agent call and surfaced into audit records.

portfolio_remediation.immediate_action: Standardise one delegation claim across the portfolio and require it on any agent call made on a user's behalf; never forward the user's raw token to a downstream tool.
portfolio_remediation.target_state: Standardise one delegation claim across the portfolio and require it on any agent call made on a user's behalf; never forward the user's raw token to a downstream tool.

cross_cutting_findings.compensating_controls: On-behalf-of token exchange at the identity plane; an `act` / delegation claim carried on every agent call and surfaced into audit records.
cross_cutting_findings.portfolio_recommendation: Standardise one delegation claim across the portfolio and require it on any agent call made on a user's behalf; never forward the user's raw token to a downstream tool.

cross_cutting_findings.title: Credential Management
cross_cutting_findings.common_finding_summary: Credentials are embedded or statically configured: connection strings in source and config (legacy services), long-lived static secrets, and no rotation anywhere. No service reads its credential from a managed secret store at runtime.
cross_cutting_findings.root_cause_pattern: AWS Secrets Manager with automatic rotation; short-lived tokens from the shared IdP instead of static keys; no plaintext credential in any repository.

portfolio_remediation.immediate_action: Move every agent-path credential into Secrets Manager with rotation enabled, and replace static service keys with short-lived client-credentials tokens.
portfolio_remediation.target_state: Move every agent-path credential into Secrets Manager with rotation enabled, and replace static service keys with short-lived client-credentials tokens.

cross_cutting_findings.compensating_controls: AWS Secrets Manager with automatic rotation; short-lived tokens from the shared IdP instead of static keys; no plaintext credential in any repository.
cross_cutting_findings.portfolio_recommendation: Move every agent-path credential into Secrets Manager with rotation enabled, and replace static service keys with short-lived client-credentials tokens.

cross_cutting_findings.title: Draft/Pending State
cross_cutting_findings.common_finding_summary: Mutating operations commit immediately. There is no draft, pending or proposed state an agent could write into for a human to confirm — the write is the decision.
cross_cutting_findings.root_cause_pattern: A `pending` status plus a confirm/reject transition on mutating resources; agent writes land in pending by default.

portfolio_remediation.immediate_action: Add a draft/pending state to every mutating agent-callable resource and make `pending` the default outcome of an agent-initiated write during pilot.
portfolio_remediation.target_state: Add a draft/pending state to every mutating agent-callable resource and make `pending` the default outcome of an agent-initiated write during pilot.

cross_cutting_findings.compensating_controls: A `pending` status plus a confirm/reject transition on mutating resources; agent writes land in pending by default.

cross_cutting_findings.title: Circuit Breakers and Resilience
cross_cutting_findings.common_finding_summary: Calls to dependencies have no timeout, retry budget or circuit breaker, so a slow dependency becomes an unbounded queue of agent-initiated work.
cross_cutting_findings.root_cause_pattern: Shared client wrapper with timeouts, bounded retries with jitter, and a circuit breaker; bulkheads/reserved concurrency per caller class.

portfolio_remediation.immediate_action: Publish one resilience client wrapper (timeout + bounded retry + breaker) and require its use on every outbound call on an agent-reachable path.
portfolio_remediation.target_state: Publish one resilience client wrapper (timeout + bounded retry + breaker) and require its use on every outbound call on an agent-reachable path.

cross_cutting_findings.compensating_controls: Shared client wrapper with timeouts, bounded retries with jitter, and a circuit breaker; bulkheads/reserved concurrency per caller class.
cross_cutting_findings.portfolio_recommendation: Publish one resilience client wrapper (timeout + bounded retry + breaker) and require its use on every outbound call on an agent-reachable path.

cross_cutting_findings.title: Schema Versioning and API Contracts
cross_cutting_findings.common_finding_summary: Every service in the portfolio lacks schema versioning and a contract-change policy. Breaking changes are shipped without a version bump, deprecation window or consumer notification.
cross_cutting_findings.root_cause_pattern: Explicit API/schema version in the path or media type; contract tests in CI; a published deprecation policy.

portfolio_remediation.immediate_action: Publish one portfolio API-versioning and deprecation policy and enforce it with contract tests, so an agent's tool definitions do not silently break.
portfolio_remediation.target_state: Publish one portfolio API-versioning and deprecation policy and enforce it with contract tests, so an agent's tool definitions do not silently break.

cross_cutting_findings.compensating_controls: Explicit API/schema version in the path or media type; contract tests in CI; a published deprecation policy.
cross_cutting_findings.portfolio_recommendation: Publish one portfolio API-versioning and deprecation policy and enforce it with contract tests, so an agent's tool definitions do not silently break.

cross_cutting_findings.title: Temporal Metadata and Freshness
cross_cutting_findings.common_finding_summary: Responses carry no temporal metadata — no `as_of`, `last_modified` or freshness indicator — so an agent cannot tell whether it is reasoning over current or stale data. Nightly batch sync makes this acute for legacy-crm-desktop and legacy-payroll-system.
cross_cutting_findings.root_cause_pattern: A standard `as_of` / `last_modified` field on every agent-facing read response, plus documented staleness bounds per data source.

portfolio_remediation.immediate_action: Add a uniform freshness field to agent-facing responses and document the staleness bound of each backing store, especially where a nightly batch sits between the source and the agent.
portfolio_remediation.target_state: Add a uniform freshness field to agent-facing responses and document the staleness bound of each backing store, especially where a nightly batch sits between the source and the agent.

cross_cutting_findings.compensating_controls: A standard `as_of` / `last_modified` field on every agent-facing read response, plus documented staleness bounds per data source.
cross_cutting_findings.portfolio_recommendation: Add a uniform freshness field to agent-facing responses and document the staleness bound of each backing store, especially where a nightly batch sits between the source and the agent.

cross_cutting_findings.title: API Test Coverage
cross_cutting_findings.common_finding_summary: API test coverage of agent-reachable paths is minimal to nonexistent; the mutating paths that most need coverage are the least tested.
cross_cutting_findings.root_cause_pattern: Integration tests per agent-callable operation, including idempotency, authorization-denial and rollback cases, enforced by a coverage gate.

portfolio_remediation.immediate_action: Require integration test coverage of every agent-callable operation — including negative authorization and retry cases — before that operation is exposed to an agent.
portfolio_remediation.target_state: Require integration test coverage of every agent-callable operation — including negative authorization and retry cases — before that operation is exposed to an agent.

cross_cutting_findings.compensating_controls: Integration tests per agent-callable operation, including idempotency, authorization-denial and rollback cases, enforced by a coverage gate.
cross_cutting_findings.portfolio_recommendation: Require integration test coverage of every agent-callable operation — including negative authorization and retry cases — before that operation is exposed to an agent.

cross_cutting_findings.title: Sandbox/Staging Environment
cross_cutting_findings.common_finding_summary: There is no sandbox or staging environment where agent behaviour can be rehearsed. Agents would have to be trialled against production data.
cross_cutting_findings.root_cause_pattern: A production-like staging environment with synthetic or masked data, and agent-specific smoke suites run there first.

portfolio_remediation.immediate_action: Provide one shared staging environment with masked data as the mandatory first target for any new agent integration.
portfolio_remediation.target_state: Provide one shared staging environment with masked data as the mandatory first target for any new agent integration.

cross_cutting_findings.compensating_controls: A production-like staging environment with synthetic or masked data, and agent-specific smoke suites run there first.
cross_cutting_findings.portfolio_recommendation: Provide one shared staging environment with masked data as the mandatory first target for any new agent integration.

cross_cutting_findings.title: Distributed Tracing and Structured Logging
cross_cutting_findings.common_finding_summary: Structured logging and distributed tracing are missing or half-present — X-Ray enabled with no structured logs (modern-catalog-graphql), a documented pino/CloudWatch stack that is not actually installed (modern-orders-service), and plain-text `logging.basicConfig` with no correlation id (modern-claims-agent). No trace context propagates between services.
cross_cutting_findings.root_cause_pattern: A shared structured-logging library emitting a correlation id, trace-context propagation (`traceparent` / X-Ray) on every hop, and CloudWatch Transaction Search enabled per account.

portfolio_remediation.immediate_action: Mandate one structured-logging format with a propagated correlation id across the portfolio, and enable transaction search so a single agent session can be traced end to end.
portfolio_remediation.target_state: Mandate one structured-logging format with a propagated correlation id across the portfolio, and enable transaction search so a single agent session can be traced end to end.

cross_cutting_findings.compensating_controls: A shared structured-logging library emitting a correlation id, trace-context propagation (`traceparent` / X-Ray) on every hop, and CloudWatch Transaction Search enabled per account.
cross_cutting_findings.portfolio_recommendation: Mandate one structured-logging format with a propagated correlation id across the portfolio, and enable transaction search so a single agent session can be traced end to end.

cross_cutting_findings.title: Alerting on Error Rates and Latency
cross_cutting_findings.common_finding_summary: No service alerts on agent-relevant signals: no error-rate, latency or throughput alarms, and no anomaly detection on call volume.
cross_cutting_findings.root_cause_pattern: CloudWatch alarms on error rate, p99 latency and invocation volume per agent client, with anomaly detection on agent traffic.

portfolio_remediation.immediate_action: Define a standard agent-traffic alarm set (error rate, latency, volume anomaly) and apply it to every agent-facing service, so a runaway agent is detected in minutes.
portfolio_remediation.target_state: Define a standard agent-traffic alarm set (error rate, latency, volume anomaly) and apply it to every agent-facing service, so a runaway agent is detected in minutes.

cross_cutting_findings.compensating_controls: CloudWatch alarms on error rate, p99 latency and invocation volume per agent client, with anomaly detection on agent traffic.
cross_cutting_findings.portfolio_recommendation: Define a standard agent-traffic alarm set (error rate, latency, volume anomaly) and apply it to every agent-facing service, so a runaway agent is detected in minutes.

cross_cutting_findings.title: Input Validation and Schema Enforcement
cross_cutting_findings.common_finding_summary: Input validation is absent or partial: free-text parameters interpolated into SQL and shell commands in the legacy services, and no schema enforcement on request bodies in the modern ones.
cross_cutting_findings.root_cause_pattern: Request-schema validation at the edge (API Gateway models / JSON Schema) plus parameterised queries everywhere.

portfolio_remediation.immediate_action: Enforce request-schema validation at the perimeter for every agent-facing endpoint and eliminate string-interpolated query construction on those paths.
portfolio_remediation.target_state: Enforce request-schema validation at the perimeter for every agent-facing endpoint and eliminate string-interpolated query construction on those paths.

cross_cutting_findings.compensating_controls: Request-schema validation at the edge (API Gateway models / JSON Schema) plus parameterised queries everywhere.
cross_cutting_findings.portfolio_recommendation: Enforce request-schema validation at the perimeter for every agent-facing endpoint and eliminate string-interpolated query construction on those paths.

cross_cutting_findings.title: Infrastructure Governance for Agent-Facing Surface
cross_cutting_findings.common_finding_summary: The agent-facing surface is not governed by infrastructure as code, or the IaC omits the agent-relevant controls (authorizers, throttles, log retention). Several legacy services are hand-configured entirely.
cross_cutting_findings.root_cause_pattern: All agent-facing infrastructure in IaC, with AWS Config rules and conformance packs detecting drift centrally.

portfolio_remediation.immediate_action: Bring the agent-facing perimeter of every service under IaC and add Config rules for the agent-relevant controls, so a throttle or authorizer cannot be removed silently.
portfolio_remediation.target_state: Bring the agent-facing perimeter of every service under IaC and add Config rules for the agent-relevant controls, so a throttle or authorizer cannot be removed silently.

cross_cutting_findings.compensating_controls: All agent-facing infrastructure in IaC, with AWS Config rules and conformance packs detecting drift centrally.
cross_cutting_findings.portfolio_recommendation: Bring the agent-facing perimeter of every service under IaC and add Config rules for the agent-relevant controls, so a throttle or authorizer cannot be removed silently.

cross_cutting_findings.title: CI/CD with API Contract Testing
cross_cutting_findings.common_finding_summary: CI/CD either does not exist or does not test the API contract. No pipeline in the portfolio fails a build on a breaking contract change.
cross_cutting_findings.root_cause_pattern: Contract tests (provider verification) as a required pipeline stage; spec linting; automated deployment gates.

portfolio_remediation.immediate_action: Add API contract testing as a mandatory pipeline stage across the portfolio, so the agent-facing contract is verified on every change.
portfolio_remediation.target_state: Add API contract testing as a mandatory pipeline stage across the portfolio, so the agent-facing contract is verified on every change.

cross_cutting_findings.compensating_controls: Contract tests (provider verification) as a required pipeline stage; spec linting; automated deployment gates.
cross_cutting_findings.portfolio_recommendation: Add API contract testing as a mandatory pipeline stage across the portfolio, so the agent-facing contract is verified on every change.

cross_cutting_findings.title: Structured Error Responses
cross_cutting_findings.common_finding_summary: Errors are unstructured: HTML error pages, stack traces, CGI text output, or 500s with free-text bodies. There is no machine-parseable error code an agent can branch on.
cross_cutting_findings.root_cause_pattern: A shared RFC 9457 problem-details error envelope with a stable `type` code per failure class, and a retryability hint.

portfolio_remediation.immediate_action: Adopt one portfolio error envelope with stable error codes and an explicit retryable flag, so an agent can distinguish a permanent rejection from a transient fault.
portfolio_remediation.target_state: Adopt one portfolio error envelope with stable error codes and an explicit retryable flag, so an agent can distinguish a permanent rejection from a transient fault.

cross_cutting_findings.compensating_controls: A shared RFC 9457 problem-details error envelope with a stable `type` code per failure class, and a retryability hint.
cross_cutting_findings.portfolio_recommendation: Adopt one portfolio error envelope with stable error codes and an explicit retryable flag, so an agent can distinguish a permanent rejection from a transient fault.

cross_cutting_findings.title: Rollback Capability
cross_cutting_findings.common_finding_summary: Rollback is manual or unavailable — no versioned deployment artefact, no documented rollback procedure, and in the legacy services no way to revert a hand-distributed binary or batch change.
cross_cutting_findings.root_cause_pattern: Versioned immutable artefacts, automated rollback (Lambda aliases / ECS task-definition revisions / CodeDeploy), and rollback rehearsal.

portfolio_remediation.immediate_action: Standardise versioned immutable deployments with an automated, rehearsed rollback path for every agent-facing service.
portfolio_remediation.target_state: Standardise versioned immutable deployments with an automated, rehearsed rollback path for every agent-facing service.

cross_cutting_findings.compensating_controls: Versioned immutable artefacts, automated rollback (Lambda aliases / ECS task-definition revisions / CodeDeploy), and rollback rehearsal.
cross_cutting_findings.portfolio_recommendation: Standardise versioned immutable deployments with an automated, rehearsed rollback path for every agent-facing service.

cross_cutting_findings.title: Encryption at Rest for Agent-Accessible Data
cross_cutting_findings.common_finding_summary: Encryption at rest for agent-accessible data is unconfirmed or absent: a file-share .mdb, unencrypted legacy volumes, and modern stores relying on defaults with no customer-managed key.
cross_cutting_findings.root_cause_pattern: KMS customer-managed keys on agent-accessible stores, with key policies restricting the agent roles and CloudTrail data events on key use.

portfolio_remediation.immediate_action: Enable KMS encryption with customer-managed keys on every agent-accessible store and record key usage, so agent data access is both protected and attributable.
portfolio_remediation.target_state: Enable KMS encryption with customer-managed keys on every agent-accessible store and record key usage, so agent data access is both protected and attributable.

cross_cutting_findings.compensating_controls: KMS customer-managed keys on agent-accessible stores, with key policies restricting the agent roles and CloudTrail data events on key use.
cross_cutting_findings.portfolio_recommendation: Enable KMS encryption with customer-managed keys on every agent-accessible store and record key usage, so agent data access is both protected and attributable.

cross_cutting_findings.title: Machine-Readable API Specification
cross_cutting_findings.common_finding_summary: No machine-readable specification exists for the agent-facing surface, or the published spec does not match the implementation (modern-payments-api's `openapi/payments.yaml` omits the limits and error shapes the code produces).
cross_cutting_findings.root_cause_pattern: Spec-first development with the specification generated from or validated against the implementation in CI.

portfolio_remediation.immediate_action: Require a committed OpenAPI/GraphQL schema per agent-facing service and validate it against the running implementation in CI, so agent tool definitions can be generated rather than hand-written.
portfolio_remediation.target_state: Require a committed OpenAPI/GraphQL schema per agent-facing service and validate it against the running implementation in CI, so agent tool definitions can be generated rather than hand-written.

cross_cutting_findings.compensating_controls: Spec-first development with the specification generated from or validated against the implementation in CI.
cross_cutting_findings.portfolio_recommendation: Require a committed OpenAPI/GraphQL schema per agent-facing service and validate it against the running implementation in CI, so agent tool definitions can be generated rather than hand-written.

cross_cutting_findings.title: Queryable Current State
cross_cutting_findings.common_finding_summary: Current state is not cleanly queryable — state is implicit in UI flow, derived during batch processing, or spread across tables with no single read model an agent can consult before acting.
cross_cutting_findings.root_cause_pattern: An explicit read model or status endpoint per workflow, so an agent can establish state before deciding.

portfolio_remediation.immediate_action: Expose an explicit state/status read model for each agent-relevant workflow rather than requiring the caller to infer state.
portfolio_remediation.target_state: Expose an explicit state/status read model for each agent-relevant workflow rather than requiring the caller to infer state.

cross_cutting_findings.compensating_controls: An explicit read model or status endpoint per workflow, so an agent can establish state before deciding.
cross_cutting_findings.portfolio_recommendation: Expose an explicit state/status read model for each agent-relevant workflow rather than requiring the caller to infer state.

cross_cutting_findings.title: Selective Query Support
cross_cutting_findings.common_finding_summary: Query support is all-or-nothing: no field selection, filtering or pagination, so an agent must fetch whole collections to answer narrow questions.
cross_cutting_findings.root_cause_pattern: Mandatory pagination with server-side caps; field projection; filter parameters validated against a schema.

portfolio_remediation.immediate_action: Add pagination and field projection to agent-facing read endpoints, with a server-enforced maximum page size.
portfolio_remediation.target_state: Add pagination and field projection to agent-facing read endpoints, with a server-enforced maximum page size.

cross_cutting_findings.compensating_controls: Mandatory pagination with server-side caps; field projection; filter parameters validated against a schema.
cross_cutting_findings.portfolio_recommendation: Add pagination and field projection to agent-facing read endpoints, with a server-enforced maximum page size.

cross_cutting_findings.title: Graceful Degradation Signaling
cross_cutting_findings.common_finding_summary: Degraded operation is not signalled. When a dependency fails the service either fails opaquely or silently returns partial data, giving an agent no way to detect reduced capability.
cross_cutting_findings.root_cause_pattern: Health and degradation endpoints plus explicit partial-result markers in responses.

portfolio_remediation.immediate_action: Signal degradation explicitly — a health endpoint and a partial-result marker — so an agent can back off instead of acting on incomplete data.
portfolio_remediation.target_state: Signal degradation explicitly — a health endpoint and a partial-result marker — so an agent can back off instead of acting on incomplete data.

cross_cutting_findings.compensating_controls: Health and degradation endpoints plus explicit partial-result markers in responses.
cross_cutting_findings.portfolio_recommendation: Signal degradation explicitly — a health endpoint and a partial-result marker — so an agent can back off instead of acting on incomplete data.

cross_cutting_findings.title: Asynchronous Operation Support
cross_cutting_findings.common_finding_summary: Long-running operations provide no asynchronous pattern — no job id, no status endpoint, no callback — so a caller can only block or poll blindly.
cross_cutting_findings.root_cause_pattern: 202-plus-status-resource pattern with a job id; event-driven completion notification.

portfolio_remediation.immediate_action: Where an operation can exceed the agent's call timeout, return a job id and expose a status resource rather than holding the connection open.
portfolio_remediation.target_state: Where an operation can exceed the agent's call timeout, return a job id and expose a status resource rather than holding the connection open.

cross_cutting_findings.compensating_controls: 202-plus-status-resource pattern with a job id; event-driven completion notification.
cross_cutting_findings.portfolio_recommendation: Where an operation can exceed the agent's call timeout, return a job id and expose a status resource rather than holding the connection open.

items.common_finding_summary: Ten services cannot authenticate a non-human caller. Credentials are a shared OS/file-share account (legacy-crm-desktop, legacy-timesheet-webforms), a session cookie issued only after an interactive human login (legacy-document-portal, legacy-helpdesk-tickets, legacy-storefront-rails, legacy-loan-calculator), no authentication at all (legacy-pricing-cgi, legacy-partner-soap, legacy-payroll-system), or an MCP gateway declared `AuthorizerType: NONE` with a self-asserted `--actor-id` (modern-claims-agent).
items.root_cause_pattern: Identity is modelled as a person, not a principal. There is no issuer in the portfolio that can mint a per-agent machine credential, so no service can attribute an action to a specific agent.
items.remediation: Deploy a single portfolio identity plane (one Amazon Cognito user pool, or the existing pool from modern-payments-api promoted to shared) issuing OAuth2 client-credentials tokens with one app client per agent, and front the ten affected services with an API Gateway Cognito/Lambda authorizer.

remediation_detail.immediate_action: Deploy a single portfolio identity plane (one Amazon Cognito user pool, or the existing pool from modern-payments-api promoted to shared) issuing OAuth2 client-credentials tokens with one app client per agent, and front the ten affected services with an API Gateway Cognito/Lambda authorizer.
remediation_detail.target_state: Every agent call carries a verifiable machine identity; `client_id` is available to every downstream authorization and audit decision.

affected_services.resolution_reasoning: No machine identity, no principal authentication, and no trustworthy principal attribution. Every caller is indistinguishable at the data layer, so no downstream authorization or audit decision can be relied upon.

There is no way for a non-human caller to authenticate as itself, and therefore no authenticated principal that could be attributed to an agent in any log. An agent could only integrate by replaying a human user's session cookie, which destroys attribution and inherits that human's full access.

There is no machine identity an agent could use, and no mechanism to attribute a call to a specific non-human principal. Every downstream authorization and audit decision (AUTH-Q2, AUTH-Q3, AUTH-Q6) is therefore unenforceable.
No machine identity mechanism and no principal attribution for non-human callers; an agent could only call the system by impersonating a loan officer's interactive session.

No verifiable machine identity. The authenticated principal is self-asserted by the caller, and even the documented mechanism (plaintext PasswordText over plain HTTP) cannot be used to attribute an agent identity safely. Every downstream authorization and audit decision is therefore unenforceable.

There is no way to issue a distinct machine/agent principal, and no principal attribution available to downstream authorization or audit. Every invocation looks like the same shared `payroll` account or the submitting RACF user.

There is no mechanism to identify a calling principal, so no agent call can be attributed, scoped, rate-limited per identity, or revoked. Every downstream authorization and audit control is unimplementable without this.

The system cannot authenticate a non-human caller or attribute a request to a specific agent principal. Every downstream authorization and audit decision (AUTH-Q2, AUTH-Q3, AUTH-Q6) is therefore unenforceable.
No machine principal can authenticate and no non-human caller can be attributed.
No authenticated machine identity and no principal attribution on the agent-facing surface.

items.common_finding_summary: All ten write-enabled services fail to produce a tamper-evident record of agent writes. The modern services verify a JWT then discard the principal before writing (modern-catalog-graphql, modern-orders-service), log the principal on one path but not the refund path (modern-payments-api), or write to a mutable CloudWatch log group with no CloudTrail trail, log-file validation or S3 Object Lock (modern-claims-agent). The legacy services have no write log at all.
items.root_cause_pattern: Logging was built for debugging, not attribution. The authenticated principal is either unavailable (see AUTH-Q1) or available and dropped, and no log sink in the portfolio is immutable.
items.remediation: Create one organization CloudTrail trail with log-file validation and an Object-Lock audit bucket, then patch each write path to emit a structured audit record containing principal, action, resource and correlation id — starting with modern-payments-api `refund_charge` and modern-claims-agent `settlement_writer`.

remediation_detail.immediate_action: Create one organization CloudTrail trail with log-file validation and an Object-Lock audit bucket, then patch each write path to emit a structured audit record containing principal, action, resource and correlation id — starting with modern-payments-api `refund_charge` and modern-claims-agent `settlement_writer`.
remediation_detail.target_state: Any agent write in the portfolio can be reconstructed end-to-end from an immutable log, with the acting principal named.

items.common_finding_summary: Eight services can move regulated data out of its jurisdiction with no control: a .mdb on an unconstrained SMB share (legacy-crm-desktop), unrestricted bulk extracts (legacy-payroll-system, legacy-timesheet-webforms), partner SOAP responses with no residency tagging (legacy-partner-soap), and modern handlers whose export/read paths carry no region or residency predicate (modern-orders-service, modern-claims-agent).
items.root_cause_pattern: Residency was enforced implicitly by the fact that data never left the data centre. Once an agent can call the service, there is no code-level boundary preventing cross-jurisdiction export.
items.remediation: Record the residency requirement per data store, pin agent-reachable stores and their replicas to the required Region, and add a residency predicate to every bulk-export and list operation.

remediation_detail.immediate_action: Record the residency requirement per data store, pin agent-reachable stores and their replicas to the required Region, and add a residency predicate to every bulk-export and list operation.

affected_services.resolution_reasoning: The jurisdiction of the customer data is undetermined and unconstrained, and there is no technical control preventing data read from the .mdb from being transmitted to an out-of-region processor (including an LLM endpoint).
affected_services.conditional_resolution: agent_scope is 'write-enabled' (inferred from has_write_operations=true) — evaluated as BLOCKER

affected_services.resolution_reasoning: Residency constraints on regulated consumer-lending PII are undocumented and unenforced, so there is nothing preventing an agent from forwarding that data to an LLM endpoint in another jurisdiction.
affected_services.conditional_resolution: Resolved to BLOCKER: agent_scope=write-enabled and the system holds regulated consumer-lending PII with no documented or enforced residency constraints.

affected_services.resolution_reasoning: Whether partner order data may leave the current jurisdiction - and therefore whether an agent may transmit it to an LLM endpoint in another region - is undetermined. There is no classification, no documented constraint, and no technical control preventing egress.

affected_services.resolution_reasoning: There is no declared or enforced boundary for where this regulated payroll data may travel, and no encryption in transit on the one hop that does cross a boundary. Nothing would prevent an agent from relaying the data to an out-of-jurisdiction endpoint.
affected_services.conditional_resolution: Resolved to BLOCKER: agent_scope=write-enabled, has_persistent_data_store=true, and no residency control or in-transit protection exists on the cross-boundary hop.

affected_services.resolution_reasoning: The jurisdiction of both the data store and the payment endpoint is undocumented, so there is no basis on which to decide whether order or card data may be sent to an LLM endpoint in another region. items.common_finding_summary: Eight write-enabled services provide no compensation path for an incorrect agent write. items.common_finding_summary: Nine services expose no programmatic contract an agent can call. The integration surface is a GUI form (legacy-crm-desktop, legacy-timesheet-webforms), a server-rendered page or CGI binary (legacy-document-portal, legacy-pricing-cgi), a JCL/batch job (legacy-payroll-system), an undocumented SOAP endpoint (legacy-partner-soap), or HTML-only Rails/Python controllers (legacy-storefront-rails, legacy-helpdesk-tickets, legacy-loan-calculator). No OpenAPI, GraphQL schema, gRPC proto or AsyncAPI document exists in any of them.
items.root_cause_pattern: These are pre-API-era applications whose only consumer was a human at a screen or a scheduled batch window. There was never a machine-facing contract to document, so agent integration would require UI automation, direct database access, or screen scraping — all brittle and unauditable.
items.remediation: Stand up a shared API facade layer (Amazon API Gateway + per-service adapter) and publish an OpenAPI 3 document per service, starting with the three services that already have a parseable request/response shape (legacy-partner-soap, legacy-pricing-cgi, legacy-document-portal).

remediation_detail.immediate_action: Stand up a shared API facade layer (Amazon API Gateway + per-service adapter) and publish an OpenAPI 3 document per service, starting with the three services that already have a parseable request/response shape (legacy-partner-soap, legacy-pricing-cgi, legacy-document-portal).

items.common_finding_summary: Eight write-enabled services accept repeated writes with no idempotency key and no dedupe window: INSERT-on-click (legacy-crm-desktop), re-runnable batch posting (legacy-payroll-system), non-idempotent SOAP operations (legacy-partner-soap), and modern handlers that accept a POST with no Idempotency-Key header (modern-orders-service, modern-claims-agent).
items.root_cause_pattern: Request de-duplication was delegated to a human who would not click twice. Machine-speed retry — the normal agent failure mode — therefore produces duplicate orders, duplicate settlements and duplicate payroll postings.
items.remediation: Define one portfolio-wide idempotency contract (client-supplied `Idempotency-Key` header, 24h dedupe window, stored request fingerprint) and implement it first on the money-moving paths: modern-orders-service, modern-claims-agent, legacy-payroll-system.

remediation_detail.immediate_action: Define one portfolio-wide idempotency contract (client-supplied `Idempotency-Key` header, 24h dedupe window, stored request fingerprint) and implement it first on the money-moving paths: modern-orders-service, modern-claims-agent, legacy-payroll-system.
remediation_detail.target_state: Every mutating operation is safe to retry; a replayed agent request returns the original result rather than creating a second side effect.
